12890.s: This order changes Executive Order 12864 to allow up to 30 members on the United States Advisory Council on the National Information Infrastructure. It affects the council by raising the member limit from 25 to 30.

12891.s: This order creates an Advisory Committee on Human Radiation Experiments and a chairperson chosen by the President. The committee is to advise the Human Radiation Interagency Working Group on ethical and scientific standards for human radiation experiments done or sponsored by the U.S. government. It also reviews certain named experiments and may recommend notice to subjects or their descendants if health risks or medical follow-up may be needed.

12892.s: This order directs federal departments and agencies to administer housing and urban development programs in a way that further fair housing. It gives the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development the main responsibility for leading and coordinating this work. It also creates the President's Fair Housing Council to review federal programs, propose changes, and help coordinate agency efforts. The order sets rules for sharing complaints, reviewing regulations, and taking enforcement action against people or agencies that do not comply.

12893.s: This order directs federal agencies with infrastructure duties to use set principles for federal spending on infrastructure programs. Those programs include transportation, water resources, energy, and environmental protection. Agencies must base investments on benefits and costs, manage facilities efficiently, seek private sector participation, and encourage state and local planning systems. Agencies must also submit plans to the Office of Management and Budget and use these principles in budget and legislative proposals.

12894.s: This executive order designates the North Pacific Marine Science Organization as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. That gives the organization the privileges, exemptions, and immunities allowed by that law. It applies to the organization and to any rights it may also have under international agreements or congressional action.

12895.s: This order designates the North Pacific Anadromous Fish Commission as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It gives the commission the privileges, exemptions, and immunities that the law provides. The order says this does not reduce any rights the commission may have from international agreements or congressional action.

12896.s: This order changes the civil service rules on political activity by revoking section 4.1 of Civil Service Rule IV. It affects the rules that apply to civil service employees.

12897.s: This order directs the Office of Personnel Management, working with the Attorney General, to write rules for carrying out federal wage garnishment rules for civilian employees and agencies in the executive branch. It also directs the Postmaster General to write rules for those same rules for employees of the United States Postal Service.

12898.s: This executive order directs federal agencies to make environmental justice part of their mission. It tells agencies to identify and address health and environmental effects of their programs on minority populations and low-income populations. It also creates an interagency working group, requires agency environmental justice strategies and reports, and calls for more research, data collection, and public participation.

12899.s: This order establishes a three-member board to investigate a dispute between The Long Island Rail Road and certain employees represented by the United Transportation Union. The board is to review final offers from the parties and report to the President with its selection of the most reasonable offer. From the time the board is requested until 60 days after its report, the parties must not change the conditions that led to the dispute except by agreement.

12900.s: This order creates a presidential advisory commission and a White House initiative in the Department of Education to focus on educational excellence for Hispanic Americans. It directs these groups to advise on Federal education efforts, collect information, and help prepare an annual Federal plan. It also asks agencies to appoint senior officials, share information, and prepare plans to increase Hispanic American participation in Federal education programs and improve outcomes.

12901.s: The order directs the United States Trade Representative to review trade expansion priorities and identify foreign country practices whose elimination is likely to increase U.S. exports. The Trade Representative must report those practices to Congress and publish the report in the Federal Register. The order also requires investigations into the identified practices and directs the Trade Representative to seek agreements to end them or, if that is not possible, to get compensatory trade benefits.

12902.s: This order directs federal agencies to cut energy use, save water, and increase the use of solar and other renewable energy sources in federal facilities. It sets goals for agencies and industrial facilities, and it requires surveys, audits, and plans to carry out cost-effective improvements. It also directs agencies to reduce petroleum use in buildings and to design new federal space and leases to lower life cycle energy and water costs where practicable.

12903.s: This order extends the period for peaceful nuclear cooperation with the European Atomic Energy Community until March 10, 1995. It says that ending this cooperation would be seriously harmful to U.S. non-proliferation goals and could affect the common defense and security of the United States. It also supersedes Executive Order 12840.

12904.s: This order designates four international organizations as public international organizations under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It applies to the Commission for Environmental Cooperation, the Commission for Labor Cooperation, the Border Environment Cooperation Commission, and the North American Development Bank. The order says this does not limit any privileges, exemptions, or immunities they may already have or later get under international agreements or congressional action.

12905.s: This order creates the Trade and Environment Policy Advisory Committee in the Office of the United States Trade Representative. The committee gives policy advice on trade and the environment and reports on whether trade agreements promote the interests of the United States. Its members are appointed by the Trade Representative and come from a mix of groups with an interest in trade and environmental policy.

12906.s: This order directs federal agencies to coordinate the development of a National Spatial Data Infrastructure for geospatial data. It sets up an electronic National Geospatial Data Clearinghouse, requires agencies to document and share geospatial data, and calls for standards so data from different agencies can work together. It also tells agencies to plan for public access to geospatial data where allowed by law. The order does not impose requirements on tribal governments and exempts certain national security, defense, and intelligence activities.

12907.s: This order changes Executive Order 12882 to add three members to the President's Committee of Advisors on Science and Technology. It also changes the committee size numbers in that order from 16 to 19 and from 15 to 18.

12908.s: This order sets who will act as Secretary of the Army if the office is vacant because of death, permanent disability, or resignation. It names the Under Secretary of the Army first, then the Assistant Secretaries and General Counsel in order of service, and then the Chief of Staff of the Army. It also says these duties are temporary and do not change the person’s regular appointment.

12909.s: This order sets who will act as Secretary of the Air Force if the office is vacant, or if the Secretary is absent or temporarily disabled. The Under Secretary goes first, then the Assistant Secretaries and General Counsel in order of service, and then the Chief of Staff. It also says this acting role is temporary and does not remove the person's regular job.

12910.s: The order closes all executive departments, independent establishments, and other government agencies, including field services, on April 27, 1994. It says that day is to be treated under rules about federal employee pay and leave. Some offices in the Department of State, the Department of Defense, and other agencies may stay open if their heads decide they should for national security, defense, or other public reasons.

12911.s: This order approves an official seal for the Office of National Drug Control Policy in the Executive Office of the President. It sets out the seal’s design and says the seal must be the attached design.

12912.s: This order changes Executive Order 12878 to extend the reporting period for the Bipartisan Commission on Entitlement Reform. It changes the deadline from May 1, 1994, to December 15, 1994.

12913.s: This order revokes Executive Order 12582 and treats it as void, effective February 2, 1987. It says this revocation is not meant to change the status of anyone who was naturalized under that order before this order was published in the Federal Register.

12914.s: This order blocks funds and financial resources of certain Haitian military officers, their immediate families, major participants in the 1991 coup and later illegal governments, and people working for or on behalf of the Haitian military. It also bars most aircraft travel connected to Haiti and stops U.S. persons from making transactions that evade these rules. Regularly scheduled commercial passenger flights are excepted.

12916.s: This order implements an agreement between the United States and Mexico to set up a Border Environment Cooperation Commission and a North American Development Bank. It says the agreement should be carried out in a way that protects human, animal, and plant life and the environment, and supports sustainable development, pollution prevention, environmental justice, ecosystem protection, and biodiversity preservation. It assigns United States representatives to the two boards and creates a Finance Committee to help handle community adjustment and investment programs.

12917.s: This order prohibits most imports into the United States of goods and services from Haiti that are exported after May 21, 1994, with an exception for informational materials. It also bars most sales, supplies, exports, and other transactions with Haiti by United States persons or from the United States, but allows some informational materials, medicines and medical supplies, and certain food items if the de facto regime in Haiti or a blocked person is not part of the deal.

12918.s: This order prohibits the sale or supply of arms and related materiel to Rwanda from the United States, by U.S. persons abroad, or using U.S.-registered vessels or aircraft. It also bars willful attempts to evade these restrictions. The Secretary of State and the Secretary of Commerce are given authority to carry out the order and to help implement other United Nations Security Council arms embargoes.

12919.s: This order delegates Defense Production Act powers to several federal officials to help prepare for national defense needs. It sets up rules for priorities, allocations, loans, guarantees, purchase commitments, and subsidy payments for materials, services, facilities, and critical technology. It also directs agencies to assess industrial capacity, coordinate preparedness programs, and support the domestic industrial and technology base.

12920.s: This order prohibits most payments, transfers, sales, and exports between the United States and Haiti. It allows some exceptions for government and international organization activities, humanitarian aid, travel expenses, and certain food, medicine, and medical supplies. It also bars U.S. persons from trying to evade these restrictions.

12921.s: This order changes a prior executive order to allow up to 37 members on the United States Advisory Council on the National Information Infrastructure. It affects the size of that council by replacing the number 30 with 37.

12922.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of Haitian nationals who live in Haiti, and of certain other people covered by earlier blocking orders and their immediate family members. It applies to property in the United States or under the control of United States persons. It does not apply to property of nongovernmental organizations providing essential humanitarian assistance in Haiti or carrying out refugee and migration operations in Haiti.

12923.s: This order continues export control rules under the Export Administration Act of 1979 and keeps those rules in force unless the Secretary of Commerce changes them. It also keeps related orders, regulations, licenses, and other administrative actions in effect, including sanctions under the regulations. The order applies to exports and to cooperation by U.S. persons with certain foreign boycott activities, and it declares a national emergency about the threat described in the order.

12924.s: This order declares a national emergency and keeps export control rules in effect. It says the Export Administration Act rules, regulations, licenses, and other actions will continue under this order unless changed or revoked by the Secretary of Commerce. It also lets rules for section 38(e) of the Arms Export Control Act stay in effect, and it revokes Executive Order 12923.

12925.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Soo Line Railroad Company and certain employees represented by the United Transportation Union. The board is to report to the President within 30 days after it is created. During that time, and for 30 days after the report is submitted, the parties may not change the conditions that led to the dispute unless they agree to do so.

12926.s: This order directs federal departments, agencies, and other executive branch entities to help states carry out the National Voter Registration Act of 1993. It tells some agencies to give guidance, help with implementation costs when allowed, and provide technical assistance for voter registration forms. It also directs the Secretary of Defense to work with state elections authorities on voter registration at Armed Forces recruitment offices, and it asks eligible federal offices to accept voter registration agency designations and keep required forms available to the public.

12927.s: This order says it is necessary to add to the active armed forces for missions to restore the civilian government in Haiti. It authorizes the Secretary of Defense, and the Secretary of Transportation for the Coast Guard in some cases, to order Selected Reserve units and some individual members to active duty. It is effective immediately.

12928.s: This executive order directs federal departments, agencies, and employees involved in procurement to help small businesses owned by socially and economically disadvantaged individuals, historically Black colleges and universities, and minority institutions take part in federal contracting. It says agencies must work to meet required participation goals, enforce subcontracting obligations, and make sure federal benefits and contracts go to legitimate eligible entities. It also calls for periodic reports to the President on progress.

12929.s: This order gives the Secretary of Energy the President’s authority under two sections of title 10 of the United States Code. It applies to the Naval Petroleum and Oil Shale Reserves.

12930.s: This order declares a national emergency over the spread of nuclear, biological, and chemical weapons and the means to deliver them. It directs the Secretary of Commerce, with the Secretary of State, to keep regulating United States persons to help prevent their participation in activities that could contribute to weapons proliferation. It also keeps certain prior rules in effect unless the Secretary of Commerce changes them, and it revokes Executive Order 12868.

12931.s: This order directs executive agencies that buy supplies and services to review their procurement rules and procedures and simplify them where possible. It also tells agencies to focus on measurable results, customer needs, best value, and more use of commercially available items and purchase cards. It requires agencies to strengthen training, accountability, and leadership for procurement work, and it revokes Executive Order 12352.

12932.s: This order ends the national emergency with respect to Haiti. It also revokes several earlier executive orders tied to that emergency. It says the end of the emergency does not affect actions, proceedings, rights, duties, or penalties that already existed before the order took effect.

12933.s: This order requires certain federal building service contracts to give qualified employees from the old contractor a right of first refusal for jobs under the new contract. It does not apply to some contracts and services listed in the order, including contracts under the simplified acquisition threshold and certain sheltered workshop and vending facility agreements. The Secretary of Labor is responsible for enforcing the order and may impose sanctions and remedies for noncompliance.

12934.s: This order blocks property and property interests of Bosnian Serb military and paramilitary forces, the authorities in areas they control, and certain related entities and people. It also prohibits United States persons from providing or exporting services to those areas or for business there, and bars certain U.S.-registered or U.S.-owned vessels from entering their riverine ports. It forbids transactions meant to evade these restrictions. It does not apply to activities related to the United Nations Protection Force, the International Conference on the Former Yugoslavia, or the European Community Monitoring Missions.

12935.s: This order changes the definition of "field duty" in Executive Order 11157. It removes language about a member being under orders with troops operating against an enemy, actual or potential, and removes related service wording from another section. The changes apply to members covered by that executive order.

12936.s: This order amends the Manual for Courts-Martial, United States, 1984. It affects the rules used for courts-martial in the military.

12937.s: This order declassifies selected records in the National Archives listed with the order. The Archivist must make them available for public research within 30 days, unless specific information is protected under an authorized Freedom of Information Act exemption other than national security information. It applies to the listed record groups, including World War II and earlier records and post-1945 military and civil records.

12938.s: This order declares a national emergency over the spread of nuclear, biological, and chemical weapons and the means to deliver them. It directs the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Commerce, and the Secretary of the Treasury to use export controls and sanctions to help stop that spread. It also bars certain U.S. government procurement and can restrict imports and exports involving foreign persons and foreign countries tied to these weapons.

12939.s: This order directs expedited naturalization for aliens and noncitizen nationals who served in an active-duty status in the Armed Forces during the Persian Gulf Conflict. It says those who served honorably during that period are eligible for naturalization under the stated exception to the usual requirements.

12940.s: This order changes Civil Service Rule VI for certain positions in the Department of Agriculture. It says the jobs of State Executive Directors of the Consolidated Farm Service Agency and State Directors or State Directors-at-Large for Rural Economic and Community Development must be listed in Schedule C for all General Schedule grades. These positions are excluded from the competitive service and from coverage of section 2302 of title 5.

12941.s: This order adopts minimum seismic safety standards for federally owned or leased buildings. Federal agencies must inventory those buildings, estimate the cost of fixing unacceptable seismic risks, and submit the cost estimates to FEMA. FEMA must notify agencies and report to Congress, and the National Institute of Standards and Technology must provide technical assistance.

12942.s: This order adds the Commissioner, Administration for Native Americans, to Level V of the Executive Schedule. It changes the list of positions covered by Executive Order 12154. The change affects that federal office.

12943.s: This order changes a prior executive order about how the Federal Government buys small cost items. It replaces one legal reference with another and says the order does not apply to purchases made under the micropurchase authority in section 32 of the Office of Federal Procurement Policy Act, as amended. It affects federal purchasing and the Bureau of Prisons reference in the earlier order.

12944.s: This order sets new pay and allowance rates for several federal pay systems. It covers General Schedule employees, Foreign Service employees, Veterans Health Administration employees, senior executives, executive branch officials, Congress, judges, and members of the uniformed services. It also provides interim geographic adjustments for covered employees and United States Park Police in listed areas. The new rates take effect on January 1, 1995, or at the start of the first applicable pay period after that date.

12945.s: This order amends a previous executive order about the President’s Committee on Employment of People with Disabilities. It changes the number of Vice Chairs from four to six and updates the wording in that order to use “Vice Chair” or “Vice Chairs.” It is issued to help carry out the Rehabilitation Act of 1973.

12946.s: This order creates a five-member advisory board in the Department of Defense. The board advises the President on U.S. conventional arms transfer policy and other arms proliferation policy matters. Its members serve without pay, may get travel expenses, and the board ends 30 days after the President sends its final report to Congress.

12947.s: This executive order blocks property and property interests in the United States of certain foreign persons and others listed in the order or later designated for violence tied to disrupting the Middle East peace process. It also prohibits transactions by United States persons or within the United States with those persons, including contributions of funds, goods, or services. The order directs federal agencies to help carry it out and requires possible violations to be coordinated with the FBI.

12948.s: This order changes section 1-103(e) of Executive Order 12898. It replaces the phrase "Within 12 months of the date of this order" with "By March 24, 1995,". It also changes the second sentence of that section to say "From the date of this order through March 24, 1995."

12949.s: This order lets the Attorney General approve physical searches for foreign intelligence information without a court order for up to one year, if the required certifications are made. It also lets the Attorney General approve applications to the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court for orders for physical searches. The order names certain national security and defense officials who may make the required certifications, but only if they were appointed by the President with Senate advice and consent.

12950.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between Metro North Commuter Railroad and employees represented by certain labor organizations. The board must report to the President within 30 days of its creation. For 120 days after the board is created, the carrier and the employees may not change the conditions that led to the dispute unless both sides agree.

12951.s: This order requires imagery from the Corona, Argon, and Lanyard missions to be declassified and sent to the National Archives and Records Administration, with a copy to the U.S. Geological Survey. It also sets up a review process for other space-based intelligence imagery to decide what can be released to the public while protecting national defense and foreign policy. The order says it is the only Executive order governing the public release of this kind of imagery.

12952.s: This order amends Executive Order 12950. It adds the International Brotherhood of Firemen & Oilers to the list of labor organizations attached to that order.

12953.s: This executive order directs federal agencies to help establish and enforce child support orders. It requires agencies to cooperate on paternity and support cases, process wage withholding, share information to help locate noncustodial parents and their employers, and inform employees about child support services. It also calls for reviews and reports on ways to improve child support enforcement for federal employees and members of the Uniformed Services.

12954.s: This order says federal agencies should not contract with employers that permanently replace lawfully striking employees. The Secretary of Labor may investigate complaints, hold hearings, and find that a contract should be ended for convenience or that a contractor should be debarred from getting government contracts. It applies to certain federal contracts and includes only situations where the replacements happened after the order took effect.

12955.s: This order extends the period for peaceful nuclear cooperation with the European Atomic Energy Community until December 31, 1995. It says ending that cooperation would be seriously harmful to U.S. nonproliferation goals and could put U.S. defense and security at risk.

12956.s: This order designates the Israel-United States Binational Industrial Research and Development Foundation as a public international organization. It says the foundation is entitled to the privileges, exemptions, and immunities given under the International Organizations Immunities Act, without changing any rights it may already have under other agreements or congressional action.

12957.s: This order declares a national emergency about actions and policies of the Government of Iran. It prohibits U.S. persons from entering into or approving certain contracts or guarantees for the development or financing of petroleum resources in Iran. It also bars transactions that evade or try to violate these bans, and directs federal agencies to help carry them out.

12958.s: This order sets rules for classifying, safeguarding, and declassifying national security information. It says only certain government officials may classify information, and only when disclosure could harm national security and the information fits listed categories such as military plans, foreign government information, or intelligence activities. It also sets three classification levels: Top Secret, Secret, and Confidential. The order requires declassification instructions and says information should usually be marked for declassification after 10 years unless an exemption applies.

12959.s: This order prohibits many transactions with Iran and with the Government of Iran. It bars importing Iranian goods or services, exporting goods, technology, or services to Iran, reexporting certain U.S.-origin goods or technology to Iran, and new investment in Iran or in property owned or controlled by the Government of Iran. It also restricts certain dealings by U.S. persons, and it directs federal agencies to help carry out the order.

12960.s: This order amends the Manual for Courts-Martial, which is used in military justice cases. It changes rules on rehearings, sentence review, reconsideration of findings and sentences, clemency recommendations, and when a convening authority may suspend or modify a sentence. It also adds and removes some rules in the Military Rules of Evidence and changes how certain court-martial records and actions are handled.

12961.s: This order creates the Presidential Advisory Committee on Gulf War Veterans' Illnesses. The committee is to advise the President on research, medical treatment, outreach, risk factors, and reports about possible chemical or biological weapons related to Gulf War veterans' illnesses. It must also review the work of certain boards and outside reviews, but it is not to conduct scientific research or give advice on federal legal liability.

12962.s: This order tells federal agencies to improve aquatic resources to increase recreational fishing opportunities. It directs them to work with states and Tribes, support conservation and restoration, improve access and public participation, and help private landowners conserve aquatic resources on their lands. It also creates a National Recreational Fisheries Coordination Council to coordinate federal work and develop a conservation plan for recreational fisheries.

12963.s: This order directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish the Presidential Advisory Council on HIV/AIDS. The council may have up to 30 members and is to advise the Secretary on preventing HIV disease, advancing HIV and AIDS research, and improving services for people living with HIV disease and AIDS. Its work is advisory only, and the Secretary must share its written reports with the President.

12965.s: This order extends the President's Council on Sustainable Development. It changes the council’s end date to June 29, 1997, unless it is extended again.

12966.s: This order directs the Secretary of Defense to provide disaster assistance outside the United States when it is needed to help prevent loss of life from manmade or natural disasters. The assistance may be given only at the President's direction, with the Secretary of State's concurrence, or in emergency situations when there is not time to get prior concurrence. The Secretary of Defense must also consult with the Administrator of the Agency for International Development when providing this assistance.

12967.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate disputes between Metro North Commuter Railroad and certain employees represented by labor organizations. The board must be appointed by the President and must report its choice of the most reasonable settlement offer after the parties submit final offers. Until the board reports, the parties generally may not change the conditions that led to the disputes unless they agree to do so.

12968.s: This order sets a uniform federal personnel security program for employees who may be considered for access to classified information. It says employees may get access only if they are found eligible, have a need to know, and sign a nondisclosure agreement, and they can be investigated before and during access. It also requires some employees to file financial disclosure reports and lets agencies review certain financial, credit, and travel records under the conditions listed in the order.

12969.s: This order directs federal agencies, to the greatest extent practicable, to contract with companies that report publicly on toxic chemicals released to the environment. For certain competitive federal contracts expected to be $100,000 or more, covered contractors must file and keep filing Toxic Chemical Release Forms for toxic chemicals they manufacture, process, or otherwise use at covered facilities. It also sets reporting, certification, trade secret review, and possible contract termination steps for contractors that do not comply.

12970.s: This order changes Executive Order 12864 to extend the United States Advisory Council on the National Information Infrastructure. It replaces the earlier time limit with a new extension that lasts until June 1, 1996, unless it is extended again.

12971.s: This order amends a previous executive order on the International Criminal Police Organization, or INTERPOL. It deletes certain wording from that order so the privileges, exemptions, and immunities for INTERPOL are extended. It affects INTERPOL and the parts of the earlier order that dealt with customs duties and federal internal-revenue importation taxes.

12972.s: This order amends Executive Order 12958. It changes the definition of “agency” to include executive agencies, military departments, and other executive branch entities that come into possession of classified information.

12973.s: This order changes Executive Order 12901 by replacing “1994” with “1996” and “1995” with “1997” in section 1. It says the change is meant to help U.S. trade policy support the export of U.S. products and services and use trade policy resources efficiently.

12974.s: This order continues a list of federal advisory committees until September 30, 1997. It also says the heads of the listed departments or agencies will carry out the President’s duties under the Federal Advisory Committee Act for those committees, except for annual reporting to Congress. The order revokes two earlier orders or parts of orders that created committees that had ended or finished their work.

12975.s: This order tells executive branch departments and agencies that conduct, support, or regulate research involving human subjects to review their current protections for those subjects. It also creates the National Bioethics Advisory Commission, which gives advice and recommendations on bioethical issues tied to research on human biology and behavior. The commission’s first priorities are protecting human research subjects and issues in the management and use of genetic information, including human gene patenting.

12976.s:
This order sets rules for compensation practices at certain government corporations. It says they should not pay bonuses above amounts allowed by law unless another law specifically allows it, and some bonus requests must be reviewed by the Office of Management and Budget before approval.
It also requires these corporations to provide information on senior executive pay, including salary, bonuses, and the company’s compensation plan. The information must be reviewed by OMB and made available to the public.

12977.s: This order creates the Interagency Security Committee in the executive branch. The committee is made up of officials and representatives from several federal agencies and is chaired by the Administrator of General Services or a designee. It sets policies and security standards for federal facilities, oversees security measures, and helps monitor agency compliance.

12978.s: This executive order blocks property and property interests in the United States, or under the control of United States persons, of certain foreign persons tied to narcotics trafficking centered in Colombia. It also bars United States persons and people in the United States from doing transactions involving that property or from trying to evade these rules. The order covers persons listed in an annex and others found to play a significant role in this trafficking or to help it.

12979.s: This order tells executive departments and agencies that buy supplies and services to set up administrative procedures for protests over federal contract awards. It says the procedures should be simple and fast, let some bidders or offerors ask for review above the contracting officer, and usually stop contract award or performance while a timely protest is pending. It also directs federal officials to give policy guidance, review agency experience, and amend the Federal Acquisition Regulation.

12980.s: This order changes the size of the President’s Council on Sustainable Development from 25 members to 29 members. It affects the council by adding four more members.

12981.s: This order sets procedures for reviewing export license applications under the Export Administration Act and related regulations. It keeps the Secretary of Commerce in charge of license review and lets the Departments of State, Defense, and Energy, and the Arms Control and Disarmament Agency review applications too. It also sets time limits for initial processing, agency recommendations, and appeals when agencies do not agree. It continues interagency groups to resolve disputes and consider national security and other policy issues.

12982.s: This order says it is necessary to add to the active armed forces for operations in and around former Yugoslavia. It authorizes the Secretary of Defense, and the Secretary of Transportation for the Coast Guard in some cases, to order Selected Reserve units and some individual members to active duty. It says the order is for internal management of the executive branch and does not create enforceable rights or benefits.

12983.s: This order amends a prior executive order on labor-management partnerships to improve the National Partnership Council. It adds one elected office holder each from the Senior Executives Association and the Federal Managers Association, and it requires a report to the President by October 1996 on progress and results of labor-management partnership throughout the executive branch. It also changes how the Council seeks input and says members serve without pay but may receive travel expenses allowed by law.

12984.s: This order sets new pay and allowance rates for several federal pay systems. It covers the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Health Administration schedules, senior executives, executive branch salaries that stay unchanged, uniformed services pay and allowances, and locality-based comparability payments. It also directs the Office of Personnel Management to help carry out the locality payments and publish notice of them.

12985.s: This order establishes the Armed Forces Service Medal and its ribbons and appurtenances for members of the Armed Forces who take part in certain United States military operations that are considered significant activity. It applies only when there is no foreign armed opposition or imminent hostile action, and only for operations that do not qualify for another United States service medal. The medal is awarded by the Secretary of Defense, and by the Secretary of Transportation for the Coast Guard when it is not operating as a service in the Navy. No more than one medal may be awarded to the same person, but it may be awarded after death.

12986.s: This order extends certain privileges and immunities to the International Union for Conservation of Nature and Natural Resources. It gives the group immunity from suit, and its property and assets are protected from search and confiscation. It also gives its representatives, officers, and employees immunity from suit and legal process for acts done in their official duties.

12987.s: This order amends a previous executive order about the Commission on United States-Pacific Trade and Investment Policy. It changes one section to allow up to 20 members instead of 15, and it changes another section to set a new date of about December 31, 1996 instead of before February 1, 1996. This affects the commission and its work.

12988.s: This order directs federal agencies to handle civil cases more efficiently and to try to settle disputes before filing or going to trial. It also tells agencies to review legislation and regulations to reduce ambiguity, minimize litigation, and set clear legal standards. Federal agencies should review their administrative adjudication processes to reduce delay, address bias, and improve public education about claims and benefits procedures.

12989.s: This order directs federal contracting agencies not to contract with employers that have not complied with certain Immigration and Nationality Act rules on the unlawful employment of aliens. It allows the Attorney General to investigate possible violations and send findings to contracting agencies. If a contractor is found not in compliance, the agency may debar that contractor or part of it from federal procurement and nonprocurement activities. It also says the order does not change employers’ duties under the antidiscrimination provisions of immigration law.

12990.s: This order adjusts the monthly basic pay, subsistence allowances, and quarters allowances for members of the uniformed services. It also adjusts the monthly pay for cadets and midshipmen. The changes are effective January 1, 1996, and it supersedes Section 4 and Schedule 8 of Executive Order 12984.

12991.s: This order adds the Small Business Administration to the President’s Export Council. It changes the list of members in the earlier executive order to include that agency.

12992.s: This order creates the President's Council on Counter-Narcotics. It includes the President, Vice President, and several cabinet and White House officials, and it may also include other officials the President designates. The Council advises and assists the President on the national drug control strategy and on coordination among departments and agencies. Executive departments and agencies must cooperate with the Council and provide help, information, and advice when requested, as allowed by law.

12993.s: This order creates an Integrity Committee to receive, review, and refer allegations of wrongdoing against Inspectors General and, in some cases, certain staff members of their offices. The committee can send matters to the agency with proper authority, or have the FBI chair arrange an investigation when no other agency can handle it. It also sets procedures for reporting the results, keeping records, and closing matters that do not need further action.

12994.s: This order keeps the President’s Committee on Mental Retardation in operation and gives it broader membership and responsibilities. The committee includes several federal officials and up to 21 other members appointed by the President, including self-advocates, family members, and people from the public or private sector. It advises the President and the Secretary of Health and Human Services on policies, services, and supports for people with mental retardation, and it must send an annual report to the President.

12995.s: This order changes rules in a prior executive order about recycled content in certain printing and writing papers. It raises the minimum postconsumer material standard for several kinds of paper to 30 percent starting December 31, 1998, and sets an alternative standard of 50 percent recovered materials for all printing and writing papers. It also changes a consulting requirement for the Federal Environmental Executive.

12996.s: This order says the National Wildlife Refuge System is meant to conserve fish, wildlife, and plant resources and their habitat for present and future generations. It directs the Secretary of the Interior to treat hunting, fishing, wildlife observation and photography, and environmental education as priority public uses when they are compatible with refuge management. It also calls for more public involvement, cooperation with other agencies, and continued uses needed to help with military preparedness where allowed by law.

12997.s: This order designates the Korean Peninsula Energy Development Organization as a public international organization. It makes the organization eligible for the privileges, exemptions, and immunities under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It also says this designation does not reduce any other privileges, exemptions, or immunities the organization may have under international agreements or congressional action.

12998.s: This order amends a previous executive order about who may act as Secretary of Commerce. It says the President may direct a specified officer to serve as Secretary of Commerce at any time, under law and without following the earlier rules in that order. It also renumbers the current section 2 as section 3.

12999.s: This order tells federal agencies to protect educationally useful federal computer equipment and, when possible, give it first to schools and nonprofit organizations. It also encourages agencies to help connect classrooms to the National Information Infrastructure, help teachers learn to use computers, and provide support for transferred equipment. Agencies are to share the availability of this equipment by practicable means, including newspapers, community announcements, and the Internet.

13000.s: This order sets a line of succession for who will act as Secretary of Defense if the Secretary dies, becomes permanently disabled, resigns, or is temporarily absent or disabled. It lists Department of Defense officers in order and says the acting role is temporary and does not change the person's regular appointment. It also revokes a prior executive order on the same subject.

13001.s: This order sets up a three-member emergency board to investigate a labor dispute between certain railroads and their employees represented by the Transportation Communications International Union. The board is to report to the President within 30 days. While the board is active and for 30 days after its report, the railroads and employees may not change the working conditions involved in the dispute unless both sides agree.

13002.s: This order sets June 30, 1996, at midnight as the date when combatant activities in the combat zone in Vietnam and nearby waters end. It affects the area described in Executive Order 11216.

13003.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate disputes between certain railroads and employees represented by the Brotherhood of Maintenance of Way Employes. The board must report to the President within 30 days. While the board is working and for 30 days after its report, the railroads and employees may not change the conditions involved in the disputes unless both sides agree.

13004.s: This order establishes a three-member emergency board to investigate disputes between certain railroads and their employees represented by listed labor organizations. The board must report to the President within 30 days. From the date the board is created until 30 days after its report, the railroads and employees may not change the conditions tied to the disputes unless they agree to do so.

13005.s: This order directs the Department of Commerce to develop policies and procedures for an empowerment contracting program in federal procurement. It tells agencies to give qualified large and small businesses in areas of general economic distress appropriate incentives when they compete for government contracts, if allowed by law. It also requires the Secretary of Commerce to monitor the program, reduce fraud, evaluate it, and report to the President each year.

13006.s: Federal agencies must give first consideration to properties in districts when locating Federal facilities, then other developed or undeveloped sites in districts, and then properties outside districts if no suitable site is found. The order also tells agencies to reduce rules and procedures that make it harder to place or keep Federal facilities in districts, unless those rules protect human health and safety or the environment.

13007.s: The order tells executive branch agencies that manage federal lands to accommodate access to and ceremonial use of Indian sacred sites when practical and allowed by law. It also says they should avoid harming the physical integrity of those sites and keep them confidential where appropriate. Agencies must set up procedures to carry out these steps and report on their actions.

13008.s: This order changes Executive Order 12880 by replacing "Department of State" with "Office of National Drug Control Policy" in section 1(c). It is meant to update who is named in that section for managing U.S. international narcotics control policies.

13009.s: This order changes the size of the Presidential Advisory Council on HIV/AIDS by increasing its membership from 30 to 35. It affects the council by changing the number of people who may serve on it.

13010.s: This order creates the President’s Commission on Critical Infrastructure Protection to study how to protect key systems like telecommunications, power, banking, transportation, water, emergency services, and government continuity. It tells the Commission to work with public and private groups, assess vulnerabilities and threats, and recommend a national policy and strategy for protection. It also creates a temporary Infrastructure Protection Task Force in the Department of Justice to coordinate existing efforts, share threat information, and help respond to attacks.

13011.s: This executive order directs executive agencies to improve how they manage information systems and buy information technology. It requires agencies to create Chief Information Officers, use performance measures, strengthen information security, and review major technology investments. It also sets up government councils and boards to share practices, advise agencies, and help coordinate information technology across the federal government.

13012.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority and employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers. The board must report to the President within 30 days of its creation. For 120 days after the board is created, the carrier and the employees cannot change the conditions that led to the dispute unless they agree to do so.

13013.s: This order changes the rules for the Armed Forces Reserve Medal. It says the medal may be awarded to members or former members of the reserve components of the Armed Forces who meet certain service or active duty conditions. It also says no one may receive more than one medal, and the medal is given with the design and appurtenance that match how it was earned.

13014.s: This order directs the government to maintain unofficial commercial, cultural, and other relations with the people on Taiwan without official diplomatic relations. It gives the Secretary of State and the Director of the Office of Personnel Management certain functions under the Taiwan Relations Act, and it lets the Taipei Economic and Cultural Representative Office act for Taiwan in certain matters. It also allows the Institute to use certain contracting rules and keeps earlier agreements in force unless they are changed or ended under the law.

13015.s: This order creates the White House Commission on Aviation Safety and Security. The Commission is to advise the President on aviation safety and security, including air traffic control, and to develop a strategy to improve aviation safety and security in the United States and abroad. It may use experts, hold hearings, and form committees and teams, and it is supported by the Department of Transportation and other lawful sources.

13016.s: This order amends an earlier executive order by giving certain duties under the environmental law to the Secretaries of the Interior, Commerce, Agriculture, Defense, and Energy. Those duties apply to certain releases or threatened releases in the coastal zone, Great Lakes waters, ports, and harbors that affect natural resources under their care or a vessel or facility under their control. The authority must be used only with the Coast Guard or the Administrator’s agreement, and it cannot be used at a vessel or facility where the Coast Guard or the Administrator is the lead federal official for a response action.

13017.s: This order creates the Advisory Commission on Consumer Protection and Quality in the Health Care Industry. The Commission is made up of up to 20 members and is to include consumers, health care providers, insurers, purchasers, government representatives, and experts in health care quality, financing, and administration. It advises the President on changes in the health care system and recommends measures to promote health care quality and value and protect consumers and workers in the health care system.

13018.s: This order changes Executive Order 12975 to increase the National Bioethics Advisory Commission from 15 members to 18 members. It affects the commission by adding 3 members.

13019.s: This order directs federal agencies to help collect past-due child support by using administrative offsets and sharing payment records where allowed by law. It also tells agencies to review certain federal payments and may let them deny some federal financial assistance to people with delinquent child support obligations. The order includes reporting duties for the Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of Health and Human Services, and other agencies.

13020.s: This order changes how license applications are reviewed for commercial communication satellites and for certain hot-section technologies used in commercial aircraft engines. It says the Chair of the OC must follow a majority vote decision for those applications, and it sets deadlines for appeals to the ACEP and, in some cases, to the Secretary. The order takes effect right away and does not create any right to judicial or administrative review.

13021.s: This order sets up a federal board and a White House initiative focused on tribal colleges and universities. It tells federal agencies to work with tribal colleges, make five-year plans, and report on progress and funding goals. It also says the effort should help improve access to federal resources, support education for economically disadvantaged Indian students, and preserve American Indian and Alaska Native languages and cultural traditions.

13022.s: This order transfers control of the Midway Islands and their territorial seas from the Department of the Navy to the Department of the Interior. It dissolves the Midway Islands Naval Defensive Sea Area and the Midway Islands Naval Airspace Reservation. The Department of the Interior, through the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, will administer the islands as a national wildlife refuge, and it will handle civil administration and later legal matters under this order.

13023.s: This order renames the "President's Council on Counter-Narcotics" as the "President's Drug Policy Council." It also makes the Secretaries of the Interior, Agriculture, Health and Human Services, Housing and Urban Development, Education, and Veterans Affairs permanent members, along with the Assistant to the President for Domestic Policy. The order also updates the council's membership list to include several other federal officials and any other officials the President may designate.

13024.s: This order amends a prior executive order about competitive appointments for students who have completed approved career-related work study programs. It changes one part to include “term” appointments along with career and career-conditional appointments. It also says students converted to a term appointment may later be converted noncompetitively to a career or career-conditional appointment before the term appointment expires.

13025.s: This order changes how the President's Commission on Critical Infrastructure Protection is organized. It says the Chair must be a qualified person from outside the Federal Government, and it changes the Steering Committee to five members, with four appointed by the President and one being the Chair. It also changes the commission's member limit from ten to 15.

13026.s: This order sets rules for export controls on encryption products if they are placed on the Commerce Control List. It says the government may control the export of these products, including related assistance and training to foreign persons. It also changes the export review process so several departments can review license applications for these products.

13027.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority and employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers. The parties must submit final offers for settlement within 30 days after the board is created, and the board must then report to the President with its choice of the most reasonable offer. From the time the board is requested until 60 days after its report, the parties may not change the conditions that led to the dispute unless they agree to do so.

13028.s: This order amends an earlier executive order on the Enterprise for the Americas Initiative. It updates legal references and adds a new section about future laws that are the same or substantially the same as section 571 of Public Law 104-107. It also delegates some functions under that law to the Secretary, to be carried out with recommendations of the Council and in consultation with the Secretary of State.

13029.s: This order implements part of an agreement on legal capacity and privileges and immunities for the United States. It extends the privileges and immunities in the annex to the personnel and institutions described in it. It also says the Conference on Security and Cooperation in Europe will henceforth be called the Organization for Security and Cooperation in Europe.

13030.s: This order changes several earlier executive orders about foreign assistance and arms export controls. It delegates certain authority to the Secretary of State and adds or updates sections tied to specific laws and provisions. The changes affect the Secretary of State’s role in handling those foreign assistance and arms export control functions.

13031.s: This order directs federal agencies to lead in using alternative fueled vehicles and to make plans to meet the acquisition requirements in the law. Agencies must report on their compliance, explain any failures, and describe how they will meet the requirements. It also allows certain law-enforcement, emergency, and national defense vehicles to be exempt, and it sets rules for credits, funding help for electric vehicles, and coordination with fuel suppliers and other stakeholders.

13032.s: This order changes Executive Order 12964 by replacing the date “December 31, 1996” with “February 28, 1997.” It is meant to help the work of the Commission on United States-Pacific Trade and Investment Policy.

13033.s: This order sets adjusted pay rates and allowances for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Health Administration, Senior Executive Service, the Executive Schedule, the Vice President, Congress, and justices and judges. It also sets pay and allowances for members of the uniformed services and cadet or midshipman pay. In addition, it provides locality-based comparability payments and supersedes two earlier executive orders.

13034.s: This order extends the Presidential Advisory Committee on Gulf War Veterans' Illnesses. The committee must keep advising the President and reviewing the Defense Department investigation into possible chemical or biological warfare agent exposures during the Gulf War. It must also review progress on carrying out its earlier recommendations and submit a status report and a final supplemental report.

13035.s: This order creates an advisory committee on high-performance computing, information technology, and the Next Generation Internet. The committee has up to 25 nonfederal members from research, education, library, network provider, and critical industry groups. It gives advice and information to the National Science and Technology Council and reviews progress on the HPCC Program and the Next Generation Internet initiative. The Department of Defense provides support, and the committee ends after 2 years unless the President extends it.

13036.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between American Airlines and employees represented by the Allied Pilots Association. The board must report to the President within 30 days. During that time, and for 30 days after the report is submitted, the parties may not change the conditions that led to the dispute unless they agree to do so.

13037.s: This order creates a bipartisan Commission to Study Capital Budgeting with 11 members appointed by the President. The commission will study capital budgeting practices, the definition of capital for federal budgeting, depreciation, and the effects of a federal capital budget on budget choices. It will report to the National Economic Council, and the Department of the Treasury will provide funding and administrative support.

13038.s: This order creates an advisory committee on the public interest obligations of digital television broadcasters. The committee can have up to 15 members from private industry, academic institutions, public interest organizations, and the advertising community, and the President appoints the members and chooses the chair. The committee must report to the Vice President on what public interest obligations digital television broadcasters should assume. The Department of Commerce may provide staff, services, and other support for the committee.

13039.s: This order excludes the Naval Special Warfare Development Group from the Federal Labor-Management Relations Program. It says the group has a primary function in intelligence, counter-intelligence, investigative, or national security work. It changes an earlier executive order to add that group to the list of excluded organizations.

13040.s: This order changes the Advisory Commission on Consumer Protection and Quality in the Health Care Industry. It expands the commission from 20 members to 32 members. It also sets new deadlines for the commission to send a preliminary report and a final report to the President.

13041.s: This order adds two White House officials to the Principals Committee of the President's Commission on Critical Infrastructure Protection. It also extends the life of that Commission for 90 more days. The change affects the Commission and its committee membership.

13042.s: This order implements part of the World Trade Organization agreement for the United States. It applies certain privileges and immunities to the World Trade Organization, its officials, and representatives of its members, with limits on taxation, immigration, and national service obligations for U.S. nationals and permanent residents. It also designates the World Trade Organization as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act, with limits on property tax relief for property not used for World Trade Organization purposes.

13043.s: This executive order requires Federal employees to wear seat belts while on official business when their seat has one. It also requires seat belts or child restraint systems to be used in national park areas and on Defense installations, and it directs agencies to promote seat belt policies for contractors, grantees, and Tribal Governments. The Secretary of Transportation must help with these programs and submit an annual report on seat belt use rates, crashes, injuries, and related costs.

13044.s: This order changes a prior order that helps carry out the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act of 1954. It adds “private entities” to one part that had referred only to developing countries. It also deletes two sections and renumbers the remaining sections of that order.

13045.s: This order tells federal agencies to make child health and safety risks a high priority when they deal with environmental and safety issues. It also creates a task force to recommend federal strategies, review research and data, and report on children’s environmental health and safety. The order directs agencies to evaluate how covered regulations may affect children and to improve information shared about children and families.

13046.s: This order extends the term of the National Bioethics Advisory Commission. It changes the commission’s end date to October 3, 1999, unless the President extends it before then.

13047.s: This order prohibits new investment in Burma by United States persons, with limited exceptions allowed by regulations, orders, directives, or licenses. It also bars United States persons from helping a foreign person make a transaction that would count as new investment in Burma, or from trying to evade these rules. The order applies to contracts and investments tied to the economic development of resources located in Burma, but it says not-for-profit educational, health, or other humanitarian programs are not included.

13048.s: This executive order creates an Interagency Council on Administrative Management to improve agency administrative and management practices across the executive branch. The council includes representatives from several federal departments and agencies and helps plan, promote, and recommend improvements in government administration and operations. It also revokes three earlier executive orders related to management improvement and productivity programs.

13049.s: This order designates the Organization for the Prohibition of Chemical Weapons as a public international organization under U.S. law. It gives the organization the privileges, exemptions, and immunities available under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It also says this does not limit any privileges or immunities the organization may have under international agreements or congressional action.

13050.s: This order creates a President’s Advisory Board on Race made up of 7 members from outside the Federal Government. The board will advise the President on race and racial reconciliation, including ways to promote dialogue, increase understanding of race relations, bridge racial divides, and address problems in education, economic opportunity, housing, health care, and the administration of justice. It also may advise on other matters the President refers to it.

13051.s: This order creates the Internal Revenue Service Management Board within the Department of the Treasury. The board is meant to help the Secretary of the Treasury oversee the management and operation of the IRS, including modernization, major budget issues, and customer service. It must meet at least monthly and send semiannual reports to the President and Congress.

13052.s: This order extends certain privileges, exemptions, and immunities to the Hong Kong Economic and Trade Offices. It covers protections under the International Organizations Immunities Act and part of an agreement on state and local taxation of foreign employees of public international organizations. It also says it does not reduce any privileges, exemptions, or immunities they already have or may get later by international agreement or congressional action.

13053.s: This order changes the President’s Council on Sustainable Development by increasing its membership from 29 to 35. It also replaces the Department of the Interior with the Department of Energy in two sections and extends the council’s date to February 28, 1999.

13054.s: This order lets certain U.S. citizens who are family members of Federal civilian employees get noncompetitive appointments to competitive service jobs in the executive branch when they return to the United States. It applies to family members who left Federal service to work for the American Institute in Taiwan and who meet qualifications set by the Office of Personnel Management. The Director of the Office of Personnel Management must write any needed rules to carry it out.

13055.s: This order creates a senior-level interagency working group inside the United States Information Agency. The group is meant to improve coordination, efficiency, and effectiveness of United States Government-sponsored international exchanges and training programs. It must collect and analyze data, set up a clearinghouse, identify overlap in programs, and develop a coordinated strategy and performance measures. It also involves several federal departments and agencies that run or help run these programs.

13056.s: This order changes the Advisory Commission on Consumer Protection and Quality in the Health Care Industry by increasing its membership from 32 to 34. It affects the commission by adding two more members.

13057.s: This order directs federal agencies with authority in the Lake Tahoe Region to form a partnership. The partnership is meant to coordinate federal work and share resources and data, and it must work with California, Nevada, the Washoe Tribal Government, the Tahoe Regional Planning Agency, and interested local governments. It also calls for a memorandum of agreement to document shared interests and ways to cooperate.

13058.s: This order makes the executive branch set up a smoke-free environment for Federal employees and members of the public in Federal facilities. It prohibits smoking tobacco products in all interior space owned, rented, or leased by the executive branch, and in outdoor areas under executive branch control in front of air intake ducts. It also lets agencies make limited exceptions, review smoking near doorways and courtyards, and create programs to help employees stop smoking.

13059.s: This order prohibits importing goods or services of Iranian origin, or owned or controlled by the Government of Iran, except for information and informational materials. It also bars United States persons from exporting or reexporting goods, technology, or services to Iran, making new investment in Iran, and taking part in other transactions or dealings tied to Iranian goods, services, or property. The order also restricts approvals, financing, facilitation, and guarantees for transactions by foreign persons that would be prohibited if done by a United States person.

13060.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate disputes between Amtrak and its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Maintenance of Way Employes. The board must report to the President within 30 days. During that time, and for 30 days after the report is submitted, the parties may not change the conditions behind the dispute unless both sides agree.

13061.s: This order creates the American Heritage Rivers initiative to help protect and restore rivers and the communities along them. It tells federal agencies to coordinate their programs and resources, work with state, local, and tribal governments, and support community-based efforts without creating new regulatory authority. Communities can nominate rivers for designation, and designated rivers may get a River Navigator and other federal support.

13062.s: This order keeps 15 federal advisory committees in place until September 30, 1999. It also says that, for those committees, the department or agency head will carry out the President’s duties under the Federal Advisory Committee Act, except for the annual report to Congress. The order revokes several earlier orders that set up committees whose work is completed, and it amends two other executive orders.

13063.s: This executive order removes the Executive Director of the Pension Benefit Guaranty Corporation, Department of Labor, from Level V of the Executive Schedule. It also changes the numbering of the remaining subsections in the earlier executive order.

13064.s: This order amends a prior executive order on critical infrastructure protection. It changes the membership and wording of one section, makes the Principals Committee, Steering Committee, and Advisory Committee end no later than March 15, 1998, and has them review the Commission's report and prepare recommendations to the President. It also lets some Commission staff be kept to help with that review and gives the Executive Secretary of the National Security Council authority to classify certain information as "Top Secret."

13065.s: This order changes the Advisory Committee on Public Interest Obligations of Digital Television Broadcasters. It raises the maximum number of committee members from not more than 22 to up to 25 and allows the committee to have co-chairs.

13066.s: This order changes Executive Order 13037 on the Commission To Study Capital Budgeting. It raises the commission’s membership limit from 11 to no more than 20. It also deletes the words "by March 15, 1998, or" from section 3 of that order.

13067.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of the Government of Sudan that are in the United States or come under the control of United States persons. It also prohibits many transactions with Sudan, including importing Sudanese goods or services, exporting goods or services to Sudan, helping those exports, making certain contracts there, giving credits or loans to the Government of Sudan, and some cargo transportation transactions. It allows transactions for official Federal Government or United Nations business and for journalistic activity in Sudan.

13068.s: This executive order closes all executive departments and agencies on Friday, December 26, 1997, and excuses their employees from duty that day. Agency heads may keep some offices open and require certain employees to work for reasons of national security, defense, or other public reasons. It also says that day counts under federal pay and leave rules for United States employees.

13069.s: This order closes all UNITA offices in the United States. It also bans certain transactions involving aircraft, aircraft parts, and aircraft services for UNITA and for travel to parts of Angola not approved under the order. It applies to United States persons and to people in the United States, and it allows the Treasury Secretary to set some exceptions and rules.

13070.s: This order changes the rules for the Intelligence Oversight Board. It makes the board a standing committee of the PFIAB, with up to four members chosen by the President from the PFIAB membership. It also says the board reports to the President and may use staff and consultants approved by its chairman and the PFIAB chairman.

13071.s: This order sets new basic pay rates and salaries for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Health Administration, Senior Executive Service, Executive Schedule, the Vice President, Congress, justices and judges, and the uniformed services. It also provides for locality-based comparability payments and tells the Office of Personnel Management to take the steps needed to carry them out. Most of the listed pay changes take effect with the first applicable pay period on or after January 1, 1998.

13072.s: This order forms the White House Millennium Council. The council includes representatives from several executive branch departments and agencies. Its job is to lead the country in celebrating the new millennium by starting and recognizing national and local projects, planning events, and producing materials to educate people about America’s past and future.

13073.s: This executive order directs federal agencies to make sure critical federal programs do not get disrupted by the Year 2000 computer problem. It also tells agencies to work with state, local, and tribal governments, private sector operators of critical systems, and foreign counterparts on the issue. It creates the President's Council on Year 2000 Conversion to coordinate these efforts and report on progress.

13074.s: This order amends another executive order to assign responsibility for the use of military forces to protect United States citizens and nationals overseas. It also covers certain other designated people and supports their evacuation from threatened areas overseas, under the President’s direction and procedures developed by the Secretaries of Defense and State.

13075.s: This order creates a Special Oversight Board to review Department of Defense investigations into possible chemical or biological weapons exposures and other factors that may have contributed to Gulf War illnesses. The board advises the President through the Secretary of Defense, and its members are appointed by the President. It does not do scientific research or give advice on the federal government’s legal liability, and it must submit interim and final reports. The board ends 30 days after its final report is submitted.

13076.s: This order says it is necessary to add to the active armed forces of the United States for operations in and around Southwest Asia. It authorizes the Secretary of Defense, and the Secretary of Transportation for the Coast Guard in some cases, to order Selected Reserve units and individual members to active duty. It also says the order is meant only to improve internal management of the executive branch and does not create a legal right or benefit.

13077.s: This order further amends Executive Order 13010 on critical infrastructure protection. It changes two deadlines from March 15, 1998, to September 30, 1998, for the review and implementation of the President's Commission on Critical Infrastructure Protection report.

13078.s: This order creates a National Task Force on Employment of Adults with Disabilities. The task force is told to develop a coordinated federal policy to reduce barriers to work for adults with disabilities and to recommend steps to increase their employment. It also directs several federal agencies to review their programs, report on ways to improve employment opportunities, and measure the employment rate of adults with disabilities.

13079.s: This order waives the application of sections 402(a) and 402(b) of the Trade Act of 1974 with respect to Vietnam. It affects Vietnam and follows a report to Congress required by the Act.

13080.s: This order creates an advisory committee to review community nominations for American Heritage Rivers. The committee can recommend up to 20 rivers for the President to consider, and the President may designate ten of them. The committee also helps assess each nomination and reports its recommendations to the President.

13081.s: This order changes a deadline in Executive Order 13038 for the Advisory Committee on Public Interest Obligations of Digital Television Broadcasters. It replaces the June 1, 1998 reporting deadline with October 1, 1998.

13082.s: This order changes the membership of the Joint Mexican-United States Defense Commission. It adds a Joint Staff member to the United States membership, which already includes members from the Army, Navy, Air Force, and Marine Corps. The Secretary of Defense designates these members and chooses a chair from among them.

13083.s: This order tells federal agencies to follow federalism principles when making policies that affect the states. It says agencies should respect state authority, give states and local governments the most flexibility possible, and consider when federal action is needed. It also calls for consultation with state and local officials and for agencies to review waiver requests more quickly when allowed by law.

13084.s: This order directs federal agencies to consult with Indian tribal governments when making rules that significantly or uniquely affect their communities. It also tells agencies to reduce unfunded mandates on tribal governments and to streamline waiver applications. Agencies are encouraged to use agreed-upon ways to develop regulations on tribal self-government, trust resources, and treaty rights.

13085.s: This order creates an Enrichment Oversight Committee to monitor and coordinate U.S. government work on uranium enrichment after the privatization of the United States Enrichment Corporation. It covers the privatized USEC and any successor entities involved in uranium enrichment and related businesses.
