The committee must also oversee the HEU Agreement, foreign ownership or control issues, and information related to domestic uranium mining, enrichment, and conversion industries.

13086.s: This order changes several rules in the Manual for Courts-Martial, which affects military justice proceedings. It updates when a commander, reviewing officer, or military judge may keep a person in pretrial confinement, and it sets procedures for review and credit if the rules are not followed. It also changes rules on investigating uncharged offenses, mental competency, trial delays, contempt, and certain United States appeals in courts-martial.

13087.s: This order changes federal equal employment rules to add sexual orientation as a protected category. It also amends the existing language to include age or sexual orientation and says the rule applies to the extent permitted by law. It affects the Federal Government and its employment policies.

13088.s: This order blocks property and property interests of the governments of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (Serbia and Montenegro), the Republic of Serbia, and the Republic of Montenegro that are in the United States or under the control of United States persons. It also prohibits financial transactions with those governments by United States persons, with limited exceptions for some transactions in local currency, bank notes, or barter within the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (Serbia and Montenegro). The order also prohibits new investment by United States persons in the Republic of Serbia and bars helping others make such new investments.

13090.s: This order creates the President's Commission on the Celebration of Women in American History. The Commission is to recommend ways to acknowledge and celebrate the roles and accomplishments of women in American history, including a possible focal point in Washington, D.C. and ways to connect women's history sites, museums, and libraries. It is to report to the President by March 1, 1999 and then end 60 days after its final report.

13091.s: This order changes how certain arms export control and foreign assistance powers are assigned. It gives some functions to the Secretary of State and some to the Secretary of Defense, including matters tied to commercial exports, defense articles, defense services, and foreign military sales. It also adds consultation with the Secretary of Defense for one function and updates other related delegations.

13092.s: This order changes the name of the Advisory Committee on High Performance Computing and Communications, Information Technology, and the Next Generation Internet to the President's Information Technology Advisory Committee. It also increases the number of nonfederal members from 25 to 30.

13093.s: This order changes two earlier executive orders to let the President designate up to 20 rivers as American Heritage Rivers instead of ten. It affects the process for naming rivers under those orders.

13094.s: This order amends an earlier executive order to add measures against foreign persons who materially contribute to efforts to use, acquire, design, develop, produce, or stockpile weapons of mass destruction or missiles that can deliver them. It allows the Secretary of State to apply a procurement ban and an assistance ban, and it directs the Secretary of the Treasury to prohibit imports of goods, technology, or services from those foreign persons. It also keeps other existing authorities in effect and sets out some exceptions for government needs and current contracts.

13095.s: This order suspends Executive Order 13083, which was titled "Federalism." It says this is done to allow full and adequate consultation with state and local elected officials, their representative organizations, and other interested parties.

13096.s: This executive order directs federal agencies to improve education for American Indian and Alaska Native students. It sets goals for better reading and math, higher school completion and college attendance, less poverty and substance abuse barriers, safer and drug-free schools, stronger science education, and more education technology. It creates an interagency task force, asks agencies to consult with tribal governments, and calls for research, regional forums, and pilot schools to support these students.

13097.s: This order designates the Interparliamentary Union as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. That means it is entitled to the privileges, exemptions, and immunities given by that law. The order also says this does not limit any privileges, exemptions, or immunities the organization may already have or later get through international agreements or congressional action.

13098.s: This order blocks property and property interests of UNITA, certain senior UNITA officials, and adult members of their immediate families that are in the United States or under the control of United States persons. It also bars certain transactions, including importing some diamonds from Angola, supplying mining equipment, motorized vehicles, watercraft, mining services, and ground or waterborne transportation services in covered parts of Angola. It directs the Secretary of the Treasury and other U.S. agencies to take steps needed to carry it out and allows exemptions for medical and humanitarian purposes.

13099.s: This order revises an annex to an earlier executive order about terrorists who threaten to disrupt the Middle East peace process. It adds four persons or groups to that annex, including Usama bin Ladin and the Islamic Army. It says this is part of taking additional steps about grave acts of violence by foreign terrorists and the national emergency named in the earlier order.

13100.s: This executive order establishes the President's Council on Food Safety. The Council is directed to develop a strategic plan for federal food safety work, make recommendations to the President, and help federal agencies set priority areas for food safety spending. It also calls for coordinated budgets, research planning, and cooperation with state, local, tribal, private, and academic groups.

13101.s: This order directs executive agencies to add waste prevention and recycling to daily operations and to prefer pollution prevention when possible. It also tells agencies to use environmentally preferable products and services and to set up procurement programs that favor those purchases. The order creates a Steering Committee, a Federal Environmental Executive, a Task Force, and agency environmental executives to carry out these requirements.

13102.s: This order changes Executive Order 13038 to extend the reporting deadline for the Advisory Committee on Public Interest Obligations of Digital Television Broadcasters. It replaces the October 1, 1998 date with December 31, 1998.

13103.s:
This executive order directs executive agencies to work to prevent and combat computer software piracy. Agencies must adopt procedures so they do not acquire, reproduce, distribute, or transmit software in violation of copyright laws, and they must make sure only authorized software is used on agency computers.
It also says contractors and recipients of federal financial assistance should have systems to keep federal funds from being used for software that breaks copyright laws. Agency heads must help ensure compliance, educate staff, and use performance measures, while the Chief Information Officers Council and the Office of Management and Budget are to support agency oversight.

13104.s: This order changes Executive Order 13021 to keep the President's Board of Advisors on Tribal Colleges and Universities in place longer. It says the Board will end on September 30, 1999 unless the President renews it before then.

13105.s: This order directs the Secretary of State and the Director to set up open enrollment periods from November 1, 1998, to April 30, 1999. During those periods, employee participants in the Foreign Service Retirement and Disability System may choose the Foreign Service Pension System, and employee participants in the Central Intelligence Agency Retirement and Disability System may choose the Federal Employees' Retirement System. It applies to those employee participants in those retirement systems.

13106.s: This order sets new pay rates for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Health Administration, Senior Executive Service, and the uniformed services. It also keeps some executive and judicial salaries unchanged and sets locality-based comparability payments. The Director of the Office of Personnel Management is directed to carry out the locality payments and publish notice of them.

13107.s: This order directs U.S. agencies to respect and carry out the United States’ human rights treaty obligations, including the ICCPR, CAT, and CERD. It also tells agencies to handle human rights inquiries and complaints in their areas of responsibility and to coordinate on those matters. The order creates an Interagency Working Group on Human Rights Treaties to guide, oversee, and coordinate work on treaty implementation, reporting, complaints, and related reviews.

13108.s: This order changes the deadline for the Commission to Study Capital Budgeting to submit its report to February 1, 1999. It also changes the commission’s expiration date to September 30, 1999.

13109.s: This order closed executive departments and agencies of the federal government for the last half of the workday on Christmas Eve, December 24, 1998, and excused employees from duty during that time. Agency heads could keep some offices open and keep some employees working for national security, defense, or other essential public reasons. It also said the day would count under certain pay and leave laws for federal employees, and it did not apply to state or local governments.

13110.s: This order creates a working group to find, list, and recommend declassification of classified Nazi war criminal records held by the United States. It directs the group to help make those records available to the public at the National Archives, with some exceptions allowed by law. The group is to report to Congress within 1 year and ends 3 years after the order.

13111.s: This order creates a task force and an advisory committee to improve training for federal government employees through the use of technology. It directs federal agencies to set training goals, use recommended software standards where appropriate, and make training information more widely available to employees. It also asks for options for a Federal Individual Training Account and for ways to support training and post-secondary education for adult Americans.

13112.s: This order tells federal agencies to prevent the introduction of invasive species and to control them when they appear. It directs agencies to monitor invasive species, restore native species and habitats, do research, and educate the public. It also creates an Invasive Species Council and a management plan to coordinate federal action.

13113.s: This order extends the life of the President's Information Technology Advisory Committee. It also directs the committee to carry out its responsibilities under the Research Act in the manner described in that law. The order amends Executive Order 13035 to reflect the Research Act and changes the committee's end date to February 11, 2001.

13114.s: This order extends the life of the President's Council on Sustainable Development. It changes the end date in the earlier order from February 28, 1999 to June 30, 1999.

13115.s: This order creates an interagency task force on the roles and missions of the United States Coast Guard. The task force includes representatives from several federal departments and agencies, and it is led by a chair and vice chair chosen by the Secretary of Transportation. It must advise the President on the Coast Guard’s roles and missions through 2020, with special attention to deepwater missions. It also reviews Coast Guard law enforcement and national security missions while assuming the Coast Guard will remain a law enforcement agency and an armed force of the United States.

13117.s: This order amends an earlier executive order about export controls. It removes the Arms Control and Disarmament Agency from the voting process for dual-use export license decisions and deletes references to that agency in several sections. It affects the administration of export controls and the agencies named in the earlier order.

13118.s: This order changes how functions under the Foreign Affairs Reform and Restructuring Act of 1998 are carried out. It gives many foreign assistance and development functions to the Secretary of State, the United States Agency for International Development, the Secretary of Defense, and the Secretary of the Treasury. It also revokes or amends several older executive orders and sets different effective dates for some parts.

13119.s: This order designates the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (Serbia/Montenegro), Albania, the Adriatic Sea, the Ionian Sea north of the 39th parallel, and the airspace above them as a combat zone for purposes of section 112 of the Internal Revenue Code. It says U.S. Armed Forces are and have been engaged in combat in those areas. It also sets March 24, 1999, as the start date of combatant activities in the zone.

13120.s: This order says more active-duty forces are needed for operations in and around the former Yugoslavia related to the conflict in Kosovo. It authorizes the Secretary of Defense, and the Secretary of Transportation for the Coast Guard when it is not in the Navy, to order Selected Reserve units and certain Individual Ready Reserve members to active duty. It also allows their active-duty service to be ended.

13121.s: This executive order blocks property and interests in property of the governments of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (Serbia and Montenegro), the Republic of Serbia, and the Republic of Montenegro that are in the United States or under U.S. control. It also prohibits certain exports, imports, and other trade transactions involving those governments or the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia. The order directs special consideration for the government of Montenegro and for refugees from Kosovo and other civilians, and it authorizes some commercial sales of agricultural goods, medicine, and medical equipment for civilian use under safeguards.

13122.s: This order creates an interagency task force to coordinate federal efforts on the economic development of the Southwest Border region. It includes several cabinet departments and other federal agencies, and it is meant to work with state, tribal, and local governments, community leaders, Congress, and the private sector. The task force must study existing programs, recommend ways to support sustainable economic development, and focus first on pilot communities. It must also send reports to the Vice President and will end after its final report unless it is continued.

13123.s: This order directs federal departments and agencies to improve energy management and cut greenhouse gas emissions, energy use, petroleum use, and water consumption in their facilities. It also tells agencies to expand the use of renewable energy, including solar energy systems, and to use life-cycle cost analysis, audits, and energy-saving contracts and products. Each agency must make annual plans and reports, and a senior official must be designated to oversee these requirements.

13124.s: This order changes Civil Service rules for federal employees with psychiatric disabilities. It says they should have the same hiring rules as people with severe physical disabilities or mental retardation. It also lets an employee with psychiatric disabilities gain competitive status after at least 2 years of satisfactory service in an excepted position.

13125.s: This order sets up a White House initiative and an advisory commission to help improve the quality of life of Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders through more participation in federal programs. It asks federal departments and agencies to review their programs, prepare plans, and share information about participation and eligibility where possible. The commission is to advise the President on federal efforts, data collection, research, and ways to increase involvement from the public, private, and community sectors.

13126.s: This order directs federal agencies to enforce laws against goods made with forced or indentured child labor. It also directs the Department of Labor to publish a list of products that may have been made that way. For certain federal contracts, contractors must certify they made a good faith effort to check for forced or indentured child labor and must cooperate with requested records checks. Agencies may investigate, terminate contracts, or suspend or debar contractors if products were made with forced or indentured child labor, false certifications were made, or contractors failed to cooperate.

13127.s: This order amends a prior order to create the Information Coordination Center in the General Services Administration. The center helps the Chair of the President's Council on Year 2000 Conversion with information sharing, coordination, and agency assessments of Y2K emergencies that could affect U.S. interests at home and abroad. It also may help federal agencies with reconstitution processes and coordinate work to restore critical systems.

13128.s: This order makes the Department of State the U.S. National Authority for the Chemical Weapons Convention and the Chemical Weapons Convention Implementation Act. It sets up coordination with other departments and directs agencies to issue and revise rules needed to carry out the law and the Convention. It also gives the Secretary of Commerce authority to inspect certain facilities, suspend or revoke export privileges, and restrict imports of chemicals needed to meet the Convention's requirements.

13129.s: This order blocks property and property interests of the Taliban and certain people or groups tied to the Taliban that are in the United States or under control of United States persons. It also prohibits transactions by United States persons or within the United States involving blocked property, and bans the export, reexport, sale, supply, or import of goods, software, technology, or services connected to the Taliban or Taliban-controlled territory. The Secretary of the Treasury is directed to allow commercial sales of agricultural commodities, medicine, and medical equipment for civilian end use in Taliban-controlled territory, with safeguards to prevent diversion.

13130.s: This order creates the National Infrastructure Assurance Council, made up of up to 30 members from the private sector and state and local government. The council is meant to help government and private groups work together to protect critical infrastructure, review risks, and advise federal officials and other organizations on these issues. It also says the Department of Commerce will help run the council and provide support services.

13131.s: This order amends a prior order on the Enterprise for the Americas Initiative to include the Tropical Forest Conservation Act of 1998. It changes the duties of the Enterprise for the Americas Board and says the board will also advise on Tropical Forest Agreements. It also changes who serves on the board and who appoints some of its members.

13132.s: This order tells executive agencies to consider federalism when making policies that affect the States and the relationship between the national government and the States. It says agencies should consult State and local officials, give States more administrative discretion when possible, and limit preemption of State law to cases allowed by law. It also sets rules for agency regulations, legislative proposals, and waiver requests that affect State and local governments.

13133.s: This order creates a working group to address unlawful conduct that involves the use of the Internet. The group must prepare a report and recommendations on whether existing federal laws are enough to investigate and prosecute crimes like the illegal sale of guns, explosives, controlled substances, and prescription drugs, as well as fraud and child pornography. It must also look at whether new technology or legal powers are needed, and how to help parents, teachers, and others reduce these risks.

13134.s: This order directs federal agencies to develop a national strategy for biobased products and bioenergy. It sets up an interagency council, an advisory committee, and a coordination office to plan research, development, and adoption efforts. It also covers biobased products, biomass used for energy, and related work by the Agriculture and Energy departments.

13135.s: This order changes Executive Order 12216, which sets up the President’s Committee on the International Labor Organization. It changes one sentence in section 1-101 to add the Assistant to the President for Economic Policy to the list of people named there.

13136.s: This order changes the end date for the President's Commission on the Celebration of Women in American History from March 1, 1999, to December 31, 2000. It gives the commission more time to develop support systems and test the recommendations in its report to the President.

13137.s: This order amends an earlier order on the National Bioethics Advisory Commission. It says the commission is established in the Department of Health and Human Services and is subject to the Federal Advisory Committee Act. The commission may have up to 18 nongovernment members appointed by the President, with members chosen for certain areas of expertise and at least three from the general public. Members serve 2-year terms, and the President designates the chairperson.

13138.s: This order continues a list of federal advisory committees until September 30, 2001. It also says the heads of the named departments or agencies will carry out most of the President’s duties under the Federal Advisory Committee Act for those committees, except annual reporting to Congress. The order revokes several executive orders and parts of orders that set up committees whose work is finished. It also changes several other executive orders by adding agencies, changing committee duties, and updating membership rules.

13139.s: This order sets rules for giving certain investigational drugs to members of the Armed Forces during particular military operations. It says the Defense Department should collect information on health threats, work with Health and Human Services and the FDA, and use approved products when possible. It also requires informed consent unless the President grants a waiver, and it calls for training and health risk communication for military personnel.

13140.s: This order amends the Manual for Courts-Martial to change rules for military judges, court procedures, and evidence. It adds rules for a child to give remote live testimony in some abuse or domestic violence cases, and it limits when those procedures can be used if the accused chooses to leave the courtroom. It also creates a psychotherapist-patient privilege in UCMJ cases, with several exceptions, and changes sentencing and evidence rules that affect accused service members and victims.

13141.s: This order directs the United States to consider environmental impacts when developing trade agreements. It requires certain trade agreements to get written environmental reviews, including some multilateral trade rounds, free trade agreements, and major new trade liberalization agreements in natural resource sectors. The reviews are to be started early, open to public comment, and made public in draft and final form when practicable.

13142.s: This order changes the rules for when older classified records are automatically declassified. It extends one deadline, sets other time limits for records with information from more than one agency or with intelligence sources or methods, and says some records are declassified on December 31 of the year that is 25 years from the information’s origin. It also creates the Information Security Oversight Office within the National Archives and Records Administration and gives it duties to issue binding directives and review agency programs.

13143.s: This order changes the definition of “waterfront facility” in federal rules on safeguarding vessels, harbors, ports, and waterfront facilities. It says the term includes piers, wharves, docks, similar structures, naval yards, stations, installations, nearby land and water, and buildings, equipment, and materials on or near them.

13144.s: This order sets new basic pay rates and salaries for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Health Administration, Senior Executive Service, Executive Schedule, Vice President, Congress, and justices and judges. It also sets pay for members of the uniformed services, cadets or midshipmen, locality-based comparability payments, and administrative law judges. The Office of Personnel Management is directed to take actions needed to carry out the locality payments and publish notice in the Federal Register.

13145.s: This order sets a policy for equal employment opportunity in federal employment and bars discrimination based on protected genetic information or on a request for or receipt of genetic services. It applies to federal employees, applicants, and former employees covered by the Civil Rights Act section named in the order. Federal departments and agencies may not request, collect, use, or disclose protected genetic information except in the limited situations listed here, and they must keep it separate from personnel files. The order also allows some exceptions, including certain medical evaluations, voluntary genetic services, genetic monitoring with written consent, and some research and safety programs.

13146.s: This order creates an interagency council to develop recommendations for federal agency actions to address the future of Princeville, North Carolina. The council includes officials from several federal agencies and may consult with state and local governments. It is to look at repairs, rebuilding, and ways to protect Princeville from future floods, and it may include draft legislation for more funding or other authority.

13147.s: This order creates a White House commission in the Department of Health and Human Services on complementary and alternative medicine policy. The commission is to give the President recommendations on education and training, research, information for health care professionals and the public, and access to these practices. It also sets rules for the commission’s members, support, and how long it will last.

13148.s: This order tells federal agencies to build environmental management systems into their daily decisions, planning, and operations. It requires agencies and federal facilities to improve environmental compliance, use pollution prevention, and report progress each year. It also calls for agencies to reduce releases of toxic chemicals, reduce use of selected toxic chemicals and hazardous substances, and phase out some ozone-depleting substances.

13149.s: This order directs federal agencies with 20 or more motor vehicles in the United States to cut petroleum use in their fleets and increase the use of alternative fuel vehicles and alternative fuels. It also requires agencies to use strategies like buying higher fuel economy vehicles, using more alternative fuels, and reducing vehicle miles traveled and fleet size. The order sets reporting, planning, and leadership duties for federal offices and gives some agencies and vehicles specific credits, exemptions, and compliance rules.

13150.s: The order tells federal agencies to offer certain employees a transportation fringe benefit for mass transportation and vanpools. It also requires agencies in the National Capital Region to provide transit passes to qualified federal employees, and sets up a 3-year pilot program for three federal departments. Agencies may keep more generous programs already in place.

13151.s: This order establishes a Global Disaster Information Network to use information technology to help prepare for, respond to, and recover from natural and man-made disasters. It directs federal agencies to coordinate the collection and sharing of disaster-related information with response agencies, state governments, and, where appropriate, foreign governments. It also creates an interagency committee and support office to guide the network. Tribal governments are not required to do anything under this order, and some intelligence and national security activities are exempt.

13152.s: This order amends federal equal employment rules to prohibit discrimination based on a person's status as a parent. It defines that status to include biological, adoptive, foster, and stepparents, legal custodians, people in loco parentis, and people seeking legal custody or adoption. It also lets the Office of Personnel Management develop guidance on the order, and says the order does not create a right or benefit that can be enforced against the United States.

13153.s: This order tells the Secretary of Education to work with state and local school agencies to help improve low-performing schools. It calls for technical assistance, information on best practices, help with teacher quality, parent involvement, school accountability, and use of other education resources. It also requires an annual public report and stronger monitoring of federal school-improvement rules.

13154.s: This order creates the Kosovo Campaign Medal for members of the U.S. Armed Forces who served in Kosovo, or in nearby waters or airspace, after March 24, 1999, under rules set by military officials. It also says service members who already qualified for certain other medals for Kosovo service may keep those awards, but they may choose the Kosovo Campaign Medal instead of one of them. The medal may also be awarded after death under the same rules.

13155.s: This order says the United States will not seek to change or revoke intellectual property laws in eligible sub-Saharan African countries that regulate HIV/AIDS pharmaceuticals or medical technologies if those laws help people get access and still protect intellectual property rights under trade rules. It also tells the United States to encourage those countries to adopt policies that prevent HIV/AIDS, build health care delivery systems, and support research on vaccines and other medical innovations. It applies to U.S. government actions under the Trade Act of 1974 and to beneficiary sub-Saharan African countries.

13156.s: This order changes Executive Order 12871, which deals with labor-management partnerships in the Federal Government. It replaces the word "two" with "three" in section 1(a)(10) of that order. It affects the National Partnership Council and the federal labor-management partnership policy.

13157.s: This order tells federal agencies to take steps to increase opportunities for women-owned small businesses in federal procurement. It sets a goal of at least 5 percent of prime contract awards and 5 percent of subcontract awards for women-owned small businesses each fiscal year. It also directs the Small Business Administration to help agencies, track progress, and provide training and information for women-owned small businesses.

13158.s: This order directs federal agencies to protect marine protected areas and to establish or recommend new ones where appropriate. It calls for a national system of marine protected areas, with coordination among federal, state, territorial, tribal, and local governments. It also tells agencies to avoid harming protected marine resources and requires annual public reports on actions taken to carry out the order.

13159.s: This order blocks certain property and interests in property of the Government of the Russian Federation that are directly related to the HEU Agreements. It says that property in the United States, or under the control of U.S. persons, may not be transferred, paid, exported, withdrawn, or otherwise dealt in unless licensed or authorized. The order also directs federal agencies to take appropriate steps to carry it out.

13160.s: This order prohibits discrimination in federally conducted education and training programs based on race, sex, color, national origin, disability, religion, age, sexual orientation, or status as a parent. It covers programs and activities run by executive departments and agencies, including schools, training programs, scholarships, internships, and teacher training. It does not apply to the armed forces, military education or training programs, authorized intelligence activities, or certain other programs listed in the order. The Attorney General and each executive department and agency must set up complaint procedures and reporting requirements.

13161.s: This order establishes the Presidential Medal of Valor for Public Safety Officers. It is for public safety officers who are judged to have shown extraordinary valor above and beyond the call of duty in their official work. The term includes law enforcement officers, firefighters, emergency responders, and certain government or tribal employees. The medal may be given posthumously, and the President may choose up to ten people each year from recommendations by the Attorney General.

13162.s: This order creates the Federal Career Intern Program to recruit, select, train, and develop people for careers in the Federal workforce. It directs the Office of Personnel Management to set merit-based rules for recruiting, screening, placement, and career development, and it requires agencies to use training and job assignments for Career Interns. A successful candidate is appointed to a trainee-level position for up to 2 years, with possible extension, and service in the program does not by itself give a right to further federal employment. It also revokes Executive Order 12596.

13163.s: This order directs federal agencies to increase opportunities for individuals with disabilities to be employed in the Federal Government. Agencies must use available hiring authorities, expand outreach, and increase efforts to provide reasonable accommodations. It also says agencies do not have to create new positions or change existing qualification standards.

13164.s: This order requires each Federal agency to set up written procedures for handling requests for reasonable accommodation from employees and job applicants with disabilities. The procedures must explain how requests are made and decided, may include time limits, and must address medical information, denial notices, recordkeeping, and informal dispute resolution. Agencies must send their procedures to the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission and follow its guidance for carrying out the order.

13165.s: This order creates a White House Task Force on Drug Use in Sports. The task force must make recommendations to the President on further executive and legislative actions to address doping and drug use in sports, with a focus on athletes, especially young people. It also authorizes the Director of the Office of National Drug Control Policy to serve as the United States Government’s representative on the board of the World Anti-Doping Agency.

13166.s: The order tells federal agencies to improve access to their services for people with limited English proficiency. Agencies must make plans for their own programs and work with recipients of federal financial assistance to provide meaningful access. It also says agencies should consult with affected people and organizations when making these plans.

13167.s: This order changes a prior order to increase the White House Commission on Complementary and Alternative Medicine Policy from not more than 15 members to up to 20 members. It affects the commission by allowing more people to serve on it.

13168.s: This order creates a commission to advise the President on changes in the tobacco farming economy. The commission is to recommend ways to improve economic opportunity in communities dependent on tobacco production while protecting consumers, especially children, from smoking hazards. It will also review information about efforts to help tobacco growers, tobacco quota holders, and those communities find new economic opportunities.

13169.s: The order directs federal agencies to help small businesses export products, including businesses headed by women, minorities, or those in rural communities. It creates an interagency task force to help those businesses, especially in relation to China, Sub-Saharan Africa, and the Caribbean Basin. It also tells the Labor Department to speed help for workers who lose jobs because of imports and to improve outreach about adjustment assistance.

13170.s: This order directs executive branch agencies with procurement authority to increase federal contracting with businesses in the Small Disadvantaged Business Program, section 8(a) businesses, and Minority Business Enterprises. It tells agencies to improve outreach, training, subcontracting enforcement, and data reporting, and to use these businesses more in federal advertising, information technology, and GSA schedules. It also asks agencies to review bundled contracts and set procurement goals for these businesses and for small business concerns.

13171.s: This executive order directs executive departments and agencies to recruit and develop Hispanic employees in federal jobs. It says agencies must look for barriers, improve outreach, promote Hispanic employees in management and career development programs, and train managers on diversity management. It also directs the Office of Personnel Management to give guidance, issue regulations, create an interagency task force, and report to the President on agency progress.

13172.s: This order amends an earlier executive order to expand the National Task Force on Employment of Adults With Disabilities to also focus on young people with disabilities. It directs federal departments and agencies to work with the task force on research, training, public awareness, health insurance and health care access, and participation in postsecondary education and training. It also creates a national Youth Advisory Council to advise the task force.

13173.s: This order creates an interagency task force to coordinate federal efforts for the Central San Joaquin Valley in California. The task force includes several Cabinet departments and other federal agencies, and it is meant to work with state, tribal, and local governments, community leaders, and others. It must review programs, study the region’s needs, and develop short-term and long-term options for sustainable economic development. The task force must also send reports to the President on its work and progress.

13174.s: This order creates a Commission on Workers, Communities, and Economic Change in the New Economy. The commission is to study economic dislocation and how workers and communities adjust to changes from international trade, technology, globalization, and the changing nature of work. It must report its findings and recommendations to the President and Congress within 12 months after its first meeting, and it ends 30 days after submitting that report.

13175.s: This order requires federal agencies to consult and work with Indian tribal officials when making policies that have tribal implications. It tells agencies to respect tribal self-government and sovereignty, and to give tribal governments as much administrative discretion as possible when the law allows. It also sets rules for consulting on regulations, reviewing waiver requests, and submitting certifications for tribal-related rules and legislation.

13176.s: This order sets up a council to help coordinate the transition from the current administration to the President-elect. It directs federal offices to prepare orientation materials, a transition directory, and a catalogue of presidentially appointed Senate-confirmed positions. It also calls for a transition agreement between the current administration and the Office of the President-elect on transition procedures and contacts.

13177.s: This order creates a National Commission to review the use of offsets in defense trade and a related President's Council on the use of offsets in commercial trade. The commission includes members from the private sector, academia, and executive branch agencies, and the council is made up of the commission members or their designees. They will review how offsets affect defense subcontractors, other industries, trade competitiveness, national security, and the defense and commercial industrial base, and they must report their findings and possible measures to reduce harmful effects.

13178.s: This order establishes the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands Coral Reef Ecosystem Reserve in the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands. It directs that the reserve be managed for long-term protection of the coral reef ecosystem and related marine resources and species, with science-based management, research, monitoring, enforcement, and cleanup of marine debris. It also says culturally significant, noncommercial subsistence, cultural, and religious uses by Native Hawaiians should be allowed, and it starts the process to designate the area as a national marine sanctuary.

13179.s: This order sets up a program to provide compensation and benefits to certain Department of Energy nuclear weapons workers and their survivors for work-related illnesses. It gives the Departments of Labor, Health and Human Services, Energy, and Justice duties for handling claims, gathering information, and helping people apply. It also directs help for filing state workers' compensation claims and requires agencies to report on their work under the program.

13180.s: This order directs the Secretary of Transportation to establish a performance-based organization inside the FAA called the Air Traffic Organization. It places parts of the FAA’s air traffic services and research and acquisition work into that organization, while keeping the Administrator’s safety, security, and policymaking duties in place. The head of the organization must set goals, make a 5-year strategic plan, and work under an annual performance agreement. It also requires oversight and a later report on how well the organization works.

13181.s: This order says law enforcement may not use protected health information found during health oversight activities for unrelated civil, administrative, or criminal investigations unless the public interest clearly outweighs the risk of harm to the patient and the doctor-patient relationship. It sets rules for the Deputy Attorney General, and for the Defense Department when military members are involved, to approve such use and add safeguards. The Justice Department must also send an annual report to the President on these requests and their outcomes.

13182.s: This order sets new pay rates and salaries for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Health Administration, Senior Executive Service, executive salaries, uniformed services, and administrative law judges. It also provides for locality-based comparability payments and directs the Office of Personnel Management to carry out those payments and publish notice in the Federal Register. Most of the schedules take effect on the first day of the first applicable pay period, and Schedule 8 takes effect on January 1, 2001.

13183.s: This order creates the President’s Task Force on Puerto Rico’s Status. The task force is to help answer questions about Puerto Rico’s future status, study the options, and give advice and recommendations to the President and Congress. It is also to work with representatives of Puerto Rico and Congress and report on its actions and progress.

13184.s: This order revokes Executive Order 12834, which was about ethics commitments by executive branch appointees. After the effective date, employees and former employees covered by that order are no longer subject to those commitments.

13185.s: This order sets guiding and operating principles for the Federal Government-University research partnership. It says federal agencies that support university research should review their policies and procedures to fit those principles. The Office of Science and Technology Policy must regularly review the partnership and report on its status to the President.

13186.s: This order directs federal agencies whose actions are likely to have a measurable negative effect on migratory bird populations to develop and carry out agreements with the Fish and Wildlife Service. Those agreements are meant to promote conservation, limit harm to migratory birds, and address habitat, pollution, research, training, and reporting. It also creates an interagency council to oversee the order and share information, write an annual report, and foster partnerships.

13187.s: This order creates the President's Disability Employment Partnership Board. The Board gives advice and information on ways to help people with disabilities get jobs, and it works with Federal offices on public-private efforts, business opportunities, and small business support. Its members are appointed by the President, and the Department of Labor provides funding and support.

13188.s: This order extends the Advisory Committee on Expanding Training Opportunities. It changes the end date in a prior executive order to January 11, 2003.

13189.s: This order creates a Federal Interagency Task Force on the District of Columbia. The task force includes officials from several federal departments and agencies and is chaired by the Director of the Office of Management and Budget. Its job is to coordinate federal efforts for the District, help with financial stability and economic growth, and support self-government and local services. It also calls for assistance to economically distressed areas and efforts to consider concerns of local elected officials.

13190.s: This order creates the President's Commission on Educational Resource Equity. The commission must study gaps in educational resources, including finances, staff, facilities, instructional programs, and support services, and report to the President and Congress. It also must make recommendations for local, State, and Federal officials on how to achieve resource equity in education.

13191.s: This order sets up how federal officials will carry out parts of the African Growth and Opportunity Act and the United States-Caribbean Basin Trade Partnership Act. It lets officials make decisions on certain textile and apparel goods, including whether some items count as handloomed, handmade, or folklore articles, and whether some fabrics or yarns are available in commercial quantities. It also allows penalties for transshipment, including denial of trade benefits, and gives directions for export visa checks and emergency tariff actions.

13192.s: This order changes sanctions on the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia (Serbia and Montenegro) and updates earlier sanctions orders. It blocks property and interests in property of people listed in the order and of certain other people tied to the former Yugoslav government, the Republic of Serbia, the Republic of Montenegro, or Kosovo. It also bars United States persons from transactions with property of those designated people and prohibits attempts to evade those restrictions.

13193.s: This order makes it executive branch policy to take action on diseases caused by tobacco use around the world. It directs agencies to avoid promoting the sale or export of tobacco products and to support tobacco control work, including help to other countries and multilateral organizations. It also requires Health and Human Services to take part in trade talks about tobacco, study tobacco use in another country, and develop research and training programs with U.S. and other institutions.

13194.s: This order prohibits the direct or indirect import of rough diamonds from Sierra Leone into the United States. It does not apply to rough diamonds that are controlled through the Government of Sierra Leone's Certificate of Origin regime. It also forbids U.S. persons and others in the United States from trying to evade or violate these rules.

13195.s: This order directs federal agencies to work with Tribes, States, local governments, and citizen groups to protect, connect, promote, and assist trails across the United States. It also tells agencies to coordinate maps, signs, information, training, volunteer programs, and trail events. The order sets up interagency coordination on trail issues and calls for a handbook for federal trail administrators.

13196.s: This order makes permanent the Reserve Preservation Areas in the Northwestern Hawaiian Islands Coral Reef Ecosystem Reserve, with some changes. It limits certain commercial fishing and trolling activities, sets caps on fishing levels, and changes some rules about discharging material into the reserve. It also directs the Secretary of Commerce to manage the reserve under the earlier order and start the process to designate it as a National Marine Sanctuary.

13197.s: This order lets the Office of Personnel Management require executive agencies to report workforce information about civilian employees, including positions in the competitive, excepted, and Senior Executive services. It also lets OPM require agencies to set up accountability systems for merit system principles and to fix problems found. OPM may review agencies’ human resources programs and report to the agency head and the President. Certain agencies and intelligence-related units are excluded from some parts of the order.

13198.s: This order requires several departments to create centers for faith-based and community initiatives. The centers are meant to help remove barriers to the participation of faith-based and other community organizations in social service programs. It also requires some departments to review policies tied to "Charitable Choice" laws and to report on their work to the White House office.

13199.s: This order creates a White House office to coordinate federal efforts related to faith-based and other community organizations. The office is meant to expand their role, support their work, and help remove unnecessary barriers to their efforts. It also directs federal agencies to cooperate with the office and provide information and assistance as allowed by law.

13200.s: This order extends the life of the President’s Information Technology Advisory Committee. It lets the committee continue carrying out its responsibilities until June 1, 2001.

13201.s: This order requires most Government contractors to post a notice telling employees about their rights about union membership, union dues, and fees. The notice says employees cannot be required to join or stay in a union to keep their jobs, and that nonmembers may object to some payments and may be entitled to a refund or a reduction in future payments. The Secretary of Labor is responsible for enforcing the order, and contractors that do not comply can face cancellation, suspension, or debarment from future Government contracts.

13202.s: This order tells federal agencies not to require or ban bidders, contractors, or subcontractors from making agreements with labor organizations in bid documents for federal and federally funded construction projects. It also bars discrimination based on whether a contractor joins or refuses to join such agreements, while allowing voluntary agreements. The order does not apply to contracts awarded before its date, and it revokes earlier rules and a presidential memorandum on project agreements.

13203.s: This order revokes Executive Order 12871 and a later presidential memorandum about labor-management partnerships. It also dissolves the National Partnership Council and directs federal agencies to rescind rules, guidelines, and policies that carried out those measures. Any collective bargaining agreements already in effect are not changed by this order.

13204.s: This order revokes Executive Order 12933, which had required some new contractors for public buildings to give workers from the previous contractor a first chance at jobs. It also directs federal officials to rescind any related rules or policies and to end any investigations or compliance actions based on that order.

13205.s: This order sets up a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between Northwest Airlines and employees represented by the Aircraft Mechanics Fraternal Association. The board must report to the President within 30 days of being created. During that time, and for 30 days after the report is submitted, the parties may not change the conditions that led to the dispute unless they agree to do so.

13206.s: This order revokes Executive Order 12924 and rescinds the declaration of economic emergency for certain export controls. It affects export control rules and actions that were issued under that order and the International Emergency Economic Powers Act. The order says past violations under the revoked order are still covered, and the related rules, licenses, and other actions remain in force until changed or revoked by proper authority.

13207.s: This order changes Executive Order 10000, which deals with additional compensation and credit for certain federal employees serving outside the United States. It removes specific wording from sections 201, 205, and 210 of that order. The changes affect the rules for those employees and how the order is written.

13208.s: This order amends a prior order on Federal and federally funded or assisted construction projects. It lets the head of an executive agency exempt a particular project from some of the order’s requirements if certain project agreements or bid documents already had those requirements or prohibitions, and if construction contracts had already been awarded. The order is aimed at open competition, government neutrality in labor relations, lower construction costs, and preventing discrimination based on labor affiliation.

13209.s: This order changes a previous order to give the President's Task Force on Puerto Rico's Status more time to report to the President. It replaces the report date of May 1, 2001, with August 1, 2001.

13210.s: This order creates the President's Commission to Strengthen Social Security. The commission is to give the President bipartisan recommendations on how to modernize Social Security and restore its fiscal soundness, while not changing benefits for retirees or near-retirees, not raising payroll taxes, and not having the government invest Social Security funds in the stock market. It also says modernization must preserve disability and survivors benefits and include individually controlled, voluntary personal retirement accounts.

13211.s: This order requires certain federal agencies to prepare a Statement of Energy Effects for significant energy actions. The statement must describe possible adverse effects on energy supply, distribution, or use, including shortfalls, price increases, and greater use of foreign supplies, and it must discuss reasonable alternatives. Agencies must submit these statements and publish them in related proposed and final rules.

13212.s: This order directs federal agencies to speed up review of permits and other actions for energy-related projects, as allowed by law. It says they should do this to help increase energy production, transmission, and conservation while keeping safety, public health, and environmental protections in place. It also creates an interagency task force to help coordinate federal, state, tribal, and local permitting for these projects.

13213.s: The order prohibits the direct or indirect importation into the United States of all rough diamonds from Liberia, whether or not they originated there, unless allowed by later rules, orders, directives, or licenses. It also bans transactions or conspiracies that try to evade or violate these restrictions. The Secretary of the Treasury and other U.S. agencies are directed to take the steps needed to carry out the order.

13214.s: This order creates a 15-member task force to improve health care delivery for veterans. The task force is to look for ways to improve benefits and services by better coordinating the Department of Veterans Affairs and Department of Defense, including budgeting, billing, information technology, reimbursement, and sharing resources. It must report its findings and recommendations to the President, and it will end after its final report or no later than 2 years from the order.

13215.s: This order extends the life of the President’s Information Technology Advisory Committee so it can keep carrying out its duties. It changes the service terms for committee members appointed before or after June 1, 2001. It also says the President shall choose two co-chairs and extends a date in the earlier order to June 1, 2003.

13216.s: This order changes the title of Executive Order 13125 to "Increasing Opportunity and Improving Quality of Life of Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders." It also extends the President's Advisory Commission on Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders until June 7, 2003, unless the President renews it earlier. The order affects the commission and federal programs involving Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders.

13217.s: This order directs federal agencies to work with states to place qualified people with disabilities in community settings when that is appropriate. It says agencies should review their policies and programs, provide guidance, and help remove barriers to community-based services. It also directs the Attorney General and the Secretary of Health and Human Services to enforce Title II of the ADA and handle complaints about unjustified institutionalization.

13218.s: This order directs the Secretary of Labor to create an Office of the 21st Century Workforce in the Department of Labor. The office is to study workforce issues, gather and share information, and look for ways to update Labor Department services and reduce duplicate rules. It also creates a President’s Council on the 21st Century Workforce to advise the President on workforce issues, and it amends one prior executive order and revokes another.

13219.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of certain people and groups listed in the annex, and of others the Treasury Secretary designates with the Secretary of State. It applies to people found to have committed or supported violence in the Western Balkans, obstructed the Dayton Accords in Bosnia or U.N. Security Council Resolution 1244 in Kosovo, or provided support for those acts. United States persons are also barred from making donations or providing funds, goods, or services to designated persons.

13220.s: This executive order waives the application of two sections of the Trade Act of 1974 with respect to the Republic of Belarus. It affects trade rules that would otherwise apply to Belarus under those sections.

13221.s: This order tells executive agencies to buy products with external standby power devices or internal standby power functions that use no more than one watt in standby mode, when that is available and practical. If products meeting that standard are not available, agencies must buy the ones with the lowest standby power wattage. The Department of Energy must compile and finalize a list of products subject to these rules, and independent agencies are encouraged to follow them.

13222.s: This order declares a national emergency over unrestricted access of foreign parties to U.S. goods and technology and certain boycott practices of foreign nations. It keeps the export control system in full force and effect and lets existing rules, licenses, and other actions continue unless changed or revoked by the Secretary of Commerce. It also covers rules for section 38(e) of the Arms Export Control Act.

13223.s: This order lets the Department of Defense and the Department of Transportation call members of the Ready Reserve of the Armed Forces to active duty for up to 24 months. It also suspends certain laws about officer strength, promotion, retirement, and separation, and gives the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Transportation authority to use some of these powers. The order also allows certain Coast Guard officers and enlisted members to be ordered to active duty or detained, depending on how the Coast Guard is serving.

13224.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of certain foreign persons in the United States or under the control of United States persons. It also prohibits transactions by United States persons or within the United States involving blocked property, including contributions of funds, goods, or services to those persons. The order covers foreign persons listed in the annex, persons found to have committed or supported terrorism, and people or groups owned, controlled by, or associated with them. It directs United States agencies to take steps to carry out these restrictions and to work with other countries to stop terrorist financing.

13225.s: This order continues 14 federal advisory committees until September 30, 2003. It also says the head of each listed department or agency will carry out the President’s duties for those committees under the Federal Advisory Committee Act. The order revokes several earlier orders for committees that have ended and whose work is complete.

13226.s: This order creates the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology, or PCAST. The council is made up of up to 25 members, including one Federal Government official and 24 nonfederal members appointed by the President. PCAST advises the President on science and technology policy and helps the National Science and Technology Council bring in private sector involvement. The order also sets rules for how the council is run, pays its expenses from the Office of Science and Technology Policy, and says the council will end after 2 years unless the President extends it.

13227.s: This order creates a President's Commission on Excellence in Special Education. The commission must study federal, state, and local special education programs and recommend policies to improve educational results for students with disabilities. It must also review issues like funding, research, early reading help, staffing, and how rules affect special education services.

13228.s: This order creates an Office of Homeland Security inside the Executive Office of the President and puts it under the Assistant to the President for Homeland Security. The office is directed to coordinate federal efforts to detect, prevent, protect against, respond to, and recover from terrorist threats or attacks in the United States. It also creates a Homeland Security Council to advise and assist the President on homeland security and to coordinate related executive branch activities.

13229.s: This order extends the Task Force on Environmental Health Risks and Safety Risks to Children. It changes the time limit in the earlier order so the task force will serve for 6 years from the date of this order.

13230.s: This order creates a commission in the Department of Education to advise the Secretary of Education and report to the President on educational issues for Hispanic Americans. It also creates a White House Initiative in the Department of Education to support the commission and help gather and share information on the educational achievement gap. Federal departments and agencies are directed to provide information and cooperate, to the extent allowed by law, on participation in Federal education programs and related efforts. The order also revokes Executive Order 12900.

13231.s: This order creates the President’s Critical Infrastructure Protection Board to coordinate federal efforts to protect information systems for critical infrastructure and the physical assets that support them. It says the government should work through a voluntary public-private partnership and coordinate with private sector, state and local governments, and academic organizations. It also assigns responsibilities for federal departments and agencies, including security of executive branch and national security information systems, incident response, training, research, and law enforcement coordination.

13232.s: This order changes an earlier executive order to add the Department of Health and Human Services to a list of departments and agencies. It gives that department certain contracting authority in connection with national defense functions.

13233.s: This order sets procedures for the Archivist to handle requests for access to Presidential records that may be covered by constitutional privileges. It requires notice to the former President and the incumbent President, gives the former President time to review the records, and lets the incumbent President decide whether to agree to withholding or release. It also applies similar procedures to certain Vice Presidential records and revokes Executive Order 12667.

13234.s: This order creates a Presidential Task Force on Citizen Preparedness in the War on Terrorism. The task force is made up of heads of several executive branch offices and departments, and it may also include other senior officials. It is directed to find ways the American public can prepare at home, work, school, and other places for possible terrorist attacks and volunteer to help state and local officials respond. The task force must send its recommendations to the President within 40 days and then end 30 days after that report is submitted.

13235.s: This order invokes emergency construction authority under 10 U.S.C. 2808. It makes that authority available to the Secretary of Defense and, if the Secretary chooses, to the secretaries of the military departments. It says this is to help respond to the national emergency after the terrorist attacks on the World Trade Center and the Pentagon and the continuing threat of more attacks.

13236.s: This order lets the Director of Central Intelligence waive certain dual compensation limits for a temporary employee when needed because of an emergency with a direct threat to life or property, or because of other unusual circumstances. It applies to employees who receive both salary and annuity under this authority, and they may not earn additional retirement benefits during that time.

13237.s: This order creates the President's Council on Bioethics. The council advises the President on bioethical issues tied to advances in biomedical science and technology, and it may study topics like embryo and stem cell research, assisted reproduction, cloning, human genetics, neuroscience, and end of life issues. It is made up of up to 18 members from science, medicine, law, government, philosophy, theology, and other humanities and social science fields.

13238.s: The order closes executive branch departments and agencies of the Federal Government on Monday, December 24, 2001, and excuses their employees from duty. Department and agency heads may keep some offices open and require some employees to work for national security, defense, or other public reasons. It also treats that day under laws and orders that relate to employee pay and leave.

13239.s: This order designates Afghanistan, including the airspace above it, as an area where U.S. Armed Forces are and have been engaged in combat. It also sets September 19, 2001, as the start date of combatant activities in that zone.

13240.s: This order designates the Council of Europe’s Group of States Against Corruption, called GRECO, as a public international organization. It gives GRECO the privileges, exemptions, and immunities allowed under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It also says this designation does not reduce any privileges, exemptions, or immunities GRECO may already have or later get by international agreement or law.

13241.s: This order sets an order of succession for the office of Secretary of Agriculture. If both the Secretary and Deputy Secretary have died, resigned, or are unable to serve, certain Agriculture officials would act as Secretary in the order listed. It also says no one serving in an acting capacity may act under this order, and the President may depart from it as allowed by law.

13242.s: This order sets the line of succession for the Department of Commerce if both the Secretary and Deputy Secretary cannot serve. It lists several department officers who would act as Secretary in a set order. It also says a person serving in one of those jobs in an acting capacity cannot use this order to become Secretary, and it revokes three earlier succession orders or sections.

13243.s: This order sets the line of succession for the Department of Housing and Urban Development if both the Secretary and Deputy Secretary are unable to serve. It names several HUD officials, in a set order, who would act as Secretary. It also revokes Executive Order 11274.

13244.s: This order sets a line of succession for the Secretary of the Interior if both the Secretary and Deputy Secretary have died, resigned, or cannot serve. It says certain Interior officers, in the listed order, would act as Secretary. It also revokes Executive Order 11487.

13245.s: This order sets the line of succession for the Secretary of Labor if both the Secretary and Deputy Secretary have died, resigned, or cannot do the job. It names several Labor Department officers, in order, who would act as Secretary. It also says no one serving in one of those posts in an acting capacity may act as Secretary under this order, and it revokes Executive Order 10513.

13246.s: This order sets the line of succession for who will act as Secretary of the Treasury if both the Secretary and Deputy Secretary cannot serve. It lists Treasury officers who would take over in a set order, based on their office and the order they took the oath. It also says no one serving in an acting role may serve under this order, and it revokes Executive Order 11822.

13247.s: This order sets the line of succession for the Secretary of Veterans Affairs if both the Secretary and Deputy Secretary die, resign, or are unable to serve. It names several Veterans Affairs officers who would act as Secretary in a listed order, starting with the Under Secretary for Health. It also says no one serving in one of those offices in an acting capacity may act as Secretary under this order, and the President may depart from this order when allowed by law.

13248.s: This order creates a three-member board to investigate and report on a dispute between United Airlines and its mechanics and related employees represented by the International Association of Machinists and Aerospace Workers. The board must report to the President within 30 days of being created. Until then, and for 30 days after the report is submitted, the parties may not change the conditions that led to the dispute unless both sides agree.

13249.s: This order sets new basic pay rates and salaries for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Health Administration schedules, the Senior Executive Service, the Executive Schedule, the Vice President, Congress, and federal judges. It also sets pay rates for members of the uniformed services and cadets and midshipmen, and provides for locality-based comparability payments. The Office of Personnel Management must take steps to carry out the locality payments. Executive Order 13182 is superseded.

13250.s: This order sets the line of succession for the Secretary of Health and Human Services. If both the Secretary and Deputy Secretary cannot serve, certain officials named in the order will act as Secretary in the listed order. It says people already serving in those offices in an acting role cannot act as Secretary under this order, and the President may depart from the order where allowed by law.

13251.s: This order sets a line of succession for the Secretary of State. If the Secretary dies, resigns, or cannot do the job, the listed officers would act as Secretary in the order named. It says only Senate-confirmed officials may act as Secretary under this order, and the President may depart from the order as allowed by law. It also revokes Executive Order 12343.

13252.s: This order excludes certain parts of the Department of Justice from the Federal Labor-Management Relations Program. It says these subdivisions do intelligence, counterintelligence, investigative, or national security work, and that chapter 71 of title 5 cannot be applied to them in a way that fits national security requirements. The affected offices are United States Attorneys' Offices, the Criminal Division, INTERPOL--U.S. National Central Bureau, the National Drug Intelligence Center, and the Office of Intelligence Policy and Review.

13253.s: This order changes a prior order about calling Ready Reserve members of the Armed Forces to active duty. It gives the Secretary of Transportation authority over certain Coast Guard personnel matters and reserve forces powers. It also lets the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Transportation treat the cost of additional active duty members as an excepted expense under their control.

13254.s: This order creates the USA Freedom Corps as an interagency effort to promote public service and make service opportunities easier to find. It encourages Americans to serve their country for the equivalent of at least 2 years over their lifetimes. It also sets up a USA Freedom Corps Council and Office to coordinate federal service programs, share information, and recognize volunteers and other participants.

13255.s: This order changes the reporting date for the President's Commission on Excellence in Special Education. It replaces "April 30, 2002" with "July 1, 2002" in the earlier executive order.

13256.s: This order creates a presidential advisory board on Historically Black Colleges and Universities in the Office of the Secretary of Education. The board must report each year to the President and give advice on the needs of these schools, including infrastructure, academic programs, faculty, and institutional development. It also directs federal departments and agencies to make plans to help these colleges take part in federal programs and to provide technical assistance and information. The order also calls for a private sector strategy to increase contributions and partnerships that support these institutions.

13257.s: This order creates a task force to monitor and combat trafficking in persons. The task force includes several top federal officials and is chaired by the Secretary of State. It coordinates work on the law, tracks progress, helps prepare annual reports, and works with other countries and organizations to prevent trafficking and help victims.

13258.s: This order changes Executive Order 12866 on regulatory planning and review. It replaces several references to the Vice President with references to the Director, the Chief of Staff, or other named officials. It also updates which officials are listed in parts of the review and conflict-resolution process.

13259.s: This order designates the European Union and the European Police Office (Europol) as "public international organizations" for certain parts of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 and the Foreign Corrupt Practices Act of 1977. It includes the listed institutions, departments, agencies, and instrumentalities of the European Union and Europol. The designation is only for those laws and does not decide how other laws or regulations apply.

13260.s: This order creates the President's Homeland Security Advisory Council and four Senior Advisory Committees for Homeland Security. The council is made up of members from the private sector, academia, state and local governments, and other groups, and it advises the President through the Assistant to the President for Homeland Security. It is meant to help with homeland security strategy, coordination, and measures related to terrorist threats or attacks within the United States. The council and committees serve without pay, may get travel expenses, and end after 2 years unless extended.

13261.s: This order sets the line of succession for the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency if both the Administrator and Deputy Administrator cannot serve. It lists EPA officials who would act in that role in the order named. It also changes succession rules in several other executive orders for other departments.

13262.s: This order amends the Manual for Courts-Martial and changes several rules for military trials. It removes Federal Rule of Evidence 415 from military rules, updates what special courts-martial can punish, and changes rules on evidence, protective orders, fines, confinement, and record keeping. It also changes when a military judge is required, when appellate review can be waived, and how records are reviewed after certain sentences.

13263.s: This order creates the President's New Freedom Commission on Mental Health. The Commission must study the U.S. mental health service system and advise the President on ways to improve it, with a focus on people with serious mental illness and children with serious emotional disturbances. It must also report on unmet needs, barriers to care, and recommendations for better services and coordination.

13264.s: This order changes Executive Order 13180 by deleting the words “an inherently governmental function” from its first sentence. It also says the order is only for internal management of the executive branch and does not create any right to administrative or judicial review. It also does not give any person a right to enforce the order against the United States or its officers or employees.

13265.s: This order creates the President's Council on Physical Fitness and Sports and tells the Secretary of Health and Human Services to develop and coordinate a national program to increase physical activity and sports participation. The program is meant to reach all Americans, with special emphasis on children and adolescents, and on communities where there are risks or gaps in access or knowledge. The Council advises the President and the Secretary on ways to improve physical fitness and sports programs, public awareness, and partnerships with public and private groups.

13266.s: This order directs several federal departments and offices to review their policies, programs, and regulations that relate to the personal fitness of the general public. They are to consider changes or new programs to help increase physical activity, promote responsible dietary habits, increase use of preventive health screenings, and encourage healthy choices about alcohol, tobacco, drugs, and safety. It also creates an interagency working group to coordinate federal personal fitness activities and reduce waste and overlap.

13267.s: This order creates a Transition Planning Office within the Office of Management and Budget for the proposed Department of Homeland Security. The office is directed to coordinate transition planning across the executive branch and to work with Congress as it considers legislation to create that department.
