The Director of OMB must provide personnel, funding, and support, and other executive departments and agencies must assist to the extent allowed by law.

13268.s: This order ends the national emergency that had been declared with respect to the Taliban. It also amends a previous order by adding Mohammed Omar and the Taliban to the annex. The order says the Taliban is also known by several other names and that some earlier actions and pending matters are not affected.

13269.s: This order sets a period starting on September 11, 2001 for purposes of a naturalization exception. It makes aliens and noncitizen nationals who are serving honorably in active-duty status in the Armed Forces during that period eligible for expedited naturalization under the Immigration and Nationality Act. It says this period will end on a date set by a future Executive Order.

13270.s: This order sets federal policy to extend support for educational excellence and opportunity to tribal colleges and universities that serve Indian tribes and Alaska Native entities. It creates a presidential board and a White House initiative to advise on tribal colleges, help coordinate federal agencies, and support their work with these schools. It also directs participating agencies to make three-year plans, report on their progress, and provide information and assistance to tribal colleges.

13271.s: This order directs the Attorney General to create a Corporate Fraud Task Force within the Department of Justice. The task force is meant to help investigate and prosecute significant financial crimes, recover proceeds from those crimes, and recommend better coordination and policy changes. It includes Justice Department officials and, for some functions, certain other federal agency leaders.

13272.s: This order tells federal agencies to set procedures to better consider the effects of draft rules on small businesses, small governmental jurisdictions, and small organizations. It also tells the Small Business Administration’s Chief Counsel for Advocacy to advise agencies, give training, and comment on draft rules. Agencies must notify Advocacy about certain draft rules and respond to its comments in final rule explanations when required.

13273.s: This order says the security of the United States is endangered by disturbances in international relations that have existed since the September 11, 2001 attacks. It changes Coast Guard rules for safeguarding vessels, harbors, ports, and waterfront facilities. It adds a definition for "Area Commander" and updates who may enforce the rules and under whose direction.

13274.s: This order directs federal agencies to promote environmental stewardship in the nation’s transportation system and to speed up environmental reviews of transportation infrastructure projects. It also tells the Secretary of Transportation to identify high-priority projects for expedited review. A Transportation Infrastructure Streamlining Task Force is created to help coordinate reviews, permits, and agency cooperation for these projects.

13275.s: This order creates a Board of Inquiry to look into a labor dispute between longshore and warehouse union employees and certain steamship, stevedore, and terminal employers in California, Oregon, and Washington. The dispute involves a lock-out affecting the maritime industry, including trade, transportation, and communication. The Board must report to the President and may keep working only as allowed under the Labor Management Relations Act.

13276.s: This order gives the Attorney General, Secretary of State, and Secretary of Defense duties for undocumented aliens interdicted or intercepted in the Caribbean region. It lets the Attorney General keep custody, screen them, and provide housing and care, including at Guantanamo Bay Naval Base or another suitable location. It directs the Secretary of State to help protect people found to be in need of protection and arrange resettlement in other countries when appropriate. It also lets the Defense Secretary provide facilities, access, security, and support in a mass migration.

13277.s: This order delegates many authorities and functions under the Trade Act of 2002 to the U.S. Trade Representative. It keeps some powers with the President and assigns certain tasks to the Secretaries of State, Labor, and Treasury. It also sets who will carry out parts of the trade promotion and Andean Trade Preference Act programs within the federal government.

13278.s: This order creates a commission to examine the United States Postal Service and write a report for the President. The commission will look at the Postal Service’s role, its pricing and cost flexibility, service changes, long-term delivery of mail at affordable rates, and its oversight structure. It will also recommend legislative and administrative reforms needed to keep postal services viable. The commission will include nine members appointed by the President and will end after it submits its report.

13279.s: This order tells federal agencies to review and update policies that affect faith-based and other community organizations. It says eligible organizations should be able to compete for federal aid for social service programs, and that no group should be discriminated against because of religion or religious belief. It also says religious activities must be kept separate from services supported with direct federal financial assistance, and participation in those activities must be voluntary.

13280.s: This order tells the Department of Agriculture and the Agency for International Development to each create a Center for Faith-Based and Community Initiatives. The centers are meant to help remove barriers to faith-based and other community organizations taking part in social services and agency programs. They must also report on those barriers, outreach efforts, and ways to improve participation.

13281.s: This order closes all executive branch departments and agencies of the federal government for the last half of the workday on Tuesday, December 24, 2002. Their employees are excused from duty for that time. Agency heads may keep some offices open and require some employees to work for national security, defense, or other public reasons. It also says that day counts under certain federal pay and leave laws.

13282.s: This order sets new basic pay rates for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Health Administration, Senior Executive Service, executive salaries, uniformed services, and administrative law judges. It also provides locality-based comparability payments and tells the Office of Personnel Management to carry them out and publish notice in the Federal Register.

13283.s: This order creates an Office of Global Communications within the White House Office. The office advises the President and other officials on how the U.S. government can keep messages consistent and inform audiences abroad. It also works with agencies on truthful, accurate, and effective messages, and may help coordinate temporary information teams for short-term placement in areas of high global interest and media attention.

13284.s: This order amends many earlier executive orders to add the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Department of Homeland Security to their lists and duties. It also gives the Secretary of Homeland Security responsibility for coordinating domestic response efforts for a set period, and it designates certain Homeland Security elements as part of the Intelligence Community. The order also authorizes the Secretary of Homeland Security to classify information originally as "Top Secret."

13285.s: This order creates the President's Council on Service and Civic Participation within the Corporation for National and Community Service. The Council is to encourage volunteer service and civic participation, especially among America's youth, and to help spread information about ways Americans have served their communities and nation. It also lets the Council advise federal officials, recommend programs, and work with schools and youth organizations. The Council members serve without pay, and the order expires after 2 years unless the President extends it.

13286.s: This order changes several earlier executive orders to replace other officials or agencies with the Secretary of Homeland Security or the Department of Homeland Security. It moves some responsibilities for undocumented aliens interdicted in the Caribbean, homeland security advice, domestic incident management, and critical infrastructure protection to Homeland Security. It also amends other task forces and councils to add the Secretary of Homeland Security or the department as a member or coordinating office.

13288.s: This order declares a national emergency about actions in Zimbabwe that undermine democratic processes or institutions. It blocks property and interests in property of certain listed persons, and of people owned or controlled by them, when that property is in the United States or under the control of United States persons. It also bars United States persons and people in the United States from dealing in that blocked property or making contributions to listed persons or related people.

13289.s: This order establishes the Global War on Terrorism Expeditionary Medal and the Global War on Terrorism Service Medal. These medals are for members of the Armed Forces of the United States who served in military expeditions or military operations to combat terrorism on or after September 11, 2001, under rules set by the military departments, the Secretary of Defense, or the Secretary of Homeland Security for the Coast Guard. It also lets some members keep qualifying for the Armed Forces Expeditionary Medal or Armed Forces Service Medal, and allows the new medals to be awarded posthumously.

13290.s: This order confiscates certain blocked funds in the United States that are in accounts of the Government of Iraq, the Central Bank of Iraq, Rafidain Bank, Rasheed Bank, or the State Organization for Marketing Oil. Those funds are vested in the Department of the Treasury, with exceptions for certain diplomatic or consular funds and some funds tied to judgment writs. The Secretary of the Treasury is authorized to carry out the order and take needed steps to do so. The order says the vested property should be used to assist the Iraqi people and the reconstruction of Iraq.

13291.s: This order changes certain pay rates in a prior executive order. It sets a new schedule for justices and judges and changes how locality-based comparability payments are paid under Schedule 9.

13292.s: This order sets rules for classifying, protecting, and declassifying national security information, including information about defense against transnational terrorism. It applies to information held by the U.S. Government and to officials who classify information, along with employees, contractors, licensees, certificate holders, and grantees who may handle it. It sets three classification levels, limits when information can be classified, and gives rules for marking and declassifying it.

13293.s: This order changes the rules for the National Defense Service Medal. It extends eligibility to members in good standing in the Selected Reserve of the Armed Forces. It also updates the wording of the earlier order to reflect that change.

13294.s: This order gives the Secretaries of Defense, Commerce, Health and Human Services, and Homeland Security the power to exercise certain authority about hazardous duty incentive pay, aviation career incentive pay, and submarine duty incentive pay for members of the uniformed services under their control. It says they can do this without approval or other action by the President, and they must consult with each other to try to treat similarly situated members the same unless their services need different treatment. It also revokes two earlier executive orders on the same subject.

13295.s: This order sets a revised list of communicable diseases for rules that allow the apprehension, detention, or conditional release of people to help prevent the introduction, transmission, or spread of those diseases. The list includes cholera, diphtheria, infectious tuberculosis, plague, smallpox, yellow fever, viral hemorrhagic fevers, and Severe Acute Respiratory Syndrome (SARS). It also gives the Secretary of Health and Human Services discretion to decide whether a condition is a disease covered by the order.

13296.s: This order amends an earlier order about protecting children from environmental health and safety risks. It extends the Task Force on Environmental Health Risks and Safety Risks to Children and changes some of its reporting rules. It also changes the task force’s term from 6 years to 8 years and changes some annual reports to biennial reports.

13297.s: This order applies rules from the Federal Physicians Comparability Allowance Amendments of 2000 to three retirement and disability systems: the Foreign Service Retirement and Disability System, the Foreign Service Pension System, and the Central Intelligence Agency Retirement and Disability System. It says the physicians comparability allowance must be counted as basic pay and included in annuity calculations under the same rules used for the Civil Service Retirement System or the Federal Employees Retirement System, depending on the system. It also directs the Secretary of State and the Director of Central Intelligence to issue regulations to carry out these changes, with the rules made retroactive to December 28, 2000.

13298.s: This order ends the national emergency tied to the actions and policies of UNITA. It also revokes Executive Orders 12865, 13069, and 13098. Actions already taken, pending proceedings, and rights, duties, or penalties that had already matured are not affected.

13299.s: This executive order creates the Interagency Group on Insular Areas within the Department of the Interior for administrative purposes. The group is made up of the heads of executive departments and any other agencies the Secretary of the Interior designates. It gives the group a role in advising on policies and policy actions affecting American Samoa, Guam, the United States Virgin Islands, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, including reports to the President and the Secretary of the Interior. It also allows the group to get advice from governors, other elected officials, and other people about these areas.

13300.s: This order directs federal departments and agencies to help carry out a plan for timely judicial nominations. It says the President should submit nominations to fill vacancies in United States courts of appeals and district courts within 180 days after notice of a vacancy or intended retirement, unless there are extraordinary circumstances. It also says the order does not change the President's constitutional authority to fill vacancies and does not create a legal right or benefit.

13301.s: This order changes Executive Order 12863 by replacing the word “four” with “five” in section 2.1. It increases the number of members on the Intelligence Oversight Board from four to five.

13302.s: This order changes an earlier order on energy-related projects to include projects that will strengthen pipeline safety. It also changes the interagency task force so it can help speed reviews of permits, coordinate federal, state, tribal, and local permitting, and carry out pipeline safety-related functions. The task force includes specified federal officials and is chaired by the Chairman of the Council on Environmental Quality.

13303.s: This order blocks certain court actions, like attachment, judgments, liens, and garnishments, against the Development Fund for Iraq and certain Iraqi petroleum and petroleum products. It also says Executive Orders 12722, 12724, and 13290 do not apply to that property and those interests. The Secretary of the Treasury and other U.S. agencies are directed to take actions needed to carry out the order.

13304.s: This order ends the national emergencies declared in 1992 and 1998 with respect to the former Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and revokes related orders. It also changes Executive Order 13219 by replacing its annex and revising the rules for blocking property of certain listed or designated persons. The order keeps some sanctions in place for people tied to open indictments, violence, obstruction of peace agreements, support for those acts, or ownership and control by such persons.

13305.s: This executive order extends the life of the President's Information Technology Advisory Committee and the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology. It changes the end dates for those committees so they can continue carrying out their responsibilities.

13306.s: This order establishes the Bob Hope American Patriot Award. The President may give it to a civilian person or an organization that has shown extraordinary love of country and devotion to members of the United States Armed Forces. The award may be given posthumously, and usually no more than one may be granted in a year except in exceptional circumstances.

13307.s: This order extends to the European Central Bank the privileges, exemptions, and immunities given to public international organizations designated by the President under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It also says this extension does not limit any privileges, exemptions, or immunities the bank may already have or may get under international agreements or law.

13308.s: This order changes how some Superfund and brownfields duties are handled within the federal government. It gives certain functions to the heads of executive departments and agencies, and other functions to the Administrator, with some decisions made in consultation with the appropriate federal natural resource trustee. It also says the order is only for internal government management and does not create a legal right or benefit for anyone.

13309.s: This order renames the President's Committee on Mental Retardation as the President's Committee for People with Intellectual Disabilities. It also updates Executive Order 12994 to replace the older term with "intellectual disabilities" throughout most of the order. The order expands the committee's membership by adding several Cabinet secretaries and continues the committee until September 30, 2005.

13311.s: This order assigns some homeland security information-sharing functions to the Secretary of Homeland Security. It also gives one function to the Attorney General and the Director of Central Intelligence to exercise jointly. The Secretary’s procedures on access to classified information will apply to all federal agencies, and decisions about access for state and local personnel will be final and not subject to review or appeal.

13312.s: This order puts rules in place to carry out the Clean Diamond Trade Act and the Kimberley Process Certification Scheme for rough diamonds. It prohibits importing or exporting rough diamonds unless they have been controlled through that scheme, and it also bars transactions or conspiracies that try to evade those rules. It also updates earlier orders covering rough diamonds from Sierra Leone and Liberia.

13313.s: This executive order assigns the President’s duty to send certain recurring reports to Congress to specific executive branch officials. It gives reporting duties to the Secretaries of State, Treasury, Defense, and Commerce, the Director of Central Intelligence, and the Director of National Drug Control Policy. It also covers some reports described in Senate resolutions. The order says it is for internal executive branch management and does not create a legal right or benefit.

13314.s: This order waives parts of section 402 of the Trade Act of 1974 with respect to Turkmenistan. It affects the application of those trade rules to Turkmenistan.

13315.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of the former Iraqi regime, its state bodies, and certain senior officials, their immediate family members, and controlled entities. It also bars transactions that try to evade the order and prohibits donations covered by the order. The Secretary of the Treasury may confiscate certain blocked property and transfer it to the Development Fund for Iraq for use on humanitarian needs, reconstruction, disarmament, civilian administration, and other purposes benefiting the Iraqi people.

13316.s: This order continues several federal advisory committees until September 30, 2005. It also says the head of the named department or agency will carry out the President’s functions under the Federal Advisory Committee Act for those committees. The order revokes several earlier executive orders that created committees that had ended or finished their work, and it amends Executive Order 12131.

13317.s: This order creates the Volunteers for Prosperity initiative to encourage highly skilled Americans to volunteer abroad. It covers USAID, the Department of State, the Department of Commerce, the Department of Health and Human Services, and any other agencies the President later designates. The agencies are to set up offices for the program, support volunteer service organizations, and consider volunteer use when reviewing grant applications for assistance work overseas. USAID is named as the inter-agency coordinator for the initiative.

13318.s: This order creates the Presidential Management Fellows Program to recruit and select outstanding employees for public sector management in the Federal service. It sets eligibility rules for PMFs and Senior PMFs, including graduate-level study or extensive work experience, and requires merit-based recruitment, equal employment opportunity, and veterans' preference. Fellows are appointed to certain federal positions for up to 2 years, with a possible 1-year extension, and generally do not have a right to further federal employment unless they meet later requirements.

13319.s: This order changes the President's Task Force on Puerto Rico's Status. It says the task force will include designees from each Cabinet member and the Deputy Assistant to the President and Director for Intergovernmental Affairs. It also says the task force must report to the President as needed, but at least once every 2 years, on progress toward determining Puerto Rico's ultimate status.

13320.s: This order closed executive branch departments and agencies of the Federal Government on Friday, December 26, 2003, and excused employees from duty that day. Agency heads could keep some offices open and require some employees to report for reasons of national security, defense, or other public need. It also treated that day as covered by certain pay and leave rules for federal employees.

13321.s: This order invokes emergency appointments authority and makes it available to the Secretary of Defense under the terms of the law and a prior executive order. It also says the order does not create any legal right or benefit that can be enforced against the United States or its officers.

13322.s: This order sets new pay rates and salary ranges for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Health Administration, Senior Executive Service, Executive Schedule, Vice President and Congress, judges, and uniformed services. It also sets locality-based comparability payments and pay for administrative law judges. The order gives the Office of Personnel Management steps to carry out the locality payments and replaces a prior executive order on pay rates.

13323.s: This order assigns to the Secretary of Homeland Security the President’s functions under section 215(a) of the Immigration and Nationality Act for persons other than citizens of the United States. It assigns to the Secretary of State the President’s functions under section 215(a) and (b) for citizens of the United States, including U.S. passports. Each secretary must get the other’s approval or consultation before issuing, amending, or revoking rules, regulations, or orders in these areas.

13324.s: This executive order ends the national emergency that had been declared for Sierra Leone and expanded for Liberia. It also revokes the two earlier orders tied to that emergency. The order says it does not change actions already taken, pending proceedings, or rights or duties that had already matured.

13325.s: This order changes the basic salary ranges for classes in the Senior Foreign Service. It says members will keep the rate of basic pay they were getting before the change, including any locality-based comparability payment. It also allows the Secretary of State, or other agency heads using the Foreign Service system, to raise a member’s pay based on performance or mission contribution if the member is otherwise eligible.

13326.s: This order creates the President’s Commission on Implementation of United States Space Exploration Policy. The commission is to give recommendations on how to carry out the President’s space exploration policy, including research on the Moon and other destinations, future exploration destinations, possible private and international roles, and ways to manage the work within available resources. NASA will provide administrative support and funding, and the commission will end after it submits its final report.

13327.s: This order directs federal agencies to manage federal real property more efficiently and economically, and to improve accountability for those reforms. It requires each covered agency to name a Senior Real Property Officer to identify, track, and plan for the agency’s real property assets. It also creates a Federal Real Property Council and gives the General Services Administration a role in oversight, guidance, and a government-wide property database.

13328.s: This order creates a commission inside the Executive Office of the President to advise the President on intelligence capabilities related to weapons of mass destruction. The commission must study how well the Intelligence Community can find, assess, and warn about weapons of mass destruction threats, including foreign powers, terrorists, and related networks. It must also review intelligence on Iraq, Libya, and Afghanistan in the ways described in the order and report its findings and recommendations to the President.

13329.s: This order tells executive branch departments and agencies with Small Business Innovation Research or Small Business Technology Transfer programs to give high priority to manufacturing-related research and development, as allowed by law. It also requires those departments and agencies to report each year on their efforts to carry out that priority. The Small Business Administration must set the report format and schedule and may issue guidelines and directives to help carry out the order, with approval from the President.

13330.s: This order creates an interagency council in the Department of Transportation to improve transportation access for people who are transportation-disadvantaged. The council is meant to reduce duplicate federal programs and make transportation services more coordinated, cost-effective, and easier to use. It focuses on people with disabilities, low income, or advanced age, and on agencies that provide transportation-related programs or services.

13331.s: This order directs the Corporation for National and Community Service to review and update policies for national and community service programs. It says these programs should encourage more volunteering, respond to state and local needs, improve accountability, and expand involvement by faith-based and other community organizations. It also calls for management changes to strengthen oversight, budget controls, accounting, and performance standards.

13332.s: This order sets new basic pay rates and salary schedules for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Health Administration, Senior Executive Service, executive branch offices, Congress, judges, and the uniformed services. It also sets locality-based comparability payments and pay rates for administrative law judges. The Office of Personnel Management is directed to take needed steps to carry out the locality payments and publish notice in the Federal Register.

13333.s: This order changes an earlier order to carry out parts of the Trafficking Victims Protection Reauthorization Act of 2003. It directs the Senior Policy Operating Group and the Secretary of State to set guidelines, policies, and regulations on international trafficking in persons. It also assigns tasks on prevention, research, grants, and contracts to the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Homeland Security, and other executive branch agencies.

13334.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate and report on a labor dispute between the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority and its conductors represented by the United Transportation Union. The board must report to the President within 30 days after it is created. During the 120 days after the board is created, the parties may not change the conditions that led to the dispute unless they agree to do so.

13335.s: This order directs the Health and Human Services Secretary to create a National Health Information Technology Coordinator. It also tells the coordinator to help carry out a national plan for interoperable health information technology in the public and private health care sectors. The order calls for reports on ways to give incentives for using this technology in HHS programs, the Federal Employee Health Benefit Program, and some health systems used by Veterans Affairs and Defense.

13336.s: This order directs federal agencies to work together on American Indian and Alaska Native education. It creates an interagency working group, requires a study and report on student progress and proven methods, and calls for consultation with tribes, colleges, and universities. It also seeks ways to strengthen research at tribal-level educational institutions and to hold a forum on improving communication and cooperation for students in Federal, State, tribal, and local schools.

13337.s: This order changes how the government reviews and decides on Presidential permits for certain facilities at the United States borders. It covers facilities for exporting or importing petroleum, petroleum products, coal, other fuels, and certain border crossings for land transportation, including motor and rail vehicles. The Secretary of State receives the applications, consults other officials, and issues or denies the permit based on whether it serves the national interest.

13338.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of certain people linked to the Government of Syria. It also bars the export or reexport of many U.S. goods to Syria, with an exception for food and medicine in some cases. The order limits air service by air carriers owned or controlled by Syria and affects people and businesses that deal with the blocked persons or prohibited exports.

13339.s: This order creates a presidential advisory commission, a White House Initiative office, and an interagency working group in the Department of Commerce. They are meant to advise the President and help improve equal access to Federal programs, contracts, and partnerships for Asian American and Pacific Islander businesses. It also calls for collecting data and making plans to support their economic opportunities and business participation.

13340.s: This order creates the Great Lakes Interagency Task Force inside the Environmental Protection Agency for administrative purposes. The task force is meant to help federal agencies work with Great Lakes States, local communities, tribes, Canada, and other groups on policies, projects, and priorities for the Great Lakes system. It also tells the task force to develop outcome-based goals, coordinate federal research and government action, and report to the President.

13341.s: This order makes several conforming changes to Executive Order 11023 to reflect the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration Commissioned Officer Corps Act of 2002. It updates references to NOAA officer authorities on retirement, temporary appointments, and other personnel actions. It also adds a provision allowing commissioned officers to be transferred into NOAA with consent, under joint regulations.

13342.s: This order tells the Departments of Commerce and Veterans Affairs and the Small Business Administration to each set up a Center for Faith-Based and Community Initiatives. The centers are meant to reduce barriers and help faith-based and other community organizations take part in agency programs, services, contracts, and outreach. The agencies must also report on their efforts and name a liaison to work with the White House office on these initiatives.

13343.s: This order closed executive departments, independent establishments, and other government agencies on June 11, 2004. It said that day would be treated under laws on federal employee pay and leave. Some offices in the Departments of State, Defense, Justice, and Homeland Security, and others, could stay open if their heads decided it was needed for national security, defense, or other essential public business.

13344.s: This order changes the order of succession in the Environmental Protection Agency. It replaces three listed succession positions with the Assistant Administrator for Solid Waste, the Assistant Administrator for Toxic Substances, and the Assistant Administrator for Air and Radiation. It affects who would follow in line if EPA succession is needed.

13345.s: This order assigns certain presidential functions under the Agricultural Trade Development and Assistance Act and the Foreign Assistance Act to the Secretary of the Treasury and the Secretary of State. It also gives USAID a role in making recommendations and sets up the government representatives who will serve on the Enterprise for the Americas Board. The order says officials must consult with other agencies as needed and revokes four earlier executive orders.

13346.s: This order assigns certain presidential waiver, determination, certification, recommendation, and reporting functions to the Secretary of State, the United States Trade Representative, and the Secretary of Commerce. It also changes earlier executive orders to add more delegated duties. The order says it is for internal management of the executive branch and does not create a legal right or benefit for anyone.

13347.s: This order sets a federal policy to support safety and security for individuals with disabilities in disasters and other emergency situations. It directs federal agencies to consider the needs of employees and people they serve with disabilities in emergency planning, and to help state, local, tribal, and private groups do the same. It also creates an interagency council to coordinate this work and report to the President each year.

13348.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of certain listed persons and others linked to Charles Taylor or the former Liberian regime. It also prohibits direct or indirect importation into the United States of round logs or timber products from Liberia. It bars transactions that try to evade these limits and applies to U.S. persons and others in the United States.

13349.s: This order changes a previous order so the President’s Council of Advisors on Science and Technology will serve as the National Nanotechnology Advisory Panel. It applies to that council and the panel’s work under the 21st Century Nanotechnology Research and Development Act. It also says the panel does not have to follow any requirement that the law exempts it from.

13350.s: This order ends the national emergency that had been declared with respect to Iraq in Executive Order 12722. It also revokes several related executive orders and changes another order so the authorities now rest on the later Iraq emergency declarations. The order keeps some restrictions in place for blocked property, bars certain transfers of illegally removed Iraqi cultural and historical items, and prohibits certain donations to people subject to the sanctions.

13351.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate and report on a dispute between the Southeastern Pennsylvania Transportation Authority and its conductors represented by the United Transportation Union. The parties must submit final offers to the board within 30 days after it is created, and the board must then send the President a report choosing the most reasonable offer. The order also says the parties may not change the conditions that gave rise to the dispute unless they agree to do so.

13352.s: This order directs the Departments of the Interior, Agriculture, Commerce, and Defense, and the Environmental Protection Agency, to carry out environmental and natural resource laws in a way that promotes cooperative conservation. It says they should include local participation in federal decisionmaking, respect people’s legally recognized interests in land and other natural resources, and keep public health and safety in mind. It also calls for annual reports on the order’s implementation and for a White House Conference on Cooperative Conservation.

13353.s: This order creates the President's Board on Safeguarding Americans' Civil Liberties. The Board advises the President on how to protect the legal rights of Americans, including civil liberties and information privacy, while carrying out national security and homeland security work. It can review federal policies, request reports from agencies, and recommend changes, and federal departments and agencies must cooperate with it.

13354.s: This order creates the National Counterterrorism Center. The Center is made the main government office for analyzing and combining terrorism intelligence, planning counterterrorism activities, and keeping a shared knowledge base on known and suspected terrorists and international terror groups. Federal agencies must share terrorism information with the Center when allowed by law and help protect Americans' rights while doing so.

13355.s: This order strengthens the Director of Central Intelligence’s role in managing U.S. intelligence activities. It gives the Director more authority over intelligence guidance, information sharing, budgets, and standards for people working in the Intelligence Community. It also requires departments and agencies to give the Director access to relevant intelligence and support the Director’s work, subject to law and available funds.

13356.s: This order tells federal agencies to give top priority to sharing terrorism information and to protect Americans’ privacy and other legal rights while doing so. It directs agencies with terrorism information to share it quickly with other agencies that have counterterrorism duties, and to work with state and local authorities when allowed by law. It also creates an Information Systems Council to plan an interoperable system for sharing terrorism information among agencies.

13357.s: This order ends the national emergency that had been declared with respect to the policies and actions of the Government of Libya. It also revokes Executive Orders 12543, 12544, 12801, and 12538. The order says earlier actions, pending proceedings, and rights or duties that already matured are not affected.

13358.s: This order assigns certain presidential functions on appointments, promotions, and commissions in the Armed Forces to the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Homeland Security. It covers some actions for the Coast Guard when it is not operating as part of the Navy. The order also lets those secretaries reassign some of these functions to certain civilian officers in their departments, with some limits.

13359.s: This order changes how the Interagency Task Force on the Economic Development of the Central San Joaquin Valley is set up and run. It lists which federal officials serve on the task force, makes the Secretary of Housing and Urban Development the chair, and says federal departments and agencies should each name one staff person for 2004 through 2006 to work on task force issues. It also changes one task force duty to include analyzing regulations and says the order does not create any legal rights or benefits.

13360.s: This order tells federal agencies to improve opportunities for service-disabled veteran businesses in federal contracting and subcontracting. Agencies must develop plans, name a senior official, report on their progress, and include steps like reserving some contracts for these businesses, helping them compete, and encouraging subcontracting with them. It also gives duties to the Small Business Administration, General Services Administration, Defense Department, Veterans Affairs, and Labor to provide training, assistance, and related support.

13361.s: This order assigns certain functions under the United States Leadership Against HIV/AIDS, Tuberculosis, and Malaria Act of 2003 to the Secretary. It also says that, for section 304, the Secretary must act after consulting with the Secretary of Health and Human Services. The order is meant to improve the internal management of the executive branch and does not create any legal right or benefit.

13362.s: This order adds several Department of Homeland Security officers to the order of succession for Secretary of Homeland Security. If the Secretary, Deputy Secretary, and certain other designated officers cannot serve, the listed FEMA regional directors would perform the Secretary’s functions and duties in the order named, if they are eligible under federal law. It also says someone already serving in one of those offices in an acting capacity cannot act as Secretary under this order, and the President may depart from the order where allowed by law.

13363.s: This order establishes the Afghanistan Campaign Medal and the Iraq Campaign Medal. The medals may be awarded to members of the uniformed services who served in Afghanistan, Iraq, or nearby air space or waters during the time periods named in the order. It also says some members may choose one of these medals instead of the Global War on Terrorism Expeditionary Medal for the same service, and the medals may be awarded posthumously.

13364.s: This order limits some legal actions against the Development Fund for Iraq and certain Iraqi oil and oil-related property. It also protects property of the Central Bank of Iraq from attachment, judgment, or similar court process. The limits do not apply to final judgments from contractual obligations entered into by the Government of Iraq after June 30, 2004.

13365.s: This order amends the Manual for Courts-Martial and updates rules used in military justice cases. It changes rules on charging offenses, rehearings, trial delay, open or closed court sessions, mental responsibility, sentencing, and who may suspend or remit sentences. It also updates evidence rules on character evidence, expert testimony, business records, and certified records. These changes affect members of the armed forces involved in courts-martial.

13366.s: This order sets a U.S. policy to coordinate executive departments and agencies on ocean-related matters in an integrated way. It also calls for coordination and consultation among federal, state, tribal, local, private, foreign, and international groups on those matters. It creates a Committee on Ocean Policy to advise on ocean-related policies, share information, and help coordinate work on the ocean part of the Global Earth Observation System of Systems.

13367.s: This order designates the United States-Mexico Border Health Commission as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It gives members and employees of the Mexican section the same privileges, exemptions, and immunities for entry into and departure from the United States that the law gives to officers and employees of foreign governments in similar situations. It does not extend any other privileges, exemptions, or immunities under that Act.

13368.s: This order sets new rates of basic pay and salaries for several federal pay systems. It covers employees under the General Schedule, Foreign Service Schedule, Veterans Health Administration schedules, senior executives, certain executive, legislative, and judicial salaries, uniformed services pay, locality-based payments, and administrative law judges. The new rates take effect on the dates listed in the order, and it supersedes Executive Order 13332.

13369.s: This order creates the President’s Advisory Panel on Federal Tax Reform. The panel must give the Secretary of the Treasury a report with revenue-neutral policy options for changing the federal tax code. The options are meant to simplify tax laws, share the burdens and benefits of the tax system, and support economic growth and job creation. The Department of the Treasury must provide support, and other executive departments and agencies may be asked to help.

13370.s: This order sets the line of succession for the Office of Management and Budget if both the Director and Deputy Director die, resign, or cannot do the job. It lists several OMB officers who would perform the Director’s duties in the order named, if they are eligible under the Federal Vacancies Reform Act. It also says someone already serving in one of those jobs in an acting role cannot use that role to become acting Director under this order, and the President may depart from the order when allowed by law.

13371.s: This order changes the mission and duties of the President's Council on Service and Civic Participation. It tells the Council to promote volunteer service and civic participation, support volunteer organizations, share information about volunteer opportunities, and help promote federally administered volunteer programs. It also extends the order so it will expire on January 29, 2007 unless extended again.

13372.s: This order clarifies earlier executive orders that block property and prohibit certain transactions. It says donations of certain articles to, by, or for the benefit of people subject to those orders are prohibited. It also directs the Secretary of the Treasury and other U.S. agencies to take needed actions to carry out the order.

13373.s: This order changes the rules for the Vice Presidential Service Badge. It adds members of the commissioned corps of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration and the Public Health Service, and it covers certain people assigned to work mainly for the Vice President or in related military units and support facilities. It also says no award can be made for service that was already used to receive the Presidential Service Badge.

13374.s: This order changes the basic salary ranges for the Senior Foreign Service and keeps three salary classes: Career Minister, Minister-Counselor, and Counselor. It also changes one official reference in a prior order to say the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development. The order revokes Executive Order 13325.

13375.s: This executive order amends a prior order to add a new category of influenza: novel or reemergent influenza viruses that are causing, or could cause, a pandemic. It applies to the public health rules for certain influenza viruses and quarantinable communicable diseases.

13376.s: This order updates the rules for the President's Foreign Intelligence Advisory Board. It replaces the term "Director of Central Intelligence" with "Director of National Intelligence" once that director is appointed. It also says the order is only for internal management of the executive branch and does not create any legal right or benefit.

13377.s: This order designates the African Union as a public international organization that can receive privileges, exemptions, and immunities under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It also says this designation does not reduce any other privileges, exemptions, or immunities the African Union may already have or later get under law. The order revokes Executive Order 11767.

13378.s: This order updates the Defense Economic Adjustment Program. The program is meant to help communities, businesses, and workers affected by major Defense base closures, realignments, and contract-related adjustments. It also helps state and local governments prevent civilian encroachment that could interfere with military installations, and it changes the membership and leadership of the Economic Adjustment Committee.

13379.s: This order changes Executive Order 13369 to extend the reporting deadline for the President's Advisory Panel on Federal Tax Reform. It changes the deadline from July 31, 2005, to September 30, 2005.

13380.s: This order changes how the United States carries out earlier rules on the Border Environment Cooperation Commission and the North American Development Bank. It says the Secretaries of State and the Treasury, and the Administrator of the Environmental Protection Agency, are members of the Board of Directors, and that some board appointments are made by the President. It also names the Secretary of the Treasury as the Board chair when the United States selects the chair and gives that secretary a lead role in coordinating U.S. policy on matters before the Board.

13381.s: This order changes how agencies handle decisions about access to classified national security information. It directs the Office of Management and Budget to oversee or assign parts of that process, and it lets the Director issue guidance for agency heads, including on Sensitive Compartmented Information and special access programs. Agency heads must carry out assigned tasks, follow the guidance, and protect counterintelligence interests and intelligence sources and methods. The order also sets a report to the President and says it will expire unless extended.

13382.s: This order blocks property and property interests in the United States, or under the control of United States persons, for certain people and groups tied to weapons of mass destruction proliferation. It also blocks property of people who help, finance, supply, or act for those listed. United States persons and people in the United States may not transfer, pay, export, withdraw, or otherwise deal in blocked property.

13383.s: This order changes two earlier executive orders to use the title “Director of National Intelligence” instead of “Director of Central Intelligence” in certain places. It also changes one reference to the “Director of the Central Intelligence Agency” and adds a reference to the “Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence.”

13384.s: This order gives the Secretary of Defense the President’s functions for certain original appointments as commissioned officers and chief warrant officer appointments in the Armed Forces. The Secretary of Defense may not pass those functions to someone else. It does not limit the President’s authority to nominate, make, or end appointments.

13385.s: This order continues several federal advisory committees until September 30, 2007. It also changes some existing executive orders about those committees and their duties. The order revokes executive orders that created two committees that have ended or finished their work, and it revokes another executive order as well.

13386.s: This order changes the deadline for the President's Advisory Panel on Federal Tax Reform to submit its report to November 1, 2005. It also changes the deadline for section 7 to November 15, 2005. The order says it does not create any right or benefit that can be enforced against the United States or other persons.

13387.s: This order amends the Manual for Courts-Martial and changes several rules for military justice. It updates rules on who may convene courts-martial, how many members must be present in general and capital cases, and how sealed exhibits and proceedings are handled. It also changes some evidence and offense rules, including references to Homeland Security and rules on operating vehicles, aircraft, or vessels while drunk or impaired.

13388.s: This order directs federal agencies to give top priority to sharing terrorism information and to protect Americans from terrorist attacks. It requires agencies with terrorism information to give access to other agencies with counterterrorism duties and to work together on reports that can be shared more widely. It also sets up an Information Sharing Council to help create an interoperable terrorism information sharing system and revokes Executive Order 13356.

13389.s: This order creates the Gulf Coast Recovery and Rebuilding Council within the Executive Office of the President. The Council is set up to help with Federal support for recovery and rebuilding in the Gulf Coast region affected by Hurricane Katrina and Hurricane Rita. It may review issues, give advice and guidance, and make recommendations to the President. Agencies must help the Council as allowed by law, and the Council will end 3 years after the order unless the President extends it.

13390.s: This order creates a Coordinator of Federal Support for the Recovery and Rebuilding of the Gulf Coast Region in the Department of Homeland Security. The Coordinator is to work with federal departments and agencies to coordinate the federal response for the Gulf Coast region affected by Hurricane Katrina and Hurricane Rita. The Coordinator also serves as the main contact within the executive branch for Congress, state and local governments, the private sector, and community leaders on this response.

13391.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of certain persons linked to actions or policies that undermine Zimbabwe's democratic processes or institutions. It also covers people who helped them, their immediate family members, and people owned or controlled by them. The blocked property cannot be transferred, paid, exported, withdrawn, or otherwise dealt in, and U.S. persons and people in the United States may not make transactions that evade these rules.

13392.s: This order directs federal agencies to improve how they disclose information under the Freedom of Information Act. It requires each agency to name a senior Chief FOIA Officer, review its FOIA operations, and make a plan to reduce backlogs and improve public access to records and request status information. It also requires agencies to set up FOIA Requester Service Centers and FOIA Public Liaisons to help people with FOIA requests.

13393.s: This order sets new rates of basic pay and salaries for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Health Administration, Senior Executive Service, executive branch offices, Congress, judges, and administrative law judges. It also sets pay rates for members of the uniformed services and cadet or midshipman pay. Locality-based comparability payments are to be paid under the attached schedule, and the Office of Personnel Management must carry out those payments and publish notice of them. The order takes effect on the dates listed in the schedules and supersedes Executive Order 13368.

13394.s: This order sets the line of succession for the Secretary of Defense if the Secretary dies, resigns, or is otherwise unable to serve. It lists officers who would act as Secretary in a specific order, starting with the Deputy Secretary of Defense. It says no one serving in an acting capacity may act under this order, and the President may depart from it where allowed by law. It also revokes a 1996 executive order and a June 2, 2005 memorandum on the same subject.

13395.s: This order designates the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria as a public international organization. It gives the Global Fund the privileges, exemptions, and immunities provided by the International Organizations Immunities Act. It also says this designation does not reduce any privileges, exemptions, or immunities the Global Fund already has or may get by law.

13396.s: This order blocks property and property interests in the United States, or under the control of a United States person, for certain people connected to the conflict in Côte d'Ivoire. It also bars transactions, donations, and support that would help those listed or designated under the order. The order covers people named in the annex and others the Treasury Secretary determines fit the listed categories, including those tied to violence, arms transfers, or support for the conflict.

13397.s: This executive order tells the Department of Homeland Security to set up a Center for Faith-Based and Community Initiatives. The center must work to remove regulatory, contracting, and other barriers that affect faith-based and other community organizations that provide social and community services. It also must improve outreach, propose pilot programs, and report on its work and barriers found.

13398.s: This order creates the National Mathematics Advisory Panel in the Department of Education. The panel advises the President and the Secretary of Education on how to improve mathematics education, including the use of proven and evidence-based math instruction. It may gather advice from federal, state, local, territorial, and tribal officials, as well as experts, parents, and teachers.

13399.s: This order blocks property and interests in property in the United States for certain people tied to attacks in Lebanon, for people who blocked the work of the Commission, and for people who helped them. It also bars transactions that try to evade these limits or conspire to violate them. It affects United States persons, people and entities in the United States, and others whose property is covered by the order.

13400.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of certain people linked to the conflict in Sudan’s Darfur region. It applies to people listed in the order and to others the Treasury Secretary identifies after consulting the Secretary of State, including people tied to threats, violence, arms support, or military overflights. It also bars attempts to evade the order and directs U.S. agencies to help carry it out.

13401.s: This order tells each federal agency to name a liaison for volunteer community service. The liaison must support volunteer service among federal employees, including those approaching retirement, and help recognize volunteer work. Agencies must also review their programs and policies related to volunteer community service and report on their activities to the USA Freedom Corps.

13402.s: This order sets a federal policy to use government resources to deter, prevent, detect, investigate, and prosecute identity theft. It creates an Identity Theft Task Force made up of several federal officials to coordinate federal work on identity theft awareness, prevention, detection, and prosecution. The task force must also work with state, local, tribal, and private sector representatives and may make recommendations to the President and federal agencies.

13403.s: This order changes parts of five earlier executive orders. It updates some wording and deadlines, changes which officials are named in one order, and removes one subsection from another. It also revokes Executive Order 13011 on Federal Information Technology.

13404.s: This order tells the Secretary of Homeland Security to create a Task Force on New Americans within the Department of Homeland Security. The task force is to help legal immigrants integrate into American society through English, civics, and history instruction, and by encouraging public-private partnerships and volunteer service. It also may make recommendations on agency cooperation, rule changes, policy changes, and proposed legislation about the integration of legal immigrants.

13405.s: This order blocks property and interests in property in the United States, or under the control of U.S. persons, for certain people tied to actions that undermine democratic processes or institutions in Belarus. It also covers people involved in human rights abuses related to political repression, public corruption, or support for those activities, as well as people owned or controlled by them. The order bars transfers, payments, exports, withdrawals, and other dealings with that property, and it prohibits efforts to evade these restrictions.

13406.s: This order says the United States should protect Americans' rights to private property and limit federal takings to public use with just compensation. It directs the Attorney General to issue instructions to agencies and monitor takings for compliance. It also says the order does not stop certain kinds of takings, including for public facilities, utilities, emergencies, abandoned property, and law enforcement or military needs.

13407.s: This order directs the federal government to maintain an effective, reliable, and integrated public alert and warning system for war, terrorist attacks, natural disasters, and other public safety hazards. It requires the Secretary of Homeland Security to review alerting resources, set common standards and procedures, support training and public education, and help ensure the President can warn the American people under all conditions. It also directs other agencies, including the Department of Commerce, the Department of Defense, and the Federal Communications Commission, to help carry out the system.

13408.s: This order extends Executive Order 13381 for one more year. It changes one deadline from April 1, 2006 to April 1, 2007, and another from July 1, 2006 to July 1, 2007. It affects the parts of Executive Order 13381 covered by those dates.

13409.s: This order sets up a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between SEPTA and employees represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen. The board must report to the President within 30 days of being created. For 120 days after the board is created, the parties may not change the conditions involved in the dispute unless they agree to do so.

13410.s: This order directs federal agencies that run or sponsor health care programs to use health information technology that meets recognized interoperability standards when they buy or upgrade systems. It also tells agencies to measure and share information about health care quality and prices for people in those programs, and in some cases with the public. Agencies must also develop ways to encourage high-quality, efficient care for beneficiaries, enrollees, and providers.

13411.s: This order creates a task force to improve how federal disaster assistance is delivered. It applies to people who are victims of a terrorist attack, natural disaster, or other incident covered by a Stafford Act emergency or major disaster declaration. The task force must look at federal disaster programs, recommend a centralized application process and information clearinghouse, and reduce duplicate forms and fraud. Federal departments and agencies must help the Secretary of Homeland Security carry out the order.

13412.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of the Government of Sudan that are in the United States or under the control of United States persons. It also prohibits United States persons from transactions related to the petroleum or petrochemical industries in Sudan, including oilfield services and oil or gas pipelines. The order does not prohibit official business for the Federal Government or the United Nations, or journalistic activity in Sudan.

13413.s: This order blocks property and property interests of certain people tied to the conflict in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It applies to people listed in the order and to others the Secretary of the Treasury designates for reasons like leading armed groups, recruiting child soldiers, committing serious violations involving children, supplying arms, or supporting those activities. It also bars transactions meant to evade the order and directs U.S. agencies to help carry it out.

13414.s: This order changes Executive Order 13402 by moving the deadline for the Identity Theft Task Force to submit its coordinated strategic plan to the President. The plan is to review executive branch activities and help improve federal efforts on identity theft awareness, prevention, detection, and prosecution.

13415.s: This order assigns certain pay-related functions under three sections of title 5, United States Code, to the Director of the Office of Personnel Management. It also revokes parts of two earlier executive orders and renumbers other sections in those orders. The order says it does not create any new right or benefit that can be enforced against the United States or other persons.

13416.s: This order directs the Department of Homeland Security to strengthen security for surface transportation systems. It covers mass transit, passenger rail, freight rail, commercial vehicles, intercity buses, pipelines, roads, and highways within the United States. The order requires the Secretary to assess security, develop a plan, identify high-risk modes or components, and work on security guidelines, requirements, and technology lists with other governments and the private sector.

13417.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate and report on disputes between Metro-North Railroad and certain employees represented by labor organizations. The board must report to the President within 30 days of its creation. From the day the board is created and for 120 days after, the parties may not change the conditions that led to the disputes unless they agree to do so.

13418.s: This order amends a previous executive order about Volunteers for Prosperity. It adds controlling malaria as an objective of the global prosperity agenda and changes the list of related goals to include the President's Malaria Initiative. It also keeps the goal of stemming the spread of HIV/AIDS.

13419.s: This order sets a U.S. policy to support progress in aeronautics research and development through federal funding and activities, working with state, local, tribal, foreign, academic, private, and other organizations as appropriate. It directs the Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy to review federal aeronautics R&D, recommend actions, and develop a national plan for aeronautics R&D and related infrastructure. It also tells federal departments and agencies involved in aeronautics R&D to improve coordination, share information, and help move research into use.

13420.s: This order sets new basic pay rates and salary schedules for federal workers in the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Health Administration, Senior Executive Service, executive, legislative, and judicial offices, uniformed services, and administrative law judges. It also provides for locality-based comparability payments and directs the Office of Personnel Management to help carry them out. Some of the new rates take effect on different dates in early 2007, and it supersedes Executive Order 13393.

13421.s: This order closes most executive departments, independent establishments, and other government agencies on January 2, 2007. It says the closure is a mark of respect for Gerald R. Ford and treats that day as covered by federal pay and leave rules. Some offices may stay open if their department heads decide they must remain open for national security, defense, or other essential public business.

13422.s: This order changes how federal agencies plan and review regulations and guidance documents. It requires agencies to identify the specific problem a new action is meant to address and adds rules for "significant guidance documents," including advance notice to OIRA and possible extra consultation. It also changes agency planning steps, including naming a Regulatory Policy Officer and giving more information about planned rules and their costs and benefits.

13423.s: This order directs federal agencies to improve energy efficiency, cut greenhouse gas emissions, and use water, energy, and transportation resources in a more sustainable way. It sets goals for agencies to buy more renewable energy, reduce water and petroleum use, and purchase more environmentally preferable products and paper with recycled fiber. It also requires agencies to manage waste, follow sustainable building rules, and use approved electronic products and fleet vehicles when available.

13424.s: This order extends the President's Council on Service and Civic Participation by changing the expiration date in a prior executive order. It says the order will expire on November 30, 2008, unless the President extends it again.

13425.s: This order establishes military commissions to try alien unlawful enemy combatants for offenses that can be tried by military commission. It says an “alien” is a person who is not a citizen of the United States. It also replaces parts of a prior presidential military order that dealt with trial by military commission.

13426.s: This order creates a commission to review the care given to returning wounded service members from the Global War on Terror and to recommend improvements. It also creates an interagency task force to review federal services for these service members, find gaps, and make an action plan to improve coordination and delivery of services. The measure affects returning Global War on Terror service members and the federal agencies that provide their care and benefits.

13427.s: This order extends privileges and immunities to the Permanent Observer Mission of the Holy See to the United Nations in New York and to its members. It gives them the same privileges and immunities that diplomatic missions of UN member states and their members enjoy, subject to the same conditions and obligations. It also says this does not reduce any other privileges or immunities they may already have or later get by law.

13428.s: This order renames the Caribbean National Forest in the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico as the El Yunque National Forest. It also says that previous references to the Caribbean National Forest in two earlier executive orders should now be treated as references to the El Yunque National Forest. It states that the order must follow applicable law and available funding.

13429.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between Metro-North Railroad and its maintenance of way employees represented by the International Brotherhood of Teamsters. The board must receive final settlement offers from the parties, then report to the President with its choice of the most reasonable offer. While the board is active, the parties may not change the conditions that led to the dispute unless they agree to do so.

13430.s: This order changes the Manual for Courts-Martial to allow some testimony and court sessions to use remote audiovisual technology, with rules for the accused, defense counsel, and military judge. It also adds rules for remote live testimony and remote means of testimony in military trials. The order adds a new offense for causing the death of or bodily injury to an unborn child during certain crimes against a pregnant woman, and it updates rules on operating vehicles, aircraft, or vessels while drunk or above the listed alcohol limits.

13431.s: This order creates a temporary office in the Department of State called the Iraq Transition Assistance Office. The office is set up to support U.S. government assistance in Iraq, help finish remaining large infrastructure projects, and assist Iraq's move to self-sufficiency. It also takes over certain functions, personnel, assets, liabilities, and records from the Iraq Reconstruction Management Office.

13432.s: This order tells the Department of Transportation, the Department of Energy, and the Environmental Protection Agency to work together on actions that affect greenhouse gas emissions from motor vehicles, nonroad vehicles, and nonroad engines. It says agencies should coordinate their regulatory actions, share research and information, and avoid duplicate requests for information from the public. It also asks them to consult with the Secretary of Agriculture when a regulatory action would significantly affect agriculture related to ethanol, biodiesel, or other renewable fuels.

13433.s: This order tells federal agencies to pay for legal and expert witness services in amounts that are reasonable and not tied to the outcome of a case, unless the law requires otherwise. It bars agencies from entering new contingency fee agreements for those services unless the Attorney General says the law requires it. Agencies must also report existing contingency fee agreements to the Attorney General and the Director of the Office of Management and Budget.

13434.s: This order says the United States will promote education, training, and experience for current and future security professionals in executive departments and agencies. It calls for a national strategy, an executive steering committee, and agency rules and guidance to carry out the plan. It also directs the Department of Homeland Security to develop training for Federal, State, local, and tribal officials in disaster preparedness, response, recovery, and crisis decision-making.

13435.s: This order directs the Department of Health and Human Services, including the National Institutes of Health, to conduct and support research on pluripotent stem cells from alternative sources. The research must not create a human embryo for research or destroy, discard, or harm a human embryo or fetus. It also requires a plan to rename the "Human Embryonic Stem Cell Registry" the "Human Pluripotent Stem Cell Registry" and to add new stem cell lines that meet the order's standard.

13436.s: This order extends Executive Order 13381 for one more year. It changes the dates in that order from April 1, 2007 and July 1, 2007 to April 1, 2008 and July 1, 2008.

13437.s: This order waives the application of two parts of section 402 of the Trade Act of 1974 for Turkmenistan. It affects the treatment of Turkmenistan under that law. The order says the President made a report to Congress before issuing the waiver.

13438.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of certain persons in the United States or under the control of United States persons. It applies to people the Secretary of the Treasury, with the Secretaries of State and Defense, determines have committed or may commit violence that threatens the peace or stability of Iraq, or who helped such acts or are owned or controlled by such persons. It also bars transactions that evade these rules and prohibits conspiracies to violate them.

13439.s: This order creates an Interagency Working Group on Import Safety within the Department of Health and Human Services. The group includes several cabinet officials and other federal officials, and the Secretary of Health and Human Services serves as chair. It is directed to review steps to promote the safety of imported products, including practices by importers, foreign manufacturers, and government agencies, and to give recommendations to the President.

13440.s: This order says Common Article 3 of the Geneva Conventions applies to a Central Intelligence Agency detention and interrogation program. It says a program approved by the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency complies if it does not use torture, other banned abuse, or acts that denigrate religion, and if detainees get basic necessities. It applies to alien detainees the Director finds are connected to al Qaeda, the Taliban, or associated organizations and are likely to have information about terrorist attacks or senior leaders.

13441.s: This order blocks property and property interests in the United States of certain people linked to undermining Lebanon’s democratic processes, rule of law, or sovereignty. It also covers people who help, finance, or act for those persons, as well as their spouses, dependent children, or controlled entities. It bars transactions meant to evade these restrictions and lets the Treasury Department carry them out.

13442.s: This order changes who will serve as acting Secretary of Homeland Security if the Secretary dies, resigns, or cannot do the job. It lists the officers who would follow in order and says people already serving in one of those jobs in an acting role cannot act as Secretary under this section. It also revokes a 2004 order about the Department of Homeland Security order of succession.

13443.s: This order tells federal agencies to help expand and improve hunting opportunities and manage game species and their habitat on public lands. It directs agencies to consider hunting trends, the economic and recreational value of hunting, and state and tribal wildlife plans in their actions. It also calls for a White House conference on North American wildlife policy and a long-term hunting and wildlife conservation plan.

13444.s: This order extends privileges and immunities to the African Union Mission to the United States and its members. It gives them the same privileges and immunities enjoyed by diplomatic missions accredited to the United States, subject to the same conditions and obligations. It also says this does not take away any other privileges or immunities they may already have or later get by law.

13445.s: This order sets a policy to use existing federal programs that serve adults, including new Americans, to strengthen literacy skills and improve opportunities for postsecondary education and employment. It creates an Interagency Adult Education Working Group in the Department of Education. The group must identify adult education programs, review them, recommend ways to improve them, find research gaps, and report to the President.

13446.s: This order continues 16 federal advisory committees until September 30, 2009. It also gives the head of the named department or agency the President’s Federal Advisory Committee Act functions for those committees. The order revokes an executive order that created the President’s Advisory Panel on Federal Tax Reform, and it amends the President’s Committee for People with Intellectual Disabilities.

13447.s: This order changes parts of the Manual for Courts-Martial, United States, by striking one sentence from Part I and making other changes to Parts II, III, and IV. It affects military justice proceedings under the manual, and the changes take effect on October 1, 2007, without making earlier conduct punishable or canceling cases already started before that date.

13448.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of certain people connected to Burma that are in the United States or under control of United States persons. It also covers people listed in the annex and people the Treasury Secretary, after consulting the Secretary of State, determines are senior Burma officials, involved in human rights abuses, public corruption, or support for the Burma government or related entities. United States persons and people in the United States are prohibited from transactions that evade these restrictions, from trying to violate them, and from making certain donations to blocked persons.

13449.s: This order sets a policy for the United States to conserve striped bass and red drum for recreational, economic, and environmental benefit. It directs the Secretary of Commerce to encourage management under federal, state, territorial, tribal, and local laws that support that policy.
