It also directs the Secretary to revise regulations to prohibit the sale of striped bass and red drum caught in the U.S. Exclusive Economic Zone off the Atlantic Ocean and Gulf of Mexico, while allowing fish produced by aquaculture.

13450.s: This order directs federal agencies to set clear yearly and long-term goals for each program they run, along with specific plans to meet those goals. It also requires agencies to measure progress, track how efficiently they use resources, and keep public websites updated with information on program performance, including successes, shortfalls, and challenges. The Office of Management and Budget must issue guidance and create a council to help improve and monitor federal program performance.

13451.s: This order designates the ITER International Fusion Energy Organization as a public international organization. That gives it the privileges, exemptions, and immunities provided by the International Organizations Immunities Act. It also says this designation does not reduce any other privileges, exemptions, or immunities the organization may already have or may get by law.

13452.s: This order creates a five-member emergency board to investigate disputes between Amtrak and certain employees represented by listed labor organizations. The board must report to the President within 30 days. From the board’s creation until 30 days after its report, the parties may not change the conditions involved in the disputes unless they agree.

13453.s: The order closes all executive branch departments and agencies of the federal government on Monday, December 24, 2007, and excuses their employees from duty. Department and agency heads may keep some offices open and require certain employees to work for national security, defense, or other public need. It also says that day counts under rules about federal employee pay and leave.

13454.s: This order sets new rates of basic pay and salaries for several federal pay systems. It covers employees under the General Schedule, Foreign Service Schedule, Veterans Health Administration schedules, the Senior Executive Service, certain executive, legislative, and judicial salaries, members of the uniformed services, locality-based comparability payments, and administrative law judges. It also says the Office of Personnel Management must take steps to implement the locality-based payments and publish notice of them in the Federal Register.

13455.s: This order creates the President's Advisory Council on Financial Literacy within the Department of the Treasury. The Council is made up of 19 members appointed by the President from outside the Federal Government, and it is meant to advise the President and the Secretary of the Treasury on ways to improve financial education, access to financial services, and measures of financial literacy. It also must report on the status of financial literacy in the United States and on progress in carrying out this policy.

13456.s: This order updates rules for foreign investment in the United States. It keeps the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States and gives the Secretary of the Treasury key duties for reviews, investigations, and regulations. It also lets the Committee and lead agencies use mitigation agreements or conditions to address national security risks in transactions. The order also assigns the Secretary of Commerce duties to gather and analyze information on foreign investment.

13457.s: This order says federal agencies should reduce the number and cost of earmarks and make their origin and purpose clear. It directs agencies not to spend funds based on earmarks in non-statutory sources, unless required by law or found to meet statutory or merit-based criteria. It also requires written congressional communications about earmarks to be made public on the Internet in most cases.

13458.s: This order directs several federal agencies to issue and enforce rules needed to carry out the Act and the United States obligations under the Additional Protocol. It authorizes the Secretary of Commerce, with help from the Attorney General if needed, to get and execute warrants for complementary access to certain locations. It also authorizes other agencies to carry out needed functions and says the Secretary of State must provide notifications or information to Congress when required by the Act.

13459.s: This order tells the Federal Government to improve coordination of youth programs and focus on better results for at-risk youth. It sets up an Interagency Working Group on Youth Programs to work with federal, state, and local organizations, including faith-based and other community groups. The group must help build a new federal youth website, encourage stronger program evaluations, and report its work to the President each year.

13460.s: This order blocks property and property interests in the United States, or controlled by U.S. persons, of certain people linked to public corruption by senior officials in the Government of Syria. It also bars transactions, donations, and other dealings that try to evade these restrictions. The Secretary of the Treasury, after consulting the Secretary of State, may issue rules to carry out the order, and federal agencies must take appropriate steps to follow it.

13461.s: This order sets the line of succession for who will act as Secretary of Health and Human Services if the Secretary dies, resigns, or cannot do the job. It lists the officers who would serve in order, starting with the Deputy Secretary and then several other department officials. It also says someone already serving in one of those jobs in an acting role cannot act as Secretary under this order, and it revokes a previous succession order and memorandum.

13462.s: This order sets up the President’s Intelligence Advisory Board in the Executive Office of the President to advise and assist the President on intelligence matters. It also creates an Intelligence Oversight Board to review intelligence activities, report possible unlawful or improper activities, and make recommendations. The order applies to the intelligence community and to departments concerned, and it revokes Executive Order 12863.

13463.s: This order changes Executive Order 13389 by replacing “Economic Policy” with “Homeland Security and Counterterrorism” in one section. It also changes the end date in Executive Orders 13389 and 13390 to February 28, 2009. The changes affect the parts of those orders that use those terms and deadlines.

13464.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of certain persons related to Burma that are in the United States or under the control of U.S. persons. It also prohibits transactions that evade these bans and bars donations to blocked persons. The Secretary of the Treasury, after consulting the Secretary of State, may make determinations about who is covered and take action to carry out the order.

13465.s: This order changes federal procurement rules to require certain contractors to use an electronic employment eligibility verification system. It applies to contractors and workers hired or assigned to work in the United States on federal contracts. It also says agencies may not contract with employers that do not use the best available means to confirm work authorization, and it keeps antidiscrimination obligations in place.

13466.s: This order declares a national emergency over the risk of weapons-usable fissile material on the Korean Peninsula. It keeps certain blocked property of North Korea and North Korean nationals frozen, so it may not be transferred, paid, exported, withdrawn, or otherwise dealt in. It also bars United States persons from registering, owning, leasing, operating, or insuring vessels flagged by North Korea.

13467.s: This order sets up a more aligned system for deciding suitability for government employment, fitness for contractor employees, and eligibility for access to classified information. It says background investigations and adjudications should use consistent standards, be accepted across agencies, and be shared more quickly when possible. It also creates a council and names executive agents to oversee these processes for executive branch agencies and, in some cases, employees in the legislative or judicial branches when the executive branch conducts the investigations.

13468.s:
This order amends Parts II and IV of the Manual for Courts-Martial, United States. It takes effect 30 days after the date of the order.

It does not make punishable any act done or left undone before the effective date if it was not punishable then. It also does not invalidate nonjudicial punishment proceedings, restraint, investigations, referral of charges, trials where arraignment has already happened, or other actions already begun before that date.

13469.s: This order expands a national emergency related to Zimbabwe. It blocks property and property interests in the United States, or under the control of U.S. persons, of certain people tied to the Government of Zimbabwe, including senior officials, people who undermine democratic processes, those involved in human rights abuses or public corruption, and some family members or helpers. It also bars transactions and donations that try to evade these restrictions.

13470.s: This order amends Executive Order 12333 on United States intelligence activities. It sets goals for the intelligence effort, including giving the President and security councils information for decisions and protecting the legal rights, civil liberties, and privacy rights of United States persons. It also sets duties for the National Security Council and gives the Director of National Intelligence broad duties over intelligence collection, sharing, classification, and covert action oversight.

13471.s:
This order changes the President's Council on Service and Civic Participation. It increases the council's membership and extends how long the council will last.
It also says the council must have at least 10 members present to conduct and vote on official business. Unless the President extends it again, the order will expire on June 30, 2009.

13472.s: This order tells executive branch agencies to make sure they have an order of succession so the agency can keep doing its essential work if the agency head dies, resigns, or cannot serve. Agencies that need presidential action must draft or update a proposed order and send it for review. Agencies that do not need presidential action must maintain their orders under the law and send copies of them to certain White House and budget officials.

13473.s: This order directs agencies to speed up hiring spouses of certain members of the Armed Forces for federal civil service jobs. It covers spouses of members on active duty with a permanent change of station move, spouses of totally disabled retired or separated members, and unremarried widows or widowers of members killed on active duty.

13474.s: This order amends an earlier executive order on recreational fishing and adds several federal laws to its list of related statutes. It also says recreational fishing should be managed as a sustainable activity in national wildlife refuges, national parks, national monuments, national marine sanctuaries, marine protected areas, and other relevant federal conservation or management areas. The order says it does not create any legal right or benefit that can be enforced against the United States or its agencies.

13475.s: This executive order amends two earlier executive orders to update who may be named in certain positions related to the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act. It adds the Deputy Director of the Federal Bureau of Investigation to those lists and says that person does not need Senate confirmation for that role. It also says the order does not create any new legal rights or benefits.

13476.s: This order sets up a Presidential Transition Coordinating Council to help with the change between administrations. The Council is to help the major party candidates and the President-elect by sharing information, coordinating orientation, and preparing briefing materials and a Transition Directory. It also allows transition agreements to be made with White House offices and executive departments and agencies.

13477.s: This order settles claims covered by the claims settlement agreement between the United States and Libya. It bars United States nationals and foreign nationals from bringing or keeping certain claims in courts, and it ends pending suits covered by the agreement. The Secretary of State must set procedures for United States nationals to seek compensation for those claims.

13478.s: This order changes rules for how federal agencies use Social Security numbers and other personal identifiers. It says agencies should handle these identifiers in a way that protects them against unlawful use. It also updates Executive Order 9397, changes some agency names and wording, and says the order does not create any new legal right or benefit.

13479.s: This order directs the government to maintain a national air transportation system that meets civil aviation, homeland security, economic, environmental protection, and national defense needs. It tells the Secretary of Transportation to work on implementing the Next Generation Air Transportation System, or NextGen, and to set up support staff and an advisory committee. It also assigns related duties to the Secretaries of Defense, Commerce, and Homeland Security, along with other agencies.

13480.s: This order excludes certain subdivisions in the Departments of Energy, Homeland Security, Justice, Transportation, and the Treasury from the Federal Labor-Management Relations Program. It says these offices have a primary function in intelligence, counterintelligence, investigative, or national security work, and that chapter 71 of title 5 cannot be applied to them consistently with national security requirements. The order lists the specific offices and subdivisions covered in each department.

13481.s: This order sets the line of succession for who may act as Attorney General if the Attorney General and certain other Justice Department officers have died, resigned, or cannot do the job. It lists three United States Attorneys, in order, to serve in that role. It also says some people in acting roles cannot use this order to become Attorney General, and the President may depart from the order if allowed by law.

13482.s: This order closes all executive branch departments and agencies of the federal government on Friday, December 26, 2008, and excuses their employees from duty. Agency heads may keep some offices open and require some employees to work for national security, defense, or other public need. It also says that day counts under certain pay and leave rules for federal employees.

13483.s: This order sets new rates of basic pay or salaries for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Health Administration, Senior Executive Service, and certain executive, legislative, judicial, and uniformed service pay. It also sets locality-based comparability payments and pay for administrative law judges. The new pay schedules apply to the affected federal employees and officials on the effective dates listed in the order.

13484.s: This order changes the line of succession for the Secretary of Agriculture. It lists which Department of Agriculture officials may serve in that role if needed, in a set order. It also says no one on the list may act as Secretary unless they are otherwise eligible under the Federal Vacancies Reform Act of 1998.

13485.s: This order sets the line of succession for the Secretary of Transportation if the Secretary, Deputy Secretary, Under Secretary for Policy, and certain other designated officials have died, resigned, or cannot serve. It lists officials who would act as Secretary in a set order, including several agency administrators and regional officials. It also says some people in acting roles cannot use this succession, and the President may depart from the order if allowed by law.

13486.s: This order says facilities that have biological select agents and toxins should use proper security and personnel checks to protect against theft, misuse, or diversion to unlawful activity. It creates a working group to review security rules and practices for federal and nonfederal facilities that research, manage, handle, store, or transport those agents and toxins. The group must report to the President with findings, recommendations, and options for oversight.

13487.s: This order creates a temporary office in the Department of State called the Afghanistan Support Office. The office is meant to support U.S. government work in Afghanistan, including helping prevent Afghanistan from becoming a safe haven for terrorists, helping Afghanistan move toward self-sufficiency, and keeping a diplomatic presence there. It also supports building civilian capabilities of the Government of Afghanistan, including central services, the private sector economy, and governance of its territory and borders.

13488.s: This order tells agencies to give credit, when possible, to prior favorable fitness or suitability decisions for people who work in the excepted service or as contractor employees. It also says people in positions of public trust must be reinvestigated to make sure they are still suitable for continued employment. The order affects federal agencies and people applying for or working in these jobs.

13489.s: This order sets policies and procedures for when the National Archives and Records Administration may release presidential records and how executive privilege claims are handled. It requires notice to the current and former Presidents before disclosure and gives them time to claim privilege or ask for more time. It also says the Archivist must follow these rules when dealing with claims by a current or former President. It revokes Executive Order 13233.

13490.s: This order requires certain executive branch appointees to sign an ethics pledge when they enter government service. The pledge bars them from taking gifts from registered lobbyists, limits some work on matters tied to former employers or clients, and restricts some lobbying after they leave government. It also says hiring decisions must be based on qualifications, competence, and experience, and it sets rules for waivers, agency procedures, and enforcement.

13491.s: This order revokes a prior executive order and sets rules for interrogations of people held by the United States in armed conflicts. It says they must be treated humanely and may not be subjected to interrogation methods or related treatment not authorized by Army Field Manual 2-22.3. It also orders the CIA to close any detention facilities it operates and bars the CIA from operating such facilities in the future. The order creates a task force to review interrogation and transfer policies and requires federal departments and agencies to give the International Committee of the Red Cross notification of, and timely access to, detained individuals.

13492.s: This order directs a review of people held at the Guantanamo Bay Naval Base and says the detention facilities there should be closed as soon as practicable, no later than 1 year from the date of the order. It also directs officials to determine whether each detainee should be transferred, released, prosecuted, or handled another lawful way. While the review is underway, no new military commission charges may be sworn or referred, and pending military commission proceedings are to be halted. It also requires humane conditions of confinement and directs the Secretary of State to pursue diplomatic efforts needed to carry out the order.

13493.s: This order creates a Special Task Force to review lawful options for the detention, trial, transfer, release, or other disposition of people captured or apprehended in connection with armed conflicts and counterterrorism operations. The task force includes the Attorney General, Secretary of Defense, Secretary of State, Secretary of Homeland Security, the Director of National Intelligence, the Director of the Central Intelligence Agency, and the Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff. It must report to the President on its work and end after it completes its duties.

13494.s: This order says certain costs are unallowable on federal contracts if they are not directly related to providing goods and services to the government. It also says contractors cannot bill the government for costs of trying to persuade employees about whether to organize and bargain collectively. Costs for maintaining good relations between contractors and employees, such as labor-management committees and employee publications, are still allowed.

13495.s: This order requires certain federal service contracts to include a clause giving qualified employees from the predecessor contract a right of first refusal for jobs on the successor contract. It applies to service contracts for the same or similar services at the same location, with some exclusions and possible exemptions by agency heads. The Secretary of Labor is responsible for enforcing it, and the order revokes Executive Order 13204.

13496.s: This order requires many federal contractors to post a notice about employee rights under federal labor laws at their worksites. It also requires contractors to follow that notice and to pass the same requirements down to covered subcontracts. If a contractor does not comply, its contract may be cancelled, terminated, or suspended, and it may be found ineligible for future government contracts. The Secretary of Labor is in charge of enforcing the order and may grant exemptions in some cases.

13497.s: This order revokes two earlier executive orders about regulatory planning and review. It directs the Director of the Office of Management and Budget and the heads of executive departments and agencies to promptly rescind any orders, rules, regulations, guidelines, or policies that carried out or enforced those revoked orders, as allowed by law. It also says the order does not create any new legal right or benefit for anyone.

13498.s: This order changes the White House office name to the White House Office of Faith-Based and Neighborhood Partnerships and sets new policy goals for working with faith-based and other neighborhood organizations. It says the federal government should help these groups deliver services, keep federally funded services in line with constitutional rules, and improve training, evaluation, and research. It also creates a President's Advisory Council to study these issues and make recommendations to the President.

13499.s: This order changes the membership list for the National Economic Council. It adds the Secretary of Health and Human Services, the Secretary of Education, the Senior Advisor and Assistant to the President for Intergovernmental Affairs and Public Liaison, the Assistant to the President for Energy and Climate Change, the Assistant to the President and Chief Technology Officer, and the Administrator of the Small Business Administration. It also renumbers the later subsections in that section.

13500.s: This order changes Executive Order 12859 by revising the list of White House officials in section 2. It replaces some existing titles with new ones, including the Senior Advisor and Assistant to the President for Intergovernmental Affairs and Public Liaison, the Assistant to the President for Energy and Climate Change, and the Assistant to the President and Chief Technology Officer. It also adds the Chief Executive Officer of the Corporation for National and Community Service and the Director of the Office of Science and Technology Policy.

13501.s: This order creates the President's Economic Recovery Advisory Board within the Department of the Treasury. The board gives the President independent, nonpartisan information, analysis, and advice on economic recovery, the economy, and the financial and banking system. It is advisory only, and its members serve without compensation. The board will end 2 years after the order unless the President extends it.

13502.s: This executive order directs executive agencies to consider requiring project labor agreements on large-scale Federal construction projects. A large-scale project is one with a total Federal cost of $25 million or more. It says such agreements may be required when they would help with economy, efficiency, labor-management stability, and compliance with labor, safety, and equal employment laws. It does not require agencies to use project labor agreements on every project, and it does not require contractors to enter into an agreement with any particular labor organization.

13503.s: This order creates the White House Office of Urban Affairs within the Executive Office of the President. The office is meant to lead and coordinate federal urban policy, including how executive departments and agencies consider the impact of their actions on urban areas. It also works with state and local officials, nonprofit organizations, and the private sector, and it coordinates with several federal departments and agencies.

13504.s: This order changes Executive Order 13390 to extend the work of the Coordinator of Federal Support for the Recovery and Rebuilding of the Gulf Coast Region. It replaces the date "February 28, 2009" with "September 30, 2009."

13505.s: This order removes limits on federal funding for research involving human embryonic stem cells and other human stem cell research. It allows the Secretary of Health and Human Services, through NIH, to support and conduct responsible, scientifically worthy research to the extent allowed by law. It also directs NIH to review its guidance and issue new guidance with appropriate safeguards. It makes the 2001 policy limiting federal funding have no further effect and revokes Executive Order 13435.

13506.s: This order creates a White House Council on Women and Girls within the Executive Office of the President. The council is made up of cabinet and other senior federal officials and is led by a chair. It is meant to coordinate a federal response to issues that affect women and girls, including women of color and women with disabilities, and to make recommendations to the President on laws, policies, and federal programs.

13507.s: This order creates a White House Office of Health Reform within the Executive Office of the President. It also directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish a similar office in HHS that works closely with the White House office. The office is meant to help coordinate federal efforts on health care access, quality, cost growth, and the health care system's sustainability.

13508.s: This order directs federal agencies to protect and restore the Chesapeake Bay and its watershed. It creates a Federal Leadership Committee to coordinate plans, reports, and public progress updates, and it requires annual action plans starting in 2010. The order also tells agencies to work on water quality, agricultural pollution, storm water, habitat, climate change research, and public access to the Bay from federal lands.

13509.s: This order creates a White House Council on Automotive Communities and Workers. The Council is meant to coordinate federal policies and programs for automotive communities and workers, advise the President, and make recommendations on changes to federal policies and programs. It also directs federal departments and agencies to help the Council and to consider requests from automotive communities for technical assistance, financial resources, surplus property, or other resources.

13510.s: This order waives the application of subsections (a) and (b) of section 402 of the Trade Act of 1974 with respect to the Republic of Belarus. It affects the rules in that law as they apply to Belarus.

13511.s: This order keeps several federal advisory committees in place until September 30, 2011. It also says the functions of the President under the Federal Advisory Committee Act for those committees will be carried out by the head of the department or agency listed for each committee. It replaces sections 1 and 2 of Executive Order 13446.

13512.s: This order extends the work of the Coordinator of Federal Support for the Recovery and Rebuilding of the Gulf Coast Region. It changes the end date from September 30, 2009, to April 1, 2010. It affects federal support for recovery and rebuilding in the Gulf Coast region.

13513.s: This order tells Federal employees not to text while driving a Government-owned, Government-leased, or Government-rented vehicle, or while driving a private vehicle on official Government business. It also bars text messaging while using Government-supplied electronic equipment while driving. Federal agencies must take steps to carry out the order, and agencies are encouraged to ask Federal contractors, subcontractors, and grant recipients to adopt similar bans.

13514.s: This order directs Federal agencies to increase energy efficiency, reduce greenhouse gas emissions, conserve water, cut waste and pollution, and use sustainable products and buildings. It also requires agencies to set reduction targets, keep inventories and reports on emissions and water use, and make their results public. The Office of Management and Budget and the Council on Environmental Quality are given oversight duties to review plans, publish scorecards, and guide agency actions.

13515.s: This order creates a President’s Advisory Commission and a White House Initiative on Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders. They are meant to help improve the quality of life of Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders by increasing their access to and participation in federal programs where they may be underserved. The order also directs federal agencies to make plans to improve outreach, research, data collection, and coordination on issues affecting AAPI communities.

13516.s: This order changes rules for the President’s Intelligence Advisory Board and the Intelligence Oversight Board. It says the PIAB may have no more than 16 members who are not full-time federal employees, and the President will choose a chair or co-chairs to lead its meetings and work. It also requires intelligence activities with possible federal criminal law issues to be sent to the Attorney General, and it updates rules for sharing information and protecting classified national security information.

13517.s: This order changes earlier executive orders about Puerto Rico and federal contracting. It says the executive branch should improve the treatment of Puerto Rico in federal programs and promote job creation, education, health care, clean energy, and economic development on the islands. It also tells a task force to review matters related to Puerto Rico's status and report to the President, and it says contracting departments and agencies may treat certain labor-management costs as allowable costs.

13518.s: This order directs the Federal Government to increase recruitment of veterans and promote their employment in the executive branch. It creates a Council on Veterans Employment and tells participating agencies to make plans, set up veterans employment offices or officials, and give annual training on veterans’ employment. It also directs agencies to help veterans and transitioning service members with counseling, training, and information about federal jobs and veterans’ preference laws.

13519.s: This order creates an interagency Financial Fraud Enforcement Task Force led by the Department of Justice and chaired by the Attorney General. The task force is meant to help investigate and prosecute significant financial crimes, recover proceeds from those crimes, and coordinate law enforcement work across federal, state, tribal, territorial, and local agencies. It also may work with representatives of financial institutions, businesses, nonprofit groups, and governments on detecting and prosecuting financial fraud and related crimes.

13520.s: This order tells federal agencies to reduce improper payments in major federal programs. It requires the government to identify high-priority programs, set targets, publish information about improper payments, and create ways for the public to report suspected waste, fraud, and abuse. It also requires agencies to name officials responsible for meeting these targets and to report on recovery and prevention efforts. The order affects federal agencies, contractors, and state and local governments that work with federal funds.

13521.s: This order creates a Presidential Commission for the Study of Bioethical Issues within the Department of Health and Human Services. The Commission advises the President on bioethical issues tied to advances in biomedicine and related science and technology, and it may recommend legal, regulatory, or policy actions. It can study issues such as stem cells, genetic sequencing, human research participants, scientific integrity, and the intersection of science and human rights. The Commission does not review or approve specific projects and will end 2 years after the order unless the President extends it.

13522.s: This order creates a National Council on Federal Labor-Management Relations and tells executive branch departments and agencies to set up labor-management forums. These forums are meant to help managers, employees, and union representatives discuss workplace problems, improve government services, and work on solutions together. The order also calls for agency implementation plans and pilot projects on bargaining over certain subjects.

13523.s: This order closes executive branch departments and agencies of the Federal Government for the last half of the workday on Thursday, December 24, 2009. Their employees are excused from duty, except for offices and employees that must stay open for national security, defense, or other public need. It also treats that day as covered by certain rules on pay and leave for federal employees.

13524.s: This executive order changes a prior order about INTERPOL and the privileges, exemptions, and immunities it may receive. It removes language that had excluded certain parts of the International Organizations Immunities Act from that treatment. It affects the International Criminal Police Organization (INTERPOL).

13525.s: This order sets new rates of basic pay and salaries for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Health Administration, Senior Executive Service, executive branch offices, the Vice President, Congress, judges, and members of the uniformed services. It also provides locality-based comparability payments and new pay rates for administrative law judges. The new rates take effect on January 1, 2010, or at the start of the first applicable pay period after that date, and it supersedes Executive Order 13483.

13526.s: This order sets rules for classifying, safeguarding, and declassifying national security information, including information about defense against transnational terrorism. It says information may be classified only in limited categories, at one of three levels: Top Secret, Secret, or Confidential. It also requires declassification dates or events, gives rules for who can classify information, and says information cannot be classified to hide law violations, embarrassment, or to delay release of information that does not need national security protection.

13527.s: This order directs the federal government to plan for the quick delivery of medical countermeasures after a biological attack in the United States. It calls for coordination with State, local, territorial, and tribal governments to help limit illness and death, support critical infrastructure, and add to local delivery capacity. It also directs plans for U.S. Postal Service delivery, federal rapid response, and medical countermeasures for personnel doing mission-essential federal work.

13528.s: This order creates a Council of Governors made up of 10 state governors appointed by the President. The council is meant to meet with Defense and Homeland Security officials to share views, information, and advice on National Guard matters, homeland defense, civil support, and the coordination of state and federal military activities. The Secretary of Defense is to name an executive director, and members serve without pay but may get travel expenses.

13529.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of Defense, and the Secretary of Homeland Security for the Coast Guard when it is not operating in the Navy, to order certain members of the Selected Reserve and Individual Ready Reserve to active duty. It says this is needed to support active Armed Forces missions, including humanitarian assistance for relief efforts in Haiti after the January 12, 2010 earthquake. It also allows their active-duty service to be ended when needed.

13530.s: This order creates the President’s Advisory Council on Financial Capability in the Department of the Treasury. The council is meant to help the federal government promote financial capability among the American people and advise the President and the Secretary of the Treasury on how to do that. It will gather views from government officials, financial services providers, consumers, educators, and other experts, and it will report on the status of financial capability in the United States.

13531.s: This order creates a National Commission on Fiscal Responsibility and Reform within the Executive Office of the President. The commission is made up of 18 members chosen by the President and leaders of Congress, and it must propose recommendations to improve the federal fiscal situation, including balancing the budget, excluding interest payments on the debt, by 2015. It also must make recommendations to improve the long-run fiscal outlook and address entitlement spending and the gap between projected revenues and expenditures.

13532.s: This order creates a White House Initiative on Historically Black Colleges and Universities in the Department of Education. It tells federal agencies to make annual plans to help HBCUs take part in federal programs, improve information about HBCUs, and encourage public, private, and community involvement. It also creates a presidential board to advise on ways to strengthen HBCUs and improve their visibility, competitiveness, and financial security.

13533.s: This order sets a line of succession for who will act as Secretary of Defense if the Secretary dies, resigns, or cannot do the job. It lists Department of Defense officials in order, and only officials appointed by the President with Senate consent may serve under this order. It also revokes Executive Order 13394.

13534.s: This order creates the National Export Initiative to improve federal efforts that help U.S. businesses export goods, services, and agricultural products. It sets up an Export Promotion Cabinet to coordinate the effort and report to the President. It also directs steps to help small and medium-sized businesses, promote federal export assistance, support trade missions, increase export credit, reduce trade barriers, and promote services trade.

13535.s: This order directs federal agencies to enforce abortion funding limits in the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act. It says federal funds, tax credits, and cost-sharing reduction payments may not be used for abortion services except in cases of rape, incest, or when the woman's life would be endangered. It also directs HHS and OMB to create model segregation guidelines for health insurance exchanges and tells HHS to make sure community health centers follow the abortion funding limits.

13536.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of certain people tied to the conflict in Somalia. It applies to people named in the annex and to people found to threaten Somalia’s peace, security, or stability, obstruct humanitarian aid, or supply arms or related support. It also bars transactions meant to evade these rules and directs federal agencies to carry them out.

13537.s: This order creates an Interagency Group on Insular Areas within the Department of the Interior. The group is set up to advise the President and help review policies and policy actions affecting Guam, American Samoa, the United States Virgin Islands, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands. It also must gather information and advice from governors, other elected officials, and other people or groups, and report recommendations to the President each year.

13538.s: This order creates the President's Management Advisory Board within the General Services Administration. The board gives advice and recommendations to the President and the President's Management Council on federal government management and operations, with a focus on productivity, technology, and customer service. Its members serve without pay, and the board is set to end 2 years after the order unless the President extends it.

13539.s: This order creates the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology, or PCAST. The council advises the President on science, technology, and innovation policy, and it also gives advice to the National Science and Technology Council when asked. It includes federal and nonfederal members, and it is set to end after 2 years unless the President extends it.

13540.s: This order creates an Interagency Task Force on Veterans Small Business Development inside the Small Business Administration. The task force is meant to coordinate federal efforts on capital, business development opportunities, and federal contracting goals for small business concerns owned and controlled by veterans and service-disabled veterans. It also looks at ways to reduce paperwork, improve training and counseling, and increase the integrity of veteran-owned business certifications.

13541.s: This order creates a temporary office in the Department of State called the Iraq Strategic Partnership Office. It is set up to help federal agencies work with the Republic of Iraq on economic, diplomatic, cultural, and security matters, and to support a continuing diplomatic presence there. The office also handles remaining coordination, oversight, and reporting tasks for Iraq relief and reconstruction funds, and it may take on other related tasks assigned by the Secretary of State.

13542.s: This order sets the line of succession for the Secretary of Agriculture if both the Secretary and Deputy Secretary cannot serve. It lists several Agriculture Department officials who would act in that role, in the order named, if they are eligible under the Federal Vacancies Reform Act. It also revokes a previous executive order on succession within the department.

13543.s: This order creates the National Commission on the BP Deepwater Horizon Oil Spill and Offshore Drilling. The Commission must examine the causes of the Deepwater Horizon oil disaster and develop options to help prevent and reduce the impact of oil spills from offshore drilling. It must hold public hearings, gather information from affected groups and officials, and submit a final public report to the President within 6 months of its first meeting.

13544.s: This executive order creates the National Prevention, Health Promotion, and Public Health Council within the Department of Health and Human Services. The Council is meant to coordinate federal work on prevention, wellness, public health, and integrative health care, and to develop a national strategy for improving health and reducing preventable illness and disability. It also requires reports to the President and Congress and creates an advisory group of outside health professionals.

13545.s: This order changes the name of the President's Council to the President's Council on Fitness, Sports, and Nutrition. It directs the Secretary of Health and Human Services to develop and coordinate a national program to promote physical activity, fitness, sports participation, and good nutrition. The Council advises the President and the Secretary on ways to improve these programs and to reach all Americans, especially children, adolescents, and groups facing risks or gaps in access or knowledge.

13546.s: This order directs federal agencies to improve security for biological select agents and toxins used in research and labs. It calls for a risk-based tiered list, new security standards for the highest-risk agents, and coordinated federal oversight. It also creates an advisory panel and a process for sharing select agent program information when needed for public health, safety, law enforcement, or national security.

13547.s: This order sets a national policy for the ocean, U.S. coasts, and the Great Lakes. It directs executive agencies to use the recommendations of an Interagency Ocean Policy Task Force, work under a National Ocean Council, and help develop coastal and marine spatial plans. It applies to executive departments, agencies, and offices that affect these waters and requires annual reports and cooperation on planning and information sharing.

13548.s: This order directs federal agencies to increase the employment of people with disabilities in the federal workforce. It requires agencies to create plans for recruitment, hiring, retention, and return-to-work efforts, including goals for people with targeted disabilities. It also calls for training for hiring staff, regular progress reports, and efforts to improve accommodations, accessible technologies, and workspace access for federal workers with disabilities.

13549.s: This order sets up a program for safeguarding and controlling access to classified national security information shared with state, local, tribal, and private sector entities. It sets rules for who may get access, how facilities are inspected and monitored, and how classified information is stored and handled. It also assigns the Department of Homeland Security as the main executive agent for the program.

13550.s: This order creates a temporary office in the Department of State called the Pakistan and Afghanistan Support Office. It is meant to help strengthen the governments of Afghanistan and Pakistan, help them resist extremists, and keep an effective U.S. diplomatic presence in both countries. The office also takes over the functions, personnel, assets, liabilities, and records of the Afghanistan Support Office.

13551.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of certain persons connected to North Korea. It applies to people listed in the annex and to people the Treasury Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of State, determines have taken part in arms deals, luxury goods exports, money laundering, counterfeiting, bulk cash smuggling, narcotics trafficking, or related support. It also prohibits transactions that evade these restrictions and bars donations and transfers of funds, goods, or services to or from blocked persons.

13552.s: This order amends Parts II and IV of the Manual for Courts-Martial, United States. The changes take effect 30 days after the order is signed. It says the amendments do not make past acts punishable if they were not punishable before, and they do not stop certain military justice actions that already began before the effective date.

13553.s: This order blocks property and property interests in the United States, or controlled by U.S. persons, for certain people linked to serious human rights abuses by the Government of Iran. It also bars certain donations, funds, goods, and services to or from those blocked persons, and prohibits transactions that try to evade these rules. The Secretary of the Treasury and the Secretary of State are given authority to carry out these sanctions, including visa sanctions.

13554.s: This order creates the Gulf Coast Ecosystem Restoration Task Force. The task force is meant to coordinate federal, state, tribal, and local work on Gulf Coast ecosystem restoration, including planning, information sharing, and a regional restoration strategy. It also includes work related to the BP Deepwater Horizon Oil Spill, natural resource damage assessment, and communication with Gulf Coast communities and tribes.

13555.s: This order creates a White House Initiative on Educational Excellence for Hispanics within the Department of Education. It directs the Initiative to expand educational opportunities and improve education outcomes for Hispanics of all ages, including support for early learning, K-12 education, college access, adult education, and career and technical education. It also creates an advisory commission and an interagency working group to help carry out these goals and advise the President and the Secretary of Education.

13556.s: This order creates a government-wide program for managing unclassified information that needs safeguarding or limits on sharing, except information classified under other rules. It makes the National Archives and Records Administration the lead office to carry out the order and oversee agency compliance. Executive departments and agencies must review their current markings, propose CUI categories and markings, and make plans for implementing the new requirements.

13557.s: This order sets an order of succession for who will act as Attorney General if the Attorney General, Deputy Attorney General, Associate Attorney General, and certain other designated officers cannot serve. It lists the United States Attorneys for the Eastern District of Virginia, the District of Minnesota, and the District of Arizona in that order. It also says no one serving in one of those offices in an acting capacity may use this order to become Attorney General, and it revokes Executive Order 13481.

13558.s: This order creates an interagency Federal Export Enforcement Coordination Center in the Department of Homeland Security. The Center coordinates export enforcement among several federal departments and offices, shares intelligence and law enforcement information, and helps resolve conflicts in investigations of U.S. export control violations. It also serves as a contact point for export licensing agencies, helps with public outreach, and tracks criminal and administrative export control enforcement activities.

13559.s: This order directs federal agencies to follow rules for working with faith-based and other neighborhood organizations in social service programs. It says eligible organizations must be able to compete for federal financial assistance on equal footing, and that no organization may be discriminated against because of religion or religious belief. It also says organizations may not use direct federal financial assistance for explicitly religious activities, and beneficiaries who object to an organization’s religious character must be referred to an alternative provider.

13560.s: This order creates the White House Council for Community Solutions within the Corporation for National and Community Service. The council supports the nationwide "Call To Service" campaign by identifying effective community-developed solutions, finding areas for cross-sector collaboration, and making recommendations to the President. It also includes members from outside the Federal Government and ends 2 years after the order unless renewed.

13561.s: This order sets new basic pay rates and salary schedules for federal employees in several pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Health Administration, Senior Executive Service, and administrative law judges. It also sets pay for the Vice President, Congress, justices and judges, and members of the uniformed services. The order directs that locality-based comparability payments be paid under a set schedule, and it says the changes take effect on the dates listed in the order.

13562.s: This order creates the Internship Program and the Recent Graduates Program, along with the Presidential Management Fellows Program, as the Pathways Programs. It directs the Office of Personnel Management to issue rules for recruiting, training, mentoring, and converting some participants to Federal civil service jobs. It applies to students, recent graduates, veterans in some cases, and agencies that use these programs.

13563.s:
This order tells federal agencies to improve how they write and review regulations. It says rules should protect public health, safety, welfare, and the environment while also considering economic growth, innovation, competitiveness, and job creation.

It requires agencies to use public participation, seek comments online on proposed rules, and give public access to rulemaking dockets when feasible. It also tells agencies to review existing significant regulations and consider whether they should be changed, simplified, expanded, or repealed.

13564.s: This order creates the President’s Council on Jobs and Competitiveness inside the Department of the Treasury. The council is advisory only and is meant to give the President and some federal agencies advice on the economy, growth, innovation, competitiveness, and job creation. It also revokes Executive Order 13501 and says the council will end 2 years after this order unless the President extends it.

13565.s: This order creates two interagency advisory committees on intellectual property enforcement. They are to help develop and carry out joint strategic plans under the PRO IP Act and share information on counterfeiting and infringement. The committees include officials from several federal departments and agencies involved in intellectual property enforcement.

13566.s: This order blocks property and interests in property in the United States for certain people tied to Libya, including listed persons, senior Libyan officials, some family members, and people who helped them. It also blocks property of the Government of Libya, its agencies, controlled entities, and the Central Bank of Libya. It prohibits certain transactions, donations, and contributions involving blocked persons, and it directs U.S. agencies to carry it out.

13567.s: This order sets up a periodic review process for certain detainees held at Guantánamo Bay under the Authorization for Use of Military Force. It applies to detainees who were designated for continued law of war detention or referred for prosecution, except those with pending charges or a conviction. The reviews decide whether continued detention is needed to protect against a significant threat to the security of the United States. If a detainee does not meet that standard, officials must look for a suitable transfer location outside the United States.

13568.s: This order extends the privileges, exemptions, and immunities in the International Organizations Immunities Act to the Office of the High Representative in Bosnia and Herzegovina and to the International Civilian Office in Kosovo. It also applies those protections to the officers and employees of both offices. If either office is dissolved, those protections would continue for the office and its officers and employees.

13569.s: This order changes several earlier executive orders. It expands one medal rule to cover any member of the Armed Forces of the United States, makes wording changes in the National Economic Council and Domestic Policy Council orders, and updates a rule for historically black colleges and universities. It also reestablishes the President's Advisory Council on Faith-Based and Neighborhood Partnerships and revokes the order that created the White House Office of Health Reform.

13570.s: This order prohibits the importation into the United States of any goods, services, or technology from North Korea, unless allowed by statute or by licenses, regulations, orders, or directives issued under it. It also bars transactions by U.S. persons or within the United States that evade, avoid, or try to violate these limits, and it bans conspiracies to do so. Federal agencies are directed to take appropriate steps to carry out the order.

13571.s: This order directs federal agencies to make their service to the public more efficient, responsive, and customer-focused. Each agency must create a customer service plan that uses technology, collects customer feedback, sets service standards, and looks for ways to speed up service and lower costs. The order also asks agencies to publish these plans online, and it applies to people and entities that receive significant services from an agency.

13572.s: This order blocks property and interests in property in the United States, or under the control of a United States person, for certain people linked to human rights abuses in Syria. It also bars transfers, payments, exports, withdrawals, donations, and other support involving those blocked persons. The Treasury Secretary, with the Secretary of State, may add people to the blocking list or remove them if blocking is no longer needed.

13573.s: This order blocks property and property interests of certain senior officials of the Government of Syria and others linked to them. It bars those blocked persons from transferring, paying, exporting, withdrawing, or otherwise dealing in that property. It also prohibits donations, contributions, and the provision or receipt of funds, goods, or services involving blocked persons, and bars transactions that evade these restrictions.

13574.s: This order sets rules for carrying out certain sanctions under the Iran Sanctions Act against people the President or Secretary of State has already designated. It lets the Treasury Department block property, limit financial transactions, and restrict imports involving those sanctioned persons. It also bans attempts to evade the sanctions or conspire to violate them.

13575.s: This order creates the White House Rural Council to help coordinate federal programs for rural communities. The council is meant to make policy recommendations, improve federal engagement with rural stakeholders, and identify rural economic opportunities. It also covers federal efforts in areas that include agriculture, small business, health care, education, telecommunications, and tribal, State, and local governments.

13576.s: This order directs the federal government to cut waste, improve efficiency, and strengthen accountability in agency operations. It requires agencies to track performance, review programs for overlap and duplication, and report on cost savings and management reforms. It also creates a Government Accountability and Transparency Board to help improve the transparency of federal spending and detect fraud, waste, and abuse.

13577.s: This order creates the SelectUSA Initiative in the Department of Commerce to attract and keep business investment in the United States. It is meant to help create jobs, support economic growth, and promote American competitiveness. The initiative will coordinate federal outreach, give information to domestic and foreign firms, and help resolve issues tied to pending investments. It also sets up a federal working group and asks executive departments and agencies with business investment duties to cooperate.

13578.s: This order keeps a coordinated federal response for automotive communities and workers. It tells the Secretary of Labor to help coordinate policies and programs, advise the President on pending legislation, and gather input from groups and officials. It also revokes Executive Order 13509 of June 23, 2009.

13579.s: This order tells independent regulatory agencies to improve their regulation and review of existing rules. It says they should consider public participation, costs and benefits, and whether rules are outmoded, ineffective, insufficient, or too burdensome. It also asks each agency to publish a plan for periodic review of its significant regulations, when allowed by law.

13580.s: This order creates an interagency working group led by the Department of the Interior. The group is meant to coordinate federal agencies on onshore and offshore energy development and permitting in Alaska. It also coordinates environmental reviews, information sharing, planning, and contact with state, local, tribal, and Alaska Native organizations.

13581.s: This order blocks property and property interests of certain significant transnational criminal organizations and people tied to them. It bars transfers and other dealings with that property, and it also bans donations, fund transfers, goods, or services for their benefit. It applies to U.S. persons and transactions in the United States, and it directs federal agencies to help carry it out.

13582.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of the Government of Syria that are in the United States or under the control of a United States person. It also blocks property of certain people who help or act for blocked persons. The order prohibits new investment in Syria by United States persons, the export or supply of services to Syria, and imports of Syrian petroleum or petroleum products into the United States.

13583.s: This order directs federal departments and agencies to work together on diversity and inclusion in the federal workforce. It requires a government-wide strategic plan, agency-specific diversity and inclusion plans, and regular reporting on progress. It also tells agencies to look for ways to improve recruiting, hiring, promotion, retention, development, and training of a diverse workforce.

13584.s: This executive order directs the State Department’s Center for Strategic Counterterrorism Communications to coordinate government public communications aimed at audiences outside the United States. It is meant to counter al-Qa'ida, its affiliates and adherents, other terrorist organizations, and violent extremists overseas, and to help reduce radicalization. It also creates a temporary office in the State Department to support agencies in government-wide communications activities abroad.

13585.s: This order continues several federal advisory committees until September 30, 2013. It also says that, for those committees, the department or agency head named for each committee will carry out the President’s functions under the Federal Advisory Committee Act. The order supersedes parts of Executive Order 13511 and changes parts of Executive Order 13515, including the co-chairs and listed agency members for that initiative.

13586.s: This order creates an emergency board to investigate disputes between certain railroads and their employees represented by certain labor organizations. The board must report to the President within 30 days of its creation. From the board’s creation until 30 days after its report is submitted, the parties may not change the conditions at issue unless they agree to do so.

13587.s: This order directs structural reforms to improve the security of classified computer networks and the sharing and safeguarding of classified information. It sets up a steering committee, a classified information office, an executive agent, and an insider threat task force to set policies, standards, and oversight. It applies to agencies that operate or access classified computer networks and to users, including contractors, who use those networks.

13588.s: This order directs the FDA to take steps to help prevent and reduce drug shortages, especially for medicines that are life-supporting, life-sustaining, or prevent debilitating disease. It tells the FDA to require more advance notice when manufacturers may stop making drugs, and to speed up review of new suppliers, manufacturing sites, and manufacturing changes when that could help avoid shortages. It also tells the FDA to report to the Department of Justice if shortages lead to stockpiling or exorbitant prices.

13589.s: This executive order directs federal agencies to cut waste and spend taxpayer money more efficiently. It requires each agency to make a plan to reduce certain combined costs by at least 20 percent below Fiscal Year 2010 levels in Fiscal Year 2013. It also tells agencies to limit spending on travel, employee technology devices, printing, executive transportation, and promotional items.

13590.s: This executive order authorizes sanctions on people who knowingly provide goods, services, technology, or support to Iran that could help develop Iran’s petroleum resources or expand its petrochemical production. It also applies to successor entities, owners or controllers of such persons, and persons under common ownership or control who knowingly take part in those activities. The sanctions can include limits on exports, loans, foreign exchange transactions, property blocking, and restrictions on imports into the United States.

13591.s: This order keeps several federal advisory committees in place past their original end dates. It also extends one advisory group only until September 30, 2012, and changes the end date for the President's Advisory Council on Financial Capability to January 29, 2013 unless extended by the President. The departments or agencies listed for each committee will carry out the President’s duties under the Federal Advisory Committee Act for those committees.

13592.s: This order sets up a White House initiative to improve education for American Indian and Alaska Native students and to strengthen Tribal Colleges and Universities. It directs federal agencies to work on better school readiness, teacher support, dropout prevention, college access, and the preservation of Native languages, cultures, and histories. It also calls for a joint plan between the Education and Interior Departments and for agencies to report on their progress.

13593.s: This order changes Parts III and IV of the Manual for Courts-Martial, United States. The changes take effect 30 days after the date of the order. It says the amendments do not make past conduct punishable if it was not punishable before, and they do not invalidate certain military proceedings or actions already begun before the effective date.

13594.s: This order sets new pay rates for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Health Administration, Senior Executive Service, executive, legislative, and judicial salaries, uniformed services pay, and administrative law judges. It also provides locality-based comparability payments under the listed schedules. The Office of Personnel Management must take steps to carry out these payments and publish notice of them in the Federal Register.

13595.s: This order directs the executive branch to have a National Action Plan on Women, Peace, and Security. The plan is to guide U.S. work in conflict-affected areas on women’s participation, protection from violence, conflict prevention, and access to relief and recovery. It also requires certain agencies to make their own implementation plans and report on progress.

13596.s: This order changes the membership of the President's Export Council. It lists executive departments and offices, certain outside organizations, five senators, five House members, and up to 28 citizens appointed by the President. It also says the Department of Energy must provide funding and support for the President's Council of Advisors on Science and Technology, and that the Secretary of Energy will handle most functions under the Federal Advisory Committee Act for that council.

13597.s: This order directs agencies to improve visa and foreign visitor processing while keeping national security requirements in place. It calls for a plan to raise visa processing capacity in China and Brazil, speed up interviews for nonimmigrant visa applicants, expand the Visa Waiver Program, and grow expedited travel programs like Global Entry. It also creates a Task Force on Travel and Competitiveness to write a national travel and tourism strategy for promoting travel in the United States and increasing the country's share of worldwide travel.

13598.s: This order gives the Secretary of Defense the President’s role in certain military promotion and appointment actions. It covers reports about officers at brigadier general or rear admiral (lower half) and above, extending officer promotion eligibility periods, and appointments of members of the Marine Band and Marine Drum and Bugle Corps to grades no higher than captain. The Secretary of Defense may pass some of these functions to certain civilian officers in the Office of the Secretary of Defense, but not the Marine Band and Marine Drum and Bugle Corps appointment function.

13599.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of the Government of Iran, including the Central Bank of Iran, that are in the United States or under the control of a U.S. person. It also blocks property of Iranian financial institutions and of certain people owned or controlled by, or acting for, blocked persons. The order bars transfers, payments, exports, withdrawals, and other dealings with that property, and it restricts donations and other contributions of funds, goods, or services to or from those persons.

13600.s: This order establishes the President’s Global Development Council within USAID for administrative purposes. The council advises the President on U.S. global development policy and programs, supports public-private partnerships, and seeks public input on global development issues. Its members include certain federal officials and up to 12 people from outside the federal government appointed by the President.

13602.s: This executive order creates a White House Council on Strong Cities, Strong Communities within the Department of Housing and Urban Development. The Council is meant to help federal agencies work together to give cities, towns, and regions technical assistance and planning resources for their economic goals. It also makes the Council report on its work and hold outreach with local governments, businesses, nonprofits, labor groups, school districts, and other community organizations.

13603.s: This order sets national defense resource policies under the Defense Production Act and delegates related powers to several Cabinet officials. It directs agencies to identify defense needs, assess the domestic industrial and technological base, and be ready to help ensure enough resources, services, and critical technology for national defense. It also gives certain agencies authority over priorities and allocations, loan guarantees and loans, subsidy payments, and other steps to expand or protect domestic industrial capacity.

13604.s: This order sets up a process to speed up federal permitting and review of infrastructure projects. It creates a steering committee and asks agencies to make plans, set timelines, track progress, and use the Dashboard to share information. It covers projects in areas such as transportation, aviation, ports, water resources, renewable energy, electricity transmission, broadband, and pipelines. It also calls for coordination with state, local, and tribal governments and says the committee may not direct decisions on any particular permit or project.

13605.s: This order creates an interagency working group to coordinate federal efforts on the safe and responsible development of unconventional domestic natural gas resources and related infrastructure. The group includes officials from several federal departments and agencies. It is meant to help coordinate policy, share information, plan research and infrastructure work, and communicate with stakeholders. The order also says it should be carried out under existing law and available funding.

13606.s: This order blocks property and property interests of certain people tied to information and communications technology that helps the governments of Iran or Syria carry out computer or network disruption, monitoring, or tracking linked to serious human rights abuses. It also blocks people who sell or provide goods, services, or technology for that use, or who support those activities. It suspends entry into the United States for aliens who meet these criteria.

13607.s: This order directs the Departments of Defense, Veterans Affairs, and Education to create Principles of Excellence for schools that receive federal military and veterans education benefits. The principles require schools to give service members, veterans, spouses, and other family members clear information about costs, financial aid, student outcomes, and graduation plans, and to provide academic and financial advising. The order also calls for rules against deceptive recruiting, stronger complaint and enforcement systems, and better access to school performance information.

13608.s: This order lets the Secretary of the Treasury block certain transactions with foreign persons who violate or try to evade U.S. sanctions related to Iran or Syria. It also bans donations, funds, goods, or services to or from those persons in covered cases. The order suspends entry into the United States for foreign persons found to meet those criteria.

13609.s: This order directs federal agencies to coordinate on international regulatory cooperation. It tells agencies to track significant regulations that have international impacts and to consider foreign regulatory approaches when allowed by law. It also sets up a working group to discuss these issues, develop guidelines, and consult with other agencies, businesses, nonprofit groups, and the public.

13610.s: This order directs federal agencies to review existing regulations to see whether they should be modified, streamlined, expanded, or repealed. It asks agencies to invite public suggestions and to make retrospective analyses public online when practical. Agencies are told to give priority to changes that reduce paperwork, cut regulatory burdens, and simplify rules for small businesses while protecting public health, welfare, safety, and the environment.

13611.s: This order blocks property and interests in property in the United States of people the Treasury Secretary, working with the Secretary of State, determines have threatened Yemen’s peace, security, or stability. It also covers political or military leaders of such entities, people who helped them, and people owned or controlled by them. The order prohibits transactions, donations, and contributions of funds, goods, or services for the benefit of those listed, and directs U.S. agencies to help carry it out.

13612.s: This order sets the line of succession for the Secretary of Agriculture if both the Secretary and Deputy Secretary cannot serve. It lists Agriculture officials who would act in that role, in a set order, and says some acting officials or people not otherwise eligible cannot serve under this order. It also revokes a prior order on the same subject.

13613.s: This order sets the line of succession for the Secretary of Commerce. If the Secretary dies, resigns, or cannot serve, certain Commerce officials listed in the order would act as Secretary in the order named. It also says no one serving in one of those jobs in an acting capacity may use this order to become acting Secretary, and it revokes two earlier Commerce succession orders.

13614.s: This order sets a line of succession for the Environmental Protection Agency if the Administrator and Deputy Administrator die, resign, or are otherwise unable to serve. It lists EPA officials who would act as Administrator in a set order, subject to federal vacancy law and certain exceptions. It also revokes two earlier executive orders on EPA succession.

13615.s: This order sets a line of succession for the Office of Management and Budget if both the Director and Deputy Director cannot serve. It lists which OMB officers would act as Director in order, if they are eligible under law. It also says people already serving in those jobs in an acting role cannot use this order to become acting Director, and it revokes a 2005 order on the same subject.

13616.s: This order directs federal agencies to coordinate rules and procedures for broadband deployment on federal lands, buildings, rights of way, federally assisted highways, and tribal lands. It creates a working group, asks agencies to make permit and access information easier to find, and calls for standard contract, application, and permit templates. It also directs transportation and interior officials to review "dig once" practices and other steps tied to broadband facilities along highways and rights of way.

13617.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of the Government of the Russian Federation that are directly related to the HEU Agreements. It covers property in the United States, property that later comes into the United States, and property in the possession or control of United States persons. The order also tells U.S. agencies to take steps to carry out the HEU Agreements and to support the transfer of payments due under them.

13618.s: This order sets up a government process for national security and emergency communications. It creates an executive committee and a joint program office to coordinate planning, testing, restoration, and policy for these communications. It also assigns duties to several agencies, including Defense, Homeland Security, Commerce, General Services, the intelligence community, and the Federal Communications Commission.

13619.s: This order blocks property and interests in property in the United States of people the Treasury Secretary determines have threatened the peace, security, or stability of Burma. It covers people linked to efforts that undermine Burma’s political reform or peace process, human rights abuses, arms from North Korea to Burma, or support for those acts. It also suspends entry into the United States for aliens who meet those criteria.

13620.s: This order blocks the U.S. property of certain people tied to threats to Somalia’s peace, security, or stability, and to people who obstruct humanitarian aid, supply arms, or commit violence against civilians. It also covers people linked to recruiting children for armed conflict, misappropriating Somali public assets, or supporting those activities. The order prohibits importing charcoal from Somalia into the United States and bans transactions that evade these restrictions.

13621.s: This order creates a White House initiative in the Department of Education to improve educational outcomes for African Americans of all ages. It also creates a federal working group and an advisory commission to help guide the effort. The order says the initiative will promote better access to early learning, school support, college and career preparation, adult education, and partnerships with public and private groups.

13622.s: This order authorizes new sanctions on foreign financial institutions that knowingly handle significant transactions with Iran’s oil, petroleum, or petrochemical trade. It also allows sanctions on people who knowingly buy Iranian petroleum or petrochemical products or who materially assist the National Iranian Oil Company, Naftiran Intertrade Company, the Central Bank of Iran, or the Government of Iran’s purchase of U.S. bank notes or precious metals. The order exempts some food, medicine, and medical device transactions, and it does not apply to a certain natural gas development and pipeline project started before the order took effect.

13623.s: This order directs the executive branch to use a multi-year strategy to prevent and respond to gender-based violence globally. It creates an interagency working group to coordinate the strategy across U.S. departments and agencies and to review progress over time.
