It also calls for better data and research, more coordination with other governments and organizations, and stronger programming on gender-based violence.

13624.s: This order tells federal agencies to help increase investment in industrial energy efficiency and combined heat and power at industrial facilities. It calls for working with states, manufacturers, utilities, and other stakeholders, giving technical help, sharing public information, and using existing federal authorities and programs. It also sets a national goal of deploying 40 gigawatts of new, cost-effective industrial CHP in the United States by the end of 2020.

13625.s: This order directs several federal agencies to expand suicide prevention and improve mental health and substance abuse treatment for veterans, service members, and their families. It tells the Department of Veterans Affairs to expand the Veterans Crisis Line, add mental health staff, and work more with community providers when there are vacancies or long wait times. It also creates a task force and research plan to improve care, prevention, diagnosis, and treatment for conditions like PTSD and traumatic brain injury.

13626.s: This order changes how the federal government handles Gulf Coast ecosystem restoration after the Deepwater Horizon Oil Spill. It ends the Gulf Coast Ecosystem Restoration Task Force after the Gulf Restoration Council begins work, and the council is to develop a comprehensive restoration plan and report on progress. The order also designates the EPA Administrator and the Secretary of Agriculture as additional trustees for natural resource damage assessment and restoration tied to the spill.

13627.s: This order directs the government to strengthen rules against trafficking in persons in federal contracts and subcontracts. It bars contractors and subcontractors from using misleading recruitment, charging recruitment fees, taking workers’ identity documents, and certain failures to pay return transportation costs in some overseas work. It also requires compliance plans, worker training, reporting steps, and government review and enforcement when trafficking-related problems are found.

13628.s: This order sets out sanctions that can be imposed on people and entities linked to Iran. It blocks property, limits financial and trade transactions, and can bar imports, loans, credits, and government contracts in certain cases. It also targets people who help transfer goods or services used for serious human rights abuses in Iran, or who take part in censorship or other limits on freedom of expression or assembly in Iran.

13629.s: This order creates a White House Homeland Security Partnership Council and a Steering Committee. They are meant to build local partnerships between the Federal Government and private groups, nonprofits, foundations, community groups, and state, local, tribal, and territorial governments and law enforcement. The Council will advise on homeland security priorities, share best practices, and hold an annual meeting to exchange findings and progress.

13630.s: This order creates an Interagency Task Force on Commercial Advocacy to help U.S. businesses compete for foreign contracts and sell goods and services overseas. The task force is led by the Secretary of Commerce and includes senior officials from several federal departments and agencies. It will review commercial advocacy cases, coordinate agency efforts, share information about foreign procurement opportunities, and report progress every 180 days.

13631.s: This order reestablishes the Advisory Group on Prevention, Health Promotion, and Integrative and Public Health. It reappoints the same members who were serving on September 30, 2012. The advisory group is set to end on September 30, 2013 unless the President extends it.

13632.s: This order creates the Hurricane Sandy Rebuilding Task Force to help coordinate rebuilding after Hurricane Sandy. The Task Force is to work with FEMA and other federal, state, local, and tribal officials on long-term rebuilding, housing, critical infrastructure, the economy, and community resilience in the affected region. It must prepare a rebuilding strategy and then end 60 days after that strategy is completed.

13633.s: This order closes all executive branch departments and agencies of the federal government on Monday, December 24, 2012, and excuses their employees from duty that day. Agency heads may keep some offices open and require some employees to work for national security, defense, or other public need. It also treats that day as covered by federal pay and leave rules for government employees.

13634.s: This order reestablishes the President's Advisory Commission on Educational Excellence for Hispanics. It reappoints the same members who were serving on October 19, 2012. The commission is set to end on September 30, 2013, unless the President extends it.

13635.s: This order sets new rates of basic pay and salary for several federal pay systems. It covers civilian federal employees under the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Health Administration, Senior Executive Service, executive, legislative, and judicial salaries, uniformed services pay, locality-based comparability payments, and administrative law judges. It also says Schedule 8 takes effect January 1, 2013, and the other schedules take effect at the start of the first applicable pay period after the date named in the continuing appropriations law.

13636.s: This order directs the federal government to improve cybersecurity for critical infrastructure. It calls for more sharing of cyber threat information, a cybersecurity framework, and a voluntary program to help owners and operators of critical infrastructure use that framework. It also tells agencies to protect privacy and civil liberties and to identify critical infrastructure at greatest risk from cyber incidents.

13637.s: This order shifts many export control duties under the Arms Export Control Act to the Secretary of State and the Secretary of Defense, and it requires them to consult with each other and other agencies. It says the Secretary of State will supervise and direct sales and exports under the Act and decide whether sales to a country will happen. It also revokes an earlier executive order. The order adds procedures for notifying Congress about certain firearms exports and exports of Major Defense Equipment.

13638.s: This order changes how certain limits of liability are adjusted under the Oil Pollution Act. It gives those duties to the Secretary of the department in which the Coast Guard is operating, the Administrator, the Secretary of Transportation, and the Secretary of the Interior for different kinds of vessels and onshore and offshore facilities. It also requires reports to Congress on whether those liability limits should be adjusted.

13639.s: This order creates the Presidential Commission on Election Administration. The commission is meant to identify best practices and make recommendations to improve the efficient administration of federal elections and the experience of voters facing obstacles, including military members, overseas voters, voters with disabilities, and voters with limited English proficiency. It will hold public meetings, work with federal, state, and local officials and others, and then submit a final report to the President.

13640.s: This order extends the President's Advisory Council on Faith-Based and Neighborhood Partnerships. The council will end 2 years after the date of the order unless the President extends it again. It also says the order does not change the authority of executive departments or the Office of Management and Budget, and it must be carried out under existing law and available funding.

13641.s: This order sets pay rates and salary schedules for several federal jobs. It covers statutory pay systems, senior executives, certain executive, legislative, and judicial salaries, uniformed service members, locality-based comparability payments, and administrative law judges. It also says the Office of Personnel Management must take needed steps to carry out the locality payments.

13642.s: The order directs agencies to make new and modernized government information open and machine readable by default, when legally allowed. It also requires them to protect privacy, confidentiality, and national security, and not release information that would break the law or policy. The Office of Management and Budget must issue an Open Data Policy, and agencies must carry it out and report on their progress.

13643.s: This order amends Parts III and IV of the Manual for Courts-Martial, United States. The changes take effect on the date of the order. It says the amendments do not make earlier acts punishable if they were not punishable before, and they do not invalidate military justice actions already begun.

13644.s: This order changes the rules for the Presidential Commission on Election Administration. It says the commission may have no more than ten members appointed by the President. The members must include people with knowledge or experience in State or local election administration, business customer service, or other experience the President finds useful.

13645.s: This order authorizes sanctions on foreign financial institutions that conduct certain large transactions involving Iranian rials or keep significant rial accounts outside Iran. It also targets people and financial institutions that support listed Iranian persons, or that help with significant transactions involving Iran’s automotive sector. The order says agencies may block property, limit banking access, deny export approvals, and restrict visas for certain people connected to sanctioned persons.

13646.s: This order creates the President's Advisory Council on Financial Capability for Young Americans inside the Department of the Treasury. The council is meant to help promote financial capability among young Americans in schools, families, communities, and the workplace. It advises the President and the Secretary of the Treasury, gathers information from government and non-government experts, and reports on progress and next steps.

13647.s: This order creates the White House Council on Native American Affairs. The Council is meant to improve coordination of federal programs and resources for federally recognized tribes. It also directs federal agencies to work together on policy, consultation, and outreach with tribal governments and Native American communities.

13648.s: This order directs federal agencies to take action to combat wildlife trafficking and to help foreign nations do the same. It also creates a Presidential Task Force on Wildlife Trafficking to develop and carry out a national strategy. The strategy must address anti-poaching efforts, law enforcement coordination, legal enforcement, and ways to reduce demand for illegally traded wildlife. It also creates an Advisory Council to give the task force advice and support.

13649.s: This order creates the HIV Care Continuum Initiative to improve HIV prevention and care in the United States. It directs federal agencies to coordinate efforts, expand HIV testing and service delivery, and focus resources on evidence-based steps along the HIV care continuum. It also creates a working group that will review agency efforts, consult with stakeholders, and report recommendations to the President.

13650.s: This order sets up a federal working group to improve chemical facility safety and security. It directs the group to work on coordination with state, local, and tribal partners, sharing information, and creating common procedures for inspections, incident response, and enforcement. It also calls for reviews of rules and standards for ammonium nitrate, the Risk Management Program, the Process Safety Management Standard, and chemicals on the CFATS list. The order also brings together stakeholders to identify best practices for reducing risks from the production and storage of harmful chemicals.

13651.s: This order prohibits importing jadeite or rubies mined or extracted from Burma, and jewelry that contains them. It also bars transactions that evade or try to evade these prohibitions. Some reimports are allowed if the items were previously exported from the United States and were not changed while abroad.

13652.s: This order continues a list of federal advisory committees until September 30, 2015. It says the head of the listed department or agency will carry out the President’s functions for those committees under the Federal Advisory Committee Act. It also changes several other executive orders, including rules for the National Infrastructure Advisory Council and a few other advisory groups.

13653.s: This order directs federal agencies to prepare for the impacts of climate change and improve climate preparedness and resilience. It tells agencies to look for barriers to climate-resilient investment, review land and water policies, and provide climate data and decision tools. It also requires agencies to update adaptation plans that address climate risks to their operations, missions, suppliers, facilities, and programs. The order creates an interagency Council on Climate Preparedness and Resilience to help coordinate this work.

13654.s: This order establishes an emergency board to investigate disputes between the Long Island Rail Road Company and certain employees represented by labor organizations. The board is made up of three members appointed by the President and must report on the disputes within 30 days. For 120 days after the board is created, the parties may not change the conditions out of which the disputes arose unless they agree to do so.

13655.s: This order sets new pay rates and salary ranges for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Health Administration, Senior Executive Service, and the Executive Schedule. It also sets pay for the Vice President, Congress, justices and judges, members of the uniformed services, cadets and midshipmen, locality-based comparability payments, and administrative law judges. The new rates take effect on the dates listed in the order, and it supersedes Executive Order 13641.

13656.s: This order creates a temporary office in the Department of State called the Afghanistan and Pakistan Strategic Partnership Office. The office is meant to help U.S. agencies work with the governments of Afghanistan and Pakistan, support security and stabilization, and move toward a normal diplomatic presence in both countries. It also tells the office to help with the drawdown of State Department civilian field operations in Afghanistan and to oversee certain State Department assistance funds.

13657.s: This order changes the name of the National Security Staff to the National Security Council staff. It also says that any references to the National Security Staff or Homeland Security Council Staff in executive orders or presidential directives should be understood to mean the staff of the National Security Council. The order says it does not change the authority of executive departments or agencies, or the functions of the Director of the Office of Management and Budget.

13658.s: This order sets a minimum hourly wage for certain workers on new federal contracts and subcontracting work. It requires covered contractors and subcontractors to pay at least $10.10 an hour starting January 1, 2015, and sets a lower cash wage for tipped employees, with rules to make sure total pay reaches the required minimum. It also says the wage can rise each year after that based on a Labor Department determination.

13659.s: This order directs federal agencies to improve the process for importing and exporting cargo by using electronic systems and shared data. It creates the Border Interagency Executive Council to coordinate agencies that handle border-related reviews and to improve supply chain processes. It also calls for review of regulations, reports on standard data use, and steps toward electronic payment of duties, taxes, fees, and charges at importation.

13660.s: This order blocks property and property interests in the United States for certain people found responsible for actions that undermine democratic processes or institutions in Ukraine, threaten Ukraine’s peace and stability, or involve misappropriation of state assets. It also blocks property for people who claimed government authority in parts of Ukraine without Ukraine’s approval, and for people who helped or acted for them. The order suspends entry into the United States for people who meet these criteria and prohibits certain donations, funds, goods, and services involving them.

13661.s: This order blocks property and interests in property in the United States of certain Russian government officials, arms sector persons, and people who support them. It also suspends entry into the United States for people who meet those criteria. Donations, transactions, and transfers of funds, goods, or services for the benefit of blocked persons are also prohibited.

13662.s: This order blocks property and interests in property in the United States for certain people the Treasury Secretary identifies as tied to the situation in Ukraine. It covers people who work in certain Russian economy sectors, help blocked persons, or are owned or controlled by them. It also suspends their entry into the United States and bars donations and other transactions involving their blocked property.

13663.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate disputes between the Long Island Rail Road Company and certain employees represented by labor organizations. The board must review the disputes, receive final offers for settlement, and report its choice of the most reasonable offer to the President. Until 60 days after the board sends its report, the parties may not change the conditions that led to the disputes unless they agree to do so.

13664.s: This order blocks property and interests in property in the United States, or under the control of U.S. persons, of certain people linked to actions that threaten peace, security, or stability in South Sudan. It also covers people tied to human rights abuses, child recruitment, attacks on peacekeepers, and blocking humanitarian aid or peace talks. It bars donations, transactions meant to evade the order, and entry into the United States for people who meet the listed criteria.

13665.s: This order says federal contractors may not fire or otherwise discriminate against an employee or job applicant for asking about, discussing, or disclosing compensation. It also limits a contractor employee with access to others’ pay information from sharing that information in some cases. The Secretary of Labor must propose regulations to carry out the order.

13666.s: This order changes the rules for the Defense Meritorious Service Medal. It adds members of the armed forces of a friendly foreign nation to the people who may receive it, along with members of the U.S. Armed Forces.

13667.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of certain people tied to the conflict in the Central African Republic. It applies to people listed in the order and others found to have taken part in actions that threaten peace and security, attack civilians, use child soldiers, block humanitarian aid, attack peacekeepers, or support armed groups through illicit natural resource trade. It also bars certain donations, suspends U.S. entry for covered aliens, and forbids transactions meant to evade these rules.

13668.s: This order ends certain restrictions on legal action against the Development Fund for Iraq and some Iraqi property and interests in property. It applies to Iraqi petroleum, petroleum products, and property connected to the Central Bank of Iraq. It does not end the national emergency declared in Executive Order 13303, and it does not change other immunities Iraq has under other law.

13669.s: This order amends Part II, the Discussion for Part II, and the Analysis for Part II of the Manual for Courts-Martial, United States. The changes take effect on the date of the order. It also says the amendments do not make earlier acts punishable if they were not punishable before, and they do not cancel military punishment or other proceedings already begun.

13670.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate disputes between SEPTA and certain employees represented by labor organizations. The board must report to the President within 30 days of its creation. For 120 days after the board is created, the parties may not change the conditions that led to the disputes unless they agree to do so.

13671.s: This order blocks property and property interests in the United States for certain people tied to the conflict in the Democratic Republic of the Congo. It covers people linked to armed groups, violence against civilians, child soldiers, blocking humanitarian aid, attacks on peacekeepers, and illicit trade in natural resources. It also prohibits transactions that try to evade these restrictions and directs federal agencies to help carry them out.

13672.s: This order changes federal equal employment rules to include sexual orientation and gender identity. It also changes federal procurement rules to bar discrimination based on sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, or national origin. The Secretary of Labor must prepare regulations to carry out these changes, and they apply to federal contracts entered into after those rules take effect.

13673.s: This order directs federal agencies to consider a contractor’s labor law violations when deciding whether to award or keep certain federal contracts. It requires contractors and some subcontractors to disclose recent labor law violations and update that information during the contract. It also creates Labor Compliance Advisors at agencies to help review compliance issues and coordinate responses. The order covers contractors doing goods, services, and some construction work for the federal government.

13674.s: This executive order revises the federal list of quarantinable communicable diseases. It adds severe acute respiratory syndromes that can spread from person to person and may cause a pandemic or serious illness or death if not properly controlled. This section does not apply to influenza.

13675.s: This order tells the Secretary of Commerce to create the President's Advisory Council on Doing Business in Africa. The council is to advise the President on strengthening business ties between the United States and Africa, with a focus on trade, investment, jobs, infrastructure, agriculture, and partnerships. It is made up of up to 15 private sector members from different industries, and it will end after 2 years unless the President extends it.

13676.s: This order directs federal agencies to work together on antibiotic-resistant bacteria, which it says are a serious threat to public health and the economy. It sets up a Task Force and an advisory council to make a national action plan, track progress, and recommend new actions. It also calls for stronger antibiotic stewardship, better surveillance, new research and diagnostics, and international cooperation. These steps affect federal agencies, healthcare providers, the agricultural community, and the general public.

13677.s: This order directs federal agencies with international development programs and investments to factor climate-resilience into their strategies, planning, projects, investments, and funding decisions. It also tells agencies to share data and tools, work with other countries, and encourage multilateral entities to do the same. A Working Group is created to set guidelines, track progress, and report on how these climate-resilient development steps are being carried out.

13678.s: This order lets certain Criminal Investigators of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms, and Explosives be converted non-competitively to career appointments. They must have been appointed under Schedule B, completed 3 years of fully satisfactory service, and meet qualifications set by the Director of the Office of Personnel Management. The order also directs the Office of Personnel Management to write rules to carry it out.

13679.s: This order sets up a three-member emergency board to investigate a dispute between SEPTA and its locomotive engineers represented by the Brotherhood of Locomotive Engineers and Trainmen. The board must review final settlement offers from the parties and send a report to the President naming the most reasonable offer. Until 60 days after the report is submitted, the parties may not change the conditions involved in the dispute unless they agree to do so.

13680.s: This order authorizes the Secretary of Defense and the Secretary of Homeland Security to order certain Selected Reserve units and some Individual Ready Reserve members to active duty. It says this is to support Operation United Assistance, which provides help for civilian-led humanitarian assistance and consequence management related to the Ebola virus disease outbreak in West Africa.

13681.s: This order directs federal agencies to improve the security of consumer financial transactions in the public and private sectors. It requires agencies to move to payment terminals and cards with enhanced security features, including chip-and-PIN technology, and to replace some cards without those features. It also directs agencies to improve identity theft help for consumers and to require multiple factors of authentication and identity proofing for some online access to personal data.

13682.s: This order closes all executive branch departments and agencies of the federal government on Friday, December 26, 2014, and excuses their employees from duty. Agency heads may keep some offices open and require some employees to report for national security, defense, or other public need. It also says that day will be treated under federal pay and leave rules, and the Office of Personnel Management must carry out the order.

13683.s: This order amends three earlier executive orders. It changes rules for preparing and handling executive orders, proclamations, and trade proclamations, and it also updates the structure of the climate change council and a section of the fair pay and safe workplaces order. It affects the Office of Management and Budget, the United States Trade Representative, the Attorney General, and members of the climate change council.

13684.s: This order creates a President's Task Force on 21st Century Policing. The task force is advisory and is to identify best practices and make recommendations on how policing can reduce crime and build public trust. Its members are appointed by the President and include people with experience in law enforcement, civil rights, and civil liberties. The task force is to hold public meetings and submit a report to the President by March 2, 2015.

13685.s: This order blocks property and interests in property in the United States for certain people tied to operating in the Crimea region of Ukraine or supporting blocked persons. It also prohibits new investment in Crimea by United States persons, and it bars imports from Crimea and exports, sales, or supplies to Crimea. The order suspends entry into the United States of aliens who meet the listed criteria and prohibits donations and transactions that evade these restrictions.

13686.s: This order sets new rates of basic pay and salaries for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service Schedule, Veterans Health Administration schedules, Senior Executive Service, Executive Schedule, Vice President, Congress, judges, and administrative law judges. It also sets monthly pay for members of the uniformed services and cadets or midshipmen, and provides locality-based comparability payments. Most changes take effect on the first applicable pay period beginning on or after January 1, 2015, and Schedule 8 takes effect on January 1, 2015.

13687.s: This order adds sanctions against certain North Korean government and Workers' Party of Korea officials, agencies, controlled entities, and others who help them. It blocks their property and interests in property in the United States, and bars donations, transactions, and the transfer of funds, goods, or services to or from them. It also suspends entry into the United States, as immigrants or nonimmigrants, of aliens who meet the listed criteria.

13688.s: This order sets up a working group to improve how the federal government supports state, local, and tribal law enforcement agencies that get certain equipment from federal programs. The group must make recommendations on items like training, rules for controlled equipment, review and approval processes, and limits on misuse or transfer of that equipment. It also calls for reports to the President with recommendations and implementation plans.

13689.s: This order creates an Arctic Executive Steering Committee to guide federal agencies and improve coordination of U.S. Arctic policy. It also directs the committee to work with state, local, Alaska Native tribal governments and organizations, and other stakeholders on Arctic issues. The committee must help set priorities, reduce overlap in agency work, and identify gaps in carrying out Arctic policy.

13690.s: This order sets a Federal Flood Risk Management Standard for federally funded projects and directs agencies to use it when planning for flood risk. It changes how agencies identify floodplains and, in many cases, requires them to use higher flood elevations or other methods based on the best available science. It also requires public comment, public meetings, and other stakeholder input before the standard is fully put into use.

13691.s: This order encourages private companies, nonprofit organizations, and federal agencies to share information about cybersecurity risks and incidents. It directs the Department of Homeland Security to encourage the formation of Information Sharing and Analysis Organizations, or ISAOs, and have the National Cybersecurity and Communications Integration Center work with them. It also requires privacy, civil liberties, and business confidentiality protections in these information-sharing activities.

13692.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of certain people connected to the situation in Venezuela. It also suspends entry into the United States for certain people who meet listed criteria, unless the Secretary of State decides their entry is in the national interest. The order also bars certain donations and other transfers of funds, goods, or services to or from blocked persons.

13693.s: This order tells federal agencies to improve sustainability and cut greenhouse gas emissions across federal operations. It sets goals for agencies to reduce energy use, increase clean and renewable energy, save water, improve vehicle efficiency, and make federal buildings and purchases more efficient and environmentally responsible. It also requires agencies to plan for emission reduction targets and report on progress toward those goals.

13694.s: This order blocks property and interests in property of certain people tied to significant malicious cyber-enabled activities. It applies to people involved in cyber activities outside the United States that harm critical infrastructure, disrupt computers or networks, or steal funds, trade secrets, personal identifiers, or financial information. It also bars certain donations, limits transactions meant to evade the order, and suspends entry into the United States for people who meet its criteria.

13695.s: This order ends the national emergency that had been declared over the risk of nuclear proliferation from weapons-usable fissile material in the territory of the Russian Federation. It also revokes the earlier order that declared that emergency. The order says it does not affect actions, proceedings, rights, duties, or penalties that were already in place before it took effect.

13696.s: This order amends Parts II, III, and IV of the Manual for Courts-Martial, United States. It applies to the military justice rules under the Uniform Code of Military Justice. The amendments take effect on the date of the order, and they do not make punishable any act that was not punishable before that date.

13697.s: This order changes an earlier executive order about awards for special ability in career and technical education. It lets the Commission choose up to 20 more Presidential Scholars in a year, from the listed jurisdictions, based on scholarship and accomplishment in career and technical education fields.

13698.s: This executive order sets up a government team to coordinate efforts to recover U.S. nationals taken hostage abroad. It creates a Hostage Recovery Fusion Cell within the FBI, a Hostage Response Group, and a Special Presidential Envoy for Hostage Affairs. These offices are to share information, recommend recovery options, support hostages and their families, and coordinate diplomatic efforts and public inquiries.

13699.s: This order creates an Advisory Board on Toxic Substances and Worker Health within the Department of Labor. The board is made up of up to 15 members and advises the Secretary of Labor on site exposure matrices, medical guidance for claims examiners, evidence rules for certain lung disease claims, and the work of Labor Department physicians and hygienists. The Secretary of Labor provides funding, staff, and administrative support, and the board is set to end 5 years after the law was enacted.

13700.s: This order creates a three-member emergency board to investigate and report on disputes between New Jersey Transit Rail and certain employees represented by labor organizations. The President appoints the board members, and the board must report back within 30 days. For 120 days after the board is created, the parties may not change the conditions that led to the disputes unless they agree to do so.

13701.s: This order gives most of the President’s authorities and functions under the Bipartisan Congressional Trade Priorities and Accountability Act of 2015 to the U.S. Trade Representative. It also gives some specific duties to the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Labor, and the Director of the Office of Management and Budget. These duties include consultative mechanisms, environmental reviews, employment impact reviews, labor rights reports, and plans for carrying out and enforcing agreements submitted to Congress.

13702.s: This order creates the National Strategic Computing Initiative, a government-wide effort on high-performance computing research, development, and deployment. It is meant to coordinate federal work with industry and academia and to strengthen scientific discovery and economic competitiveness. The order sets five goals, including building an exascale computing system, improving data and simulation computing, and creating a long-term path for future computing systems.

13703.s: This executive order directs federal agencies to carry out the updated National HIV/AIDS Strategy for the United States. It requires coordination across the federal government and asks agencies to work on HIV prevention, care, and reducing HIV-related disparities. It also sets reporting duties for the White House Office of National AIDS Policy, lead agencies, and other agencies that support HIV/AIDS programs.

13704.s: This order creates the Presidential Innovation Fellows Program in the executive branch. It lets the General Services Administration appoint people with experience in technology or innovative practices to work on projects in federal departments and agencies. The fellows serve in short-term appointments and work with senior officials on government projects.

13705.s: This order designates the International Renewable Energy Agency as a public international organization under U.S. law. It lets the agency enjoy certain privileges, exemptions, and immunities under the International Organizations Immunities Act. The order says it does not change the authority of federal agencies or create a new legal right or benefit against the United States.

13706.s: This order requires many new federal contracts and contract-like instruments to include paid sick leave for employees working on those contracts. Covered employees must earn at least 1 hour of paid sick leave for every 30 hours worked, up to at least 56 hours a year, and they can use it for illness, medical care, family care, or certain needs related to domestic violence, sexual assault, or stalking. It also says the leave can carry over, can be reinstated for some rehired workers, and cannot be tied to finding a replacement worker first. The order applies to certain service, construction, concession, and Federal property contracts, with some exceptions.

13707.s: This order directs federal agencies to use behavioral science insights when they design policies and programs. Agencies are encouraged to look for places to simplify processes, improve how information is presented, and make choices and default options work better for the public. It also sets up the Social and Behavioral Sciences Team to advise agencies and asks for yearly reports on how agencies carry out the order.

13708.s: This order continues or reestablishes a list of federal advisory committees until September 30, 2017. The committees cover subjects like the White House, science, labor, trade, health, education, veterans, and national security. It also assigns the President’s duties for these committees to the heads of the named departments or agencies and changes parts of one earlier executive order.

13709.s: This order changes the rules for the National Security Medal. It says the medal may be awarded to any person, including members of the Armed Forces, for distinguished achievement or outstanding contribution in national security. It also sets out how people may recommend candidates and how the award is processed and presented. It replaces the earlier regulations for the medal.

13710.s: This order ends the national emergency that had been declared over the actions and policies of former Liberian President Charles Taylor and other persons. It also revokes the earlier order that created that emergency. The order says pending actions, past acts, and rights or duties that already existed are not affected.

13711.s: This order establishes a three-member emergency board to investigate and report on disputes between New Jersey Transit Rail and certain employees represented by labor organizations. The parties must submit final offers for settlement, and the board must choose the most reasonable offer in a report to the President. From the time the request for the board was made until 60 days after the report is submitted, the parties may not change the conditions that led to the disputes unless they agree to do so.

13712.s: This executive order declares a national emergency over the situation in Burundi. It blocks property and interests in property of certain people tied to violence, human rights abuses, attacks on civilians, obstruction of aid, and related acts in or concerning Burundi. It also suspends entry into the United States of aliens who meet those criteria and bans certain donations, contributions, and transactions with blocked persons.

13713.s: This order closed executive branch departments and agencies of the Federal Government for the last half of the workday on Thursday, December 24, 2015. It also let department and agency heads keep certain offices or employees on duty if needed for national security, defense, or other public need. The order covered pay and leave rules for federal employees on that day.

13714.s: This order directs federal agencies to strengthen recruitment, hiring, development, and support for career members of the Senior Executive Service. It sets new steps for executive awards, pay setting, hiring reviews, talent planning, onboarding, and executive rotations. It also creates a subcommittee to advise the Office of Personnel Management, the President, and other officials on senior executive matters.

13715.s: This order sets new basic pay rates and salary schedules for several federal pay systems. It covers General Schedule employees, Foreign Service employees, Veterans Health Administration staff, senior executives, certain executive, legislative, and judicial offices, members of the uniformed services, and administrative law judges. It also sets locality-based comparability payments and tells the Office of Personnel Management to carry them out.

13716.s: This order revokes four earlier executive orders on Iran and changes another one by removing several sections. It also gives the Treasury and State Departments authority to carry out certain sanctions that are outside the U.S. commitment to lift nuclear-related sanctions under the JCPOA. The order blocks property of certain people, limits some financial and trade transactions, and suspends entry into the United States of some aliens who meet the listed criteria.

13717.s: This order directs federal agencies to use earthquake-resistant design and safety standards for new federal buildings, major alterations, leased space, and some federally financed or regulated buildings. It also requires agencies that own or lease existing federal buildings to adopt standards for managing earthquake risk, and it lets agencies require higher performance levels. The order applies to buildings in the United States and its territories and possessions, with some exemptions for law enforcement, national security, or public safety.

13718.s: This order creates a Commission on Enhancing National Cybersecurity within the Department of Commerce. The commission is to make recommendations to strengthen cybersecurity in the public and private sectors while protecting privacy, public safety, economic security, and national security. It will study issues such as identity management, the Internet of Things, cloud computing, research, workforce training, and cybersecurity for federal, state, and local governments. The commission is advisory and must submit a final report to the President.

13719.s: This order sets up the Federal Privacy Council as an interagency forum to improve government privacy practices. It directs agencies to work with the council and to designate a Senior Agency Official for Privacy. The council is to share best practices, help with privacy policies, and review hiring, training, and professional development needs for privacy work.

13721.s: This order creates the Global Engagement Center at the State Department to coordinate government communications aimed at foreign audiences abroad. Its job is to counter the messaging and reduce the influence of international terrorist organizations and other violent extremists abroad. It also revokes Executive Order 13584 and sets up a temporary office to support the Center with research, contracts, partnerships, and analysis.

13722.s: This order blocks property in the United States of the Government of North Korea and the Workers' Party of Korea. It also blocks property of certain people tied to North Korea, including those involved in listed industries, trade in certain goods, human rights abuses, worker exportation, cybersecurity, censorship, or support for blocked persons. It prohibits export of goods, services, or technology to North Korea, new investment there, and entry into the United States of people who meet the listed criteria.

13723.s: This order establishes the Inherent Resolve Campaign Medal. It says the medal may be awarded to members of the Armed Forces who served in Iraq, Syria, or nearby waters or airspace during the stated period, under rules set by the Secretary of Defense or the Secretary of Homeland Security for the Coast Guard. It also says some members may choose this medal instead of the Global War on Terrorism Expeditionary Medal for the same service, and it may be awarded after death.

13724.s: This order changes a prior executive order about the Peace Corps. It gives the Director of the Peace Corps the power to adopt, change, and use the official seal or emblem of the Peace Corps. It also deletes one section of the earlier order.

13725.s: This order directs federal agencies to use their powers to promote competition, give consumers and workers better information, and remove regulations that restrict competition without matching benefits. It tells agencies to look for actions that could address price fixing, anticompetitive behavior, exclusionary conduct, and other barriers that limit consumer or worker choice. Agencies must send reports with possible actions and later report on more steps they plan to take to promote greater competition.

13726.s: This order blocks property and interests in property in the United States of people the Treasury Secretary determines meet certain criteria tied to the situation in Libya. It also suspends entry into the United States, as immigrants or nonimmigrants, for those people. The order covers people involved in threats to Libya’s peace and security, attacks on Libyan facilities or foreign missions, abuses against civilians, and illegal exploitation of Libyan oil or other natural resources.

13727.s: This order sets up two councils to help with the Presidential transition. One council gives guidance on planning, sharing information, and emergency exercises, and the other coordinates transition work across agencies and helps prepare briefing materials. It applies to executive departments and agencies, the Executive Office of the President, and transition teams of eligible candidates.

13728.s: This order directs federal agencies to strengthen wildfire resilience for certain Federal buildings on Federal land in the wildland-urban interface. It requires new Federal buildings over 5,000 gross square feet in moderate or greater wildfire risk areas to comply with the 2015 IWUIC, and it requires certain alterations to existing buildings to meet that code as well. Agencies must complete wildfire risk assessments for covered existing buildings and report every 2 years on their progress.

13729.s: This order keeps the Atrocities Prevention Board in place and sets rules for how it works across the U.S. government. The Board is to monitor mass atrocity risks around the world, review threats, and recommend policies, programs, resources, and tools to prevent and respond to them. It also directs agencies like State, Defense, Homeland Security, Justice, and intelligence agencies to improve training, planning, intelligence sharing, civilian response capacity, and efforts to deny safe haven and remove perpetrators who are not citizens.

13730.s:
This order amends Parts II, III, and IV of the Manual for Courts-Martial, United States. The changes take effect on the date of the order.

It also says the amendments do not make punishable any act that was not punishable before the effective date. It says prior military punishment, restraint, investigations, charge referrals, trials, and other actions already begun may continue under the same effect.

13731.s: This order directs federal agencies to support innovation and entrepreneurship in the United States and around the world. It creates a program to select up to 25 people at a time to help aspiring entrepreneurs, and it sets up an advisory board to guide that work. It also has agencies work on the Global Entrepreneurship Summit and on expanding internet access, digital literacy, and related programs in developing nations.

13733.s: This order assigns several presidential functions under the Trade Facilitation and Trade Enforcement Act of 2015 to the Secretary of Commerce, the Secretary of State, the Administrator of the United States Agency for International Development, and the U.S. Trade Representative. It also requires the Secretary of the Treasury to consult with other officials on certain currency exchange rate and economic policy matters. The order applies to these agencies and officials and says it must be carried out under applicable law and available funding.

13734.s: This order changes the President's Advisory Council on Doing Business in Africa. It raises the council’s limit from not more than 15 private sector corporate members to not more than 26. The order says the change is to give the council broader private sector representation as it advises on commercial engagement between the United States and Africa.

13735.s: This order sets a line of succession for who will act as Secretary of the Treasury if both the Secretary and Deputy Secretary cannot serve. It lists Treasury officers in the order they may take over, and it says no one serving in an acting capacity may use this order to become Secretary. It also revokes a prior executive order and presidential memorandum on Treasury succession.

13736.s: This order sets the line of succession for who will act as Secretary of Veterans Affairs if both the Secretary and Deputy Secretary cannot serve. It lists department officials in the order they would take over and says acting officials in those jobs do not automatically become Secretary under this order. It also revokes earlier orders and memorandums on the same subject.

13737.s: This order sets the line of succession for the Environmental Protection Agency Administrator if the Administrator and Deputy Administrator have died, resigned, or are otherwise unable to serve. It lists EPA officials who may act as Administrator in a set order, as long as they meet the requirements of the Federal Vacancies Reform Act. It also revokes a previous order on EPA succession.

13738.s: This order changes parts of Executive Order 13673 on Fair Pay and Safe Workplaces. It moves certain disclosure and information steps to an entity named by a final rule under the Federal Acquisition Regulation. It applies to contract solicitations covered by that final rule.

13739.s: This order ends the national emergency declared for the situation in or in relation to Côte d'Ivoire and revokes the earlier order that declared it. It says the situation had changed because of progress in stabilizing Côte d'Ivoire, including the 2015 presidential election, progress on managing arms and related materiel, and efforts against illicit trafficking of natural resources. It also says the termination does not affect actions already taken, pending proceedings, or rights, duties, or penalties that existed before the order took effect.

13740.s: This order amends Parts I, II, and IV of the Manual for Courts-Martial, United States, as set out in an attached annex. The changes take effect on the date of the order. It does not make past acts punishable if they were not punishable before, and it does not invalidate certain military justice actions that started before the changes took effect.

13741.s: This order changes how the federal government handles background investigations for jobs, security clearances, and Federal credentials. It sets up the National Background Investigations Bureau as the main service provider for these investigations and gives it responsibilities for conducting them under set policies and standards. It also gives the Department of Defense responsibility for the information technology systems that support these background investigation processes.

13742.s: This order ends the national emergency declared over the actions and policies of the Government of Burma and revokes several earlier executive orders. It also waives sanctions described in the JADE Act. The order ends the suspension of entry as immigrants and nonimmigrants for individuals covered by the revoked orders.

13743.s: This order changes rules for the Combined Federal Campaign, which is a workplace giving program for Federal employees and members of the uniformed services. It lets eligible voluntary health and welfare organizations solicit contributions at places of work or duty and allow pledges of volunteer time. It also allows the Director of the Office of Personnel Management to consider letting annuitants give through deductions from their Federal annuities.

13744.s: This order directs federal agencies to prepare for space weather events like solar flares, solar energetic particles, and geomagnetic disturbances. It says the government should improve forecasting, warnings, protection, response, and recovery for critical infrastructure such as the electrical power grid, communications, aviation, satellites, and water systems. It also assigns roles to several agencies and calls for coordination with state, local, tribal, private, academic, and international partners.

13745.s: This order lets the Director of the Office of Personnel Management carry out the President’s power to direct OPM to set up an emergency leave transfer program. The Director must do this in consultation with the Director of the Office of Management and Budget and must notify the President if a program is established.

13746.s: This order sets up a White House working group to help carry out Power Africa. It directs U.S. agencies to coordinate efforts to expand access to electricity and increase electricity generation in Sub-Saharan Africa. It also tells agencies to help local and regional companies take part in power, renewable energy, and climate change projects in low-income countries in Africa.

13747.s: This order directs the United States to advance the Global Health Security Agenda, an effort to help partner countries prevent, detect, and respond to infectious disease threats. It creates an interagency council to guide policy, resolve disagreements, and review progress on the agenda. It also assigns roles to several agencies to coordinate with other governments, international organizations, donors, and nongovernmental groups on these efforts.

13748.s: This executive order creates a Council for Community Solutions to help coordinate federal work with communities. The council is meant to bring agencies together, share working solutions, and develop policy recommendations based on community-led visions. It also directs outreach to groups such as nonprofit organizations, businesses, labor groups, state, local, and tribal government agencies, school districts, youth, seniors, and faith-based organizations.

13749.s: This order lets an executive branch agency appoint certain Foreign Service employees into the competitive service if they have at least 48 months of continuous service under a Limited Non-Career Appointment and pass an exam set by the Office of Personnel Management. To qualify, they must have a satisfactory or better performance rating and use the eligibility within 1 year after that service ends, with some extensions allowed. People appointed under this order become career conditional employees, and the same disqualification rules that apply to competitive service hires also apply here.

13751.s: This order directs federal agencies to continue coordinated efforts to prevent, control, and remove invasive species. It says agencies should identify actions that may affect invasive species, use their programs to prevent their spread, monitor populations, and restore native species and ecosystems that have been impacted. It also keeps the National Invasive Species Council and tells it to coordinate federal work, with attention to public health, climate change, and new technology.

13752.s: The order designates the Department of Health and Human Services as the U.S. Central Authority for the Convention on the International Recovery of Child Support and Other Forms of Family Maintenance. It authorizes the Secretary of Health and Human Services to carry out the needed functions. It also allows the Central Authority to designate state IV-D child support agencies to perform specific functions for applications under the Convention.

13753.s: This order changes the line of succession for the Secretary of Homeland Security. It lists the officers who would act as Secretary if the Secretary dies, resigns, or cannot do the job, as long as they are eligible under the Federal Vacancies Reform Act. It also says a person already serving in one of those offices in an acting role cannot act as Secretary under this section, and it revokes a prior order on the same topic.

13754.s: This order sets a policy to strengthen resilience in the northern Bering Sea by conserving the ecosystem and coordinating federal actions in a new Northern Bering Sea Climate Resilience Area. It requires agencies to consider the rights, needs, and knowledge of Alaska Native tribes, and it creates a task force and a tribal advisory council for consultation and recommendations. It also withdraws certain Outer Continental Shelf areas from future oil or gas leasing and directs work on shipping, pollution, and oil spill preparedness.

13755.s: This order sets the line of succession for the Secretary of Labor if both the Secretary and Deputy Secretary are unable to serve. It lists the officials who would act as Secretary in a set order, if they are otherwise eligible under the law. It also says no one already serving in one of those jobs in an acting capacity can use that role to become Secretary under this order, and it revokes a 2001 order on the same subject.

13756.s: This order sets new rates of basic pay and salaries for several federal pay systems, including the General Schedule, Foreign Service, Veterans Health Administration, Senior Executive Service, executive branch offices, Congress, judges, and administrative law judges. It also sets pay rates for members of the uniformed services and cadets or midshipmen, and it provides for locality-based comparability payments. Most of the schedules take effect on the first applicable pay period beginning on or after January 1, 2017, and Schedule 8 takes effect on January 1, 2017.

13757.s: This order expands rules that block property and interests in property of certain people tied to significant malicious cyber-enabled activities. It covers people involved in cyber activities that harm critical infrastructure, disrupt computers, misappropriate funds or information, or interfere with election processes or institutions. It also covers people who help, support, control, or act for those blocked under the order.

13758.s: This order updates the rules for awarding the Purple Heart to members or former members of the armed forces, and in some cases to their families after death. It covers wounds from combat with enemy or foreign forces, certain terrorist attacks, peacekeeping operations, prisoner of war situations, and some friendly fire incidents. It also says the Purple Heart is not authorized for wounds or death caused by the member’s willful misconduct.

13759.s: This order designates the World Organisation for Animal Health as a public international organization under the International Organizations Immunities Act. It gives the organization the privileges, exemptions, and immunities provided by that law. The order says it does not affect other legal rights or benefits the organization may already have.

13760.s: This order changes which Department of Defense agencies and subdivisions are excluded from the Federal Labor-Management Relations Program. It says these units mainly do intelligence, counterintelligence, investigative, or national security work, and that chapter 71 of title 5 cannot be applied to them in a way that fits national security needs. It lists many Army, Navy, Air Force, and other defense offices, commands, and agencies covered by the exclusions.

13761.s: This order says Sudan has taken positive actions and sets steps to revoke certain Sudan-related sanctions if required conditions are met. It waives some sanctions rules for Sudan and gives certain duties under the law to the Secretary of the Treasury, the Secretary of State, and the Secretary of Homeland Security. It also keeps the national emergency in place and requires reports on whether Sudan has kept making the listed changes.

13762.s: This order sets a line of succession for who would act as Attorney General if the Attorney General, Deputy Attorney General, Associate Attorney General, and other designated officers cannot serve. It lists the United States Attorney for the District of Columbia, the Northern District of Illinois, and the Central District of California in that order. It also revokes Executive Order 13557 and says the President may depart from this order as allowed by law.

13763.s: This order sets a line of succession for the Environmental Protection Agency if the Administrator and Deputy Administrator die, resign, or cannot do the job. It lists EPA officials who would act as Administrator in a set order, if they are eligible under the law. It also revokes a previous order on EPA succession.

13764.s: This order changes rules for background checks, suitability, fitness, and federal credentials across the executive branch. It tells agencies to use consistent standards, share prior favorable determinations when possible, and align vetting for federal employees, contractor employees, and nonappropriated fund employees. It also says appointment or retention of covered individuals is subject to investigation and gives investigative agencies control over the reports and other materials they develop.

13765.s: This order directs federal agencies to seek prompt repeal of the Patient Protection and Affordable Care Act and, in the meantime, to minimize its economic and regulatory burdens. It tells agencies to use their authority to waive, defer, grant exemptions from, or delay parts of the law that create costs or burdens for states, individuals, families, healthcare providers, insurers, patients, and medical product makers. It also calls for greater flexibility for states and for a free and open market in healthcare services and health insurance.

13766.s: This order directs the executive branch to streamline and speed up environmental reviews and approvals for infrastructure projects, especially those marked as high priority. It names projects such as the electric grid, telecommunications systems, and repairs or upgrades to ports, airports, pipelines, bridges, and highways. The Chairman of the White House Council on Environmental Quality is to decide whether a project qualifies and set expedited deadlines with the relevant agency.

13767.s: This order directs federal agencies to secure the southern border, including planning and building a physical wall and using personnel to support it. It also calls for detention facilities, detention of people arrested for immigration law violations, and the return of some aliens to the territory they came from while removal proceedings are pending. The order seeks to hire 5,000 more Border Patrol agents and expand cooperation with state and local law enforcement on immigration enforcement. It also requires reporting on aid to Mexico and regular public reports on people apprehended near the southern border.

13768.s: This order directs federal agencies to use all lawful means to enforce immigration laws against removable aliens. It sets removal priorities for aliens with criminal offenses, fraud, public benefits abuse, or final removal orders, and it calls for more immigration officers and more cooperation with state and local law enforcement. It also tells agencies to limit federal grants to sanctuary jurisdictions, review prior immigration policies, and report on the status of incarcerated aliens.

13769.s: The order suspends entry into the United States for immigrants and nonimmigrants from certain countries for 90 days, with some visa types exempt. It also pauses the U.S. Refugee Admissions Program for 120 days, with special rules for Syrian refugees and for refugee admissions above 50,000 in fiscal year 2017. It directs agencies to tighten screening, review visa and refugee procedures, expand a biometric entry-exit tracking system, and require in-person visa interviews with limited exceptions.

13770.s: This order requires certain executive branch appointees to sign an ethics pledge when they take office. The pledge limits lobbying after leaving government, bans gifts from registered lobbyists and lobbying organizations, and bars some work on matters tied to former employers, former clients, or prior lobbying. It also says hiring decisions must be based on qualifications, competence, and experience. The order gives agency officials and the Office of Government Ethics duties to help enforce these rules and allows waivers in some cases.

13771.s: This order directs agencies to identify at least two existing regulations to be repealed when they propose a new regulation, unless the law says otherwise. It also sets a cap on the total incremental cost of new regulations for fiscal year 2017, unless required by law or approved in writing by the Director. It applies to executive departments and agencies and sets rules for reporting and reviewing regulations in later fiscal years.

13772.s: This order sets out principles for regulating the United States financial system. It directs the Secretary of the Treasury to consult with Financial Stability Oversight Council member agencies and report on how current laws, regulations, and other policies promote those principles. The report must also identify laws and policies that hinder federal regulation of the financial system in line with those principles.

13773.s: This order directs federal agencies to strengthen enforcement against transnational criminal organizations, including cartels and gangs. It focuses on crimes like human smuggling, drug trafficking, weapons trafficking, corruption, fraud, cybercrime, and theft of intellectual property. It also calls for more coordination and information sharing among federal agencies and with foreign partners, and it seeks the removal of foreign nationals who are members of these groups when allowed by law.

13774.s: This executive order sets a policy to enforce federal laws, develop strategies, and seek legislation to protect federal, state, tribal, and local law enforcement officers. It directs the Attorney General to review existing laws, coordinate prosecutions with other governments and agencies, and recommend changes, including possible new crimes and mandatory minimum sentences. It also calls for a review of Justice Department grant programs to see how they support and protect these officers.

13775.s: This order sets an order of succession for who will act as Attorney General if the Attorney General, Deputy Attorney General, Associate Attorney General, and certain other officers cannot serve. It lists the United States Attorneys for the Eastern District of Virginia, the Northern District of Illinois, and the Western District of Missouri in that order. It also revokes Executive Order 13762 and says the President may depart from this order as allowed by law.

13776.s: This order tells the Attorney General to set up a Task Force on Crime Reduction and Public Safety. The Task Force is to develop strategies to reduce crime, including illegal immigration, drug trafficking, and violent crime, and to look for gaps in existing laws and ways to improve crime data. It also directs the Department of Justice to lead federal efforts and work with state, tribal, and local officials to support law enforcement and restore public safety.

13777.s: This order directs federal agencies to lower regulatory burdens and improve regulatory reform. Each agency must name a Regulatory Reform Officer and set up a task force to review existing regulations and recommend repeal, replacement, or changes. The task forces must look for rules that are outdated, unnecessary, ineffective, or inconsistent with regulatory reform, and they may seek input from affected groups.

13778.s: This order directs the Environmental Protection Agency and the Army to review the 2015 Clean Water Rule on “Waters of the United States.” They are told to consider rescinding or revising the rule and other related orders, rules, regulations, guidelines, or policies as allowed by law. The order also says future rulemaking should consider a reading of “navigable waters” consistent with Justice Antonin Scalia’s opinion in Rapanos v. United States.

13779.s: This order creates a White House Initiative on Historically Black Colleges and Universities within the Executive Office of the President. The Initiative is meant to work with federal agencies and other partners to strengthen HBCUs, improve their access to federal programs, and support private-sector and public-private efforts. It also creates a President's Board of Advisors on HBCUs to advise the President on ways to strengthen these schools. The order revokes a 2010 executive order on HBCUs.

13780.s: This order revokes an earlier order and replaces it with new rules for screening people who want to enter the United States. It calls for a review of visa and refugee screening, and it imposes a temporary pause on entry for nationals of Iran, Libya, Somalia, Sudan, Syria, and Yemen, with categorical exceptions and case-by-case waivers. It also says Iraq should be treated differently, but visa and admission decisions for Iraqi nationals should get additional scrutiny. It affects foreign nationals seeking visas, refugee admissions, or entry into the United States.

13781.s: This executive order directs the Office of Management and Budget to propose a plan to reorganize the executive branch to improve efficiency, effectiveness, and accountability. It calls for possible elimination of unnecessary agencies, agency components, and programs, and for merging functions where appropriate. Agency heads must submit their own reorganization plans, and the public may suggest improvements for the plan.

13782.s: This order revokes Executive Order 13673, section 3 of Executive Order 13683, and Executive Order 13738. It directs federal departments and agencies to consider rescinding any orders, rules, regulations, guidance, guidelines, or policies that implement or enforce those revoked orders. It applies to federal departments and agencies.

13783.s: This order directs federal agencies to review rules and actions that may burden domestic energy production, especially oil, natural gas, coal, and nuclear energy. It says agencies should suspend, revise, or rescind certain regulations and guidance if appropriate and allowed by law. It also revokes several climate-related presidential actions, rescinds some reports and guidance, and directs review of rules tied to the Clean Power Plan, social cost estimates, federal coal leasing, and oil and gas development.

13784.s: This order establishes a presidential commission to study drug addiction and the opioid crisis. The commission is directed to review federal funding, treatment access, overdose reversal, prevention practices, education efforts, and federal programs. It must make recommendations to the President on how the federal government can improve its response, and it applies to the executive branch and the Office of National Drug Control Policy.

13785.s: This order directs the government to improve collection and enforcement of antidumping and countervailing duties and other trade and customs laws. It calls for a plan that could require certain importers to provide security through bonds or other legal measures if they pose a risk to U.S. revenue. It also tells officials to improve enforcement against trade and customs violations, share certain information with intellectual property rights holders, and prioritize prosecution of significant trade law offenses.

13786.s: This order directs the Secretary of Commerce and the U.S. Trade Representative to prepare a report on significant trade deficits within 90 days. The report must identify foreign trading partners with significant goods deficits in 2016 and assess the causes, trade barriers, effects on manufacturing and defense, employment and wage growth, and possible national security concerns. It also allows public meetings and comments from stakeholders such as manufacturers, workers, consumers, service providers, farmers, and ranchers.

13787.s: This order sets a line of succession for who will act as Attorney General if the Attorney General, Deputy Attorney General, Associate Attorney General, and certain other designated officers cannot serve. It names three U.S. Attorneys in order to take over that role, if they are eligible under the Federal Vacancies Reform Act. It also revokes Executive Order 13775.

13788.s: This order makes the executive branch policy to buy American goods and hire American workers. It tells agencies to use Buy American laws more, limit waivers when allowed by law, and review how those rules affect domestic jobs and manufacturing. It also directs officials to propose new rules and guidance to protect United States workers and to review the H-1B visa program.

13789.s: This order directs the Treasury Secretary to review significant tax regulations issued on or after January 1, 2016. The review is to find regulations that impose an undue financial burden on taxpayers, add undue complexity to the federal tax laws, or exceed the IRS’s statutory authority. It also directs the Secretary to recommend actions to delay, suspend, modify, or rescind the identified regulations, and to review the existing exemption for certain tax regulations from the review process.

13790.s: This order sets up an interagency task force on agriculture and rural prosperity. The task force is directed to look for changes in law, regulation, and policy to support farming, rural economic development, job growth, infrastructure, technology, education, food safety, energy security, and access to public lands. It also asks for input from state, local, tribal, and rural stakeholders and revokes a 2011 order that created the White House Rural Council.

13791.s: This order makes it the policy of the executive branch to protect state and local control over education, including curriculum, instruction, school administration, and personnel. It directs the Secretary of Education to review Department of Education regulations and guidance on certain education laws to see whether they improperly exercise federal direction or control over those areas. If any are found to be inconsistent with those limits, the Secretary is to rescind or revise them, and to the extent allowed by law, publish proposed regulations or change guidance documents within 300 days.

13792.s: This order directs the Secretary of the Interior to review certain national monument designations and expansions made under the Antiquities Act since January 1, 1996. The review covers large designations and ones made without enough public outreach or coordination with state, tribal, and local officials. The Secretary must look at how the designations fit the law, how they affect federal and nearby non-federal lands, and the concerns of affected governments. The Secretary must give an interim report and a final report to the President with possible presidential, legislative, or other actions allowed by law.

13793.s: This order directs the Department of Veterans Affairs to create an Office of Accountability and Whistleblower Protection and to appoint a special assistant to lead it. The office is meant to help discipline or remove VA managers or employees who violate the public trust, identify barriers to that authority, and help resolve complaints of wrongdoing. It also directs the VA to protect employees who lawfully report wrongdoing from retaliation.

13794.s: This order establishes the American Technology Council to help set the Federal Government’s vision, strategy, and direction for information technology and digital services. It includes the President and several other top officials, and it may also include other agency leaders at meetings. The council’s work does not extend to national security systems, and the order says it will end on January 20, 2021.

13795.s: This order directs federal officials to encourage offshore energy exploration and production, including on the Outer Continental Shelf, while saying the work should be safe and environmentally responsible. It tells the Secretary of the Interior to consider more oil and gas lease sales in several Outer Continental Shelf planning areas, streamline some permitting, and speed up review of certain offshore survey and authorization requests. It also orders reviews of several offshore rules and sanctuary decisions, revokes one earlier order, and modifies certain offshore leasing withdrawals while leaving existing lease rights in place.

13796.s: This order directs reviews of U.S. trade and investment agreements, as well as trade relations with some WTO countries. The reviews must look for violations, unfair treatment, and agreements that have failed to meet expected results. It also directs officials to take lawful action to address trade law violations, abuses, and unfair treatment.

13797.s:
This order creates the Office of Trade and Manufacturing Policy inside the White House Office. The office is led by a director selected by the President and staff as needed.

Its job is to advise the President on policies for American workers and domestic manufacturers, economic growth, the trade deficit, and the manufacturing and defense industrial bases. It also works with the Department of Commerce and helps improve domestic procurement and hiring policies, including those in Executive Order 13788.

13798.s: This order tells executive agencies to protect religious freedom and to respect religious and political speech as much as the law allows. It directs the Treasury Department not to take certain adverse tax actions against a person, house of worship, or religious organization because of speech about moral or political issues from a religious point of view, when similar speech has not been treated as election activity. It also tells the Treasury, Labor, and Health and Human Services departments to consider new rules for conscience-based objections to the preventive-care mandate, and tells the Attorney General to issue guidance on religious liberty protections.

13799.s: This order creates the Presidential Advisory Commission on Election Integrity. The Commission is led by the Vice President and has up to 15 additional members appointed by the President. It will study the registration and voting processes used in Federal elections and report on laws, rules, policies, and practices that affect confidence in those elections, as well as vulnerabilities that could lead to improper voter registrations and improper voting.

13800.s: This order directs federal agencies to manage cybersecurity risk using the National Institute of Standards and Technology framework and to report their risk management plans. It also tells agencies to prefer shared IT services, like email, cloud, and cybersecurity services, when allowed by law. The order directs federal departments to support cybersecurity efforts for critical infrastructure entities, review market transparency on cybersecurity practices, and assess risks such as botnets, power outages, and defense-related cyber risks. It also calls for reports on ways to deter adversaries and better protect the American people from cyber threats.

13801.s: This order directs the federal government to promote apprenticeships and other workforce development programs. It tells agencies to look at ways to expand apprenticeship programs, including industry-recognized programs, and to support apprenticeships in schools, colleges, and several worker groups.
